Repo-wide `grep -ran 'STALL|stallTimeout|watchdog'` over `packages/shared/src`, `packages/pi-agent-server/src` and `packages/server-core/src` returns no match, while the same sweep for `NESSY_*TIMEOUT*` returns `NESSY_ASK_USER_TIMEOUT_MS`, `NESSY_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT` and `NESSY_BROWSER_OPEN_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS` — so the grep is a working positive control, not a false absence.

pages.summary: Package/type renames for consumers moving off `@anthropic-ai/claude-code`. The one behavioural claim that binds us — the current `settingSources` default — is satisfied: `buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions` spells out `['user', 'project', 'local']`, the same three the CLI loads, with a comment saying so.

Binds the preset/append/excludeDynamicSections shape (matched, and correctly nested inside `systemPrompt`), output-style frontmatter including the `keep-coding-instructions` default (matched — a custom style defaults to `false`, i.e. it replaces the coding instructions), and CLAUDE.md discovery locations, where one documented path has no reader.

findings.claim: With the `project` setting source enabled, project instructions are discovered at either `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/CLAUDE.md` in the working directory.
findings.quote: The SDK reads CLAUDE.md when the matching setting source is enabled: `'project'` loads `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/CLAUDE.md` from the working directory, and `'user'` loads `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.
findings.ourState: The project instruction-file set is `PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES = ['AGENTS.md', 'CLAUDE.md', 'CLAUDE.local.md']`, joined against each ancestor/nested directory only. `.claude/` is read for `rules/` (`CLAUDE_RULES_DIR`) and for permission files, but never for `CLAUDE.md`: `grep -ran "CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, 'CLAUDE|'\.claude', 'CLAUDE"` over `packages` returns nothing, and the only two hits for the literal `.claude/CLAUDE.md` in `.ts` files are prose comments (capabilities/types.ts:199, base-agent.ts:972). A repo whose instructions live at `.claude/CLAUDE.md` contributes no project context.

pages.summary: Describes OpenTelemetry export of traces, metrics and log events. Nessy ships no OTLP exporter of any kind — it classifies a handful of OTEL_* variables for managed-settings approval but never emits a span, metric or log record.

findings.claim: Setting the telemetry enable switch plus at least one exporter makes the agent export spans, metrics and structured log events over OTLP to a collector.
findings.quote: Telemetry is off until you set `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1` and choose at least one exporter.
findings.ourState: There is no telemetry emitter. `grep -ran 'startSpan|tracer|trace_id|traceparent|TRACEPARENT'` over `packages` and `apps` returns zero non-test hits, and no `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY`, `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS`, `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` or `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` reader exists. The only OTEL surface is a five-entry allowlist/classification of exporter-transport variables used by the managed-settings approval dialog, which passes them through without anything consuming them. `packages/shared/src/agent/runtime-telemetry.ts` is an in-process per-turn record, not an OTLP export. (The Claude backend inherits the process env, so an operator who exports the variables would get telemetry from the SDK's own `claude` subprocess; the Pi and Codex runtimes, which are the shipped defaults, emit nothing.)

pages.summary: Product positioning, a capability index, branding rules and licence terms. Nothing here binds an implementation detail; the capability table's claim that skills, commands and memory load from `.claude/` and `~/.claude/` is covered by the project-contribution scan (`project-contribution-detect.ts`) and is checked in detail on the pages it links to.

The full API reference, which doubles as the wire contract for the TypeScript SDK we consume. Hook events, permission modes, effort levels, AgentDefinition fields, the Agent/Task and TaskStop/TaskOutput aliases, the Task tool family, Monitor's ws source and its 300000/3600000 timeouts, and the result subtypes including `error_max_budget_usd` all match. Three divergences: an unset thinking `display`, an unread result-level `is_error`/`api_error_status`, and sandbox network keys with no reader.

findings.claim: On Opus 4.7 and later the API no longer returns thinking text by default; a caller that wants ThinkingBlock content must ask for it with `display: "summarized"`.
findings.quote: The optional `display` field controls whether thinking text is returned `"summarized"` or `"omitted"`. On Claude Opus 4.7 and later, the API default is `"omitted"`, so set `"summarized"` to receive thinking content in [`ThinkingBlock`](#thinkingblock) outputs.
findings.ourState: `resolveClaudeThinkingOptions` builds `{ thinking: { type: 'adaptive' }, effort }` (and `{ type: 'adaptive' }` for the always-on Mythos path) and never sets `display`. The string `summarized` does not appear anywhere in the repo (`grep -ran` over `packages` and `apps`, zero hits). The model registry contains `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-sonnet-5` and `claude-fable-5`, i.e. exactly the class where the default flipped to `omitted`. Scoping the consequence honestly: the Claude event adapter has no `thinking` branch at all (`adaptAssistant` handles only `text` blocks), so today the effect is that thinking content is unobtainable on this backend rather than that a working display broke.

findings.claim: A result message with `subtype: "success"` can still be a failure: `is_error` is true and `api_error_status` carries the HTTP status when the agent loop finished but the final API call errored.
findings.quote: On `subtype="success"` it is `True` when the final model request failed, meaning the agent loop completed but the last API call returned an error.
findings.ourState: `adaptResult` resolves the terminal reason from `stop_reason` and `subtype` only: `msg.subtype === 'success' ? undefined : ...`. Neither `is_error` nor `api_error_status` is read anywhere on the Claude path (`grep -an 'is_error|api_error'` over `backend/claude/event-adapter.ts` matches only the assistant-message `error` field at :295 and the auth `msg.error` at :660; `claude-agent.ts` has no hit at all). A turn that ends `subtype: "success", is_error: true, api_error_status: 529` is emitted as `{ type: 'complete', usage }` with no `terminalReason` and no error event, i.e. indistinguishable from a clean success.

findings.claim: `SandboxNetworkConfig` carries Unix-socket, local-binding, Mach-lookup and proxy-port controls in addition to the domain allow/deny lists.
findings.quote: **Unix socket security**: The `allowUnixSockets` option can grant access to powerful system services.
findings.ourState: `SandboxNetworkSettingsV1` has exactly three keys — `deniedDomains`, `allowedDomains`, `allowManagedDomainsOnly` (`SANDBOX_NETWORK_KEYS` at :182). `allowUnixSockets`, `allowAllUnixSockets`, `allowLocalBinding`, `allowMachLookup`, `httpProxyPort` and `socksProxyPort` have zero occurrences in `packages` (grep -ran, `-a`; the one `allowLocalBinding` hit is a generated Codex protocol type, not our settings). Unlike `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` and `enableWeakerNestedSandbox`, which carry dated "documented, not implemented" decisions in the deviation register, these six have no recorded decision, and the scoped plan `2026-07-29-sandbox-network-enforcement.md` covers only the three domain keys. Reporting the identifier only: I did not test what an operator-set value would do at our seatbelt/bubblewrap boundary.

pages.summary: Install-and-first-agent tutorial for the SDK package, plus provider env vars for Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry that we do not ship. The one contract table in it — the six permission modes and their behaviour — was checked against `mode-manager.ts` and matches, including the two easy-to-miss clauses.

Container, gVisor, Firecracker and proxy hardening guidance for self-hosting. The two statements that bind a shipped surface both hold: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` routing exists, and `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` are honoured by the network interceptor and re-emitted into subprocess env (`network-runtime.ts`, `proxy-env.ts`), rather than being ignored the way a bare Node `fetch()` would.

The closest match on the whole set: `sessions/mirror/` implements the documented method shape, the three-attempt / no-retry-on-timeout envelope, the `mirror_error` event, uuid dedup and the summary fold, with `projectKey`→`workspaceId` recorded as a deliberate key divergence. Two documented behaviours have no production caller: the subagent `subpath` and the `load` timeout.

findings.claim: Subagent transcripts get their own mirror key under a `subagents/agent-<id>` subpath, and resume calls `listSubkeys` to materialise them.
findings.quote: Subagent transcripts are mirrored under `subpath: "subagents/agent-<id>"`. `listSubagents({ sessionStore })` requires the adapter to implement `listSubkeys`; `getSubagentMessages({ sessionStore })` uses it when available but falls back to the direct subpath when it is undefined. Resume also calls `listSubkeys` to restore subagent files; without it, only the main transcript is materialized.
findings.ourState: `subpath` and `listSubkeys` are declared in `mirror/types.ts` and exercised by `mirror/conformance.ts`, but no production code path ever sets or calls them: the host builds `{ workspaceId, sessionId }` with no `subpath` (`host.ts:146`), and `restoreSessionFromMirror` loads only that main key (`restore.ts:129`). Child/fork sessions carry their own full `SessionKey`, so their content is mirrored as separate top-level sessions rather than lost — the divergence is the key shape and the missing subkey enumeration, not (as far as I tested) dropped content.

findings.claim: The store's `load()` and `list_subkeys()` calls during resume materialisation are bounded by a per-call timeout, defaulting to 60 seconds.
findings.quote: Per-call timeout for `session_store.load()` and `list_subkeys()` during resume materialization, in milliseconds
findings.ourState: Only `append` is timed out — `appendWithEnvelope` races the call against `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000`. The load path has no timeout at all: `restoreSessionFromMirror` does a bare `await store.load(...)`, and `restoreMissingMirroredSessions` calls it in a serial loop over every session directory during the pre-listing boot sweep. A mirror root on a stalled network mount therefore hangs session listing at startup indefinitely instead of failing after a bounded wait. (The quoted sentence is the `load_timeout_ms` row on agent-sdk/python.md; session-storage.md documents the same `load` call but does not restate the bound.)

pages.summary: Binds continue/resume/forkSession/persistSession, the session-ID capture points, and the on-disk transcript location. We use resume + forkSession + resumeSessionAt correctly and keep our own session store; the one divergence is that we redirect CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR per Workspace without accounting for the transcript store that lives under it.

findings.claim: The SDK's resumable transcripts live under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so relocating that variable relocates the resume corpus.
findings.quote: Sessions are stored under `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl`, or under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl` if you set the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable, where `<encoded-cwd>` is the absolute working directory with every non-alphanumeric character replaced by `-` (so `/Users/me/proj` becomes `-Users-me-proj`).
findings.ourState: buildClaudeSubprocessEnv sets env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to <workspaceRoot>/claude-config whenever NESSY_WORKSPACE_ID is present, with no migration of any pre-existing projects/ transcripts and no per-workspace fallback lookup. The function's own doc-comment enumerates the hazards as 'TWO HAZARDS :356 NAMES, BOTH CHECKED AND CLEAR' — credentials and settings — even though the env-vars sentence it quotes says 'All settings, session history, and plugins are stored under this path'. Session history is the third hazard and is not addressed.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:255 (`if (workspaceConfigDir) env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR = workspaceConfigDir;`), hazard list at packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:196; no migration — `grep -ran "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR" --include="*.ts" packages apps` returns only options.ts and plugins/data-paths.ts

pages.summary: Binds the init-message slash_commands list, which commands are dispatchable through the SDK, and the .claude/commands file format. We read none of slash_commands, hardcode a one-entry dispatch allowlist, and advertise .claude/commands to the user with no loader behind it.

findings.claim: The set of dispatchable slash commands is discovered from the system/init message's slash_commands array.
findings.quote: Only commands that work without an interactive terminal are dispatchable through the SDK; the `system/init` message lists the ones available in your session.
findings.ourState: The init branch of the Claude event adapter captures only `msg.tools`; `slash_commands` has no reader anywhere in the repo (`grep -ra "slash_commands" packages apps` → 0 hits). The session therefore cannot tell the user, or itself, which commands the running CLI actually offers.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:625 (init branch reads `msg.tools` only); absence confirmed with `grep -ra "slash_commands" packages apps` (0 hits)

findings.claim: /clear is an SDK-dispatchable command that resets conversation context, alongside /compact.
findings.quote: The `/clear` command resets the conversation to an empty context, so subsequent prompts start with no prior conversation history.
findings.ourState: ClaudeAgent's dispatch allowlist is `const SDK_SLASH_COMMANDS = ['compact'] as const;`. Every other slash command — /clear, /context, /usage — falls through to buildTextPrompt and is sent as an ordinary context-wrapped prompt rather than dispatched as a command.

findings.claim: Project and personal custom commands are markdown files under .claude/commands/ and ~/.claude/commands/.
findings.quote: * **Project commands**: `.claude/commands/` - Available only in the current project (legacy; prefer `.claude/skills/`)
findings.ourState: `.claude/commands` is surfaced to the user as a consentable project contribution, but nothing loads it: native-sources.ts scans only skills/, agents/ and rules/ directories, and the only `kind: 'command'` producer in the repo is the plugin projection path. A user who grants the contribution gets no commands. (Skills provide the same `/name` invocation, so this may be a deliberate consolidation — but the detector advertises a surface with no reader.)
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/capabilities/project-contribution-detect.ts:218 (detector) vs packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:904-1017 (scans skills/agents/rules only); no commandRecords loader — `grep -ran "commandRecords|loadCommands" packages` → 0 hits

pages.summary: Binds includePartialMessages, the stream_event envelope, and the content_block_delta / text_delta / input_json_delta event vocabulary. We always set includePartialMessages: true and decode text_delta and content_block_start(tool_use) with the documented field names; tool-input deltas are read from the complete AssistantMessage instead of accumulated from input_json_delta, which the page presents as an option rather than a requirement.

Binds the two input modes and their limitations (no image attachments in single-message mode; query() throws after an error result). We route binary attachments through a single-message AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage>, i.e. streaming input mode, exactly as the page requires, and wrap the consumption loop in try/catch.

Binds outputFormat: { type: 'json_schema', schema }, draft-07 validation, and the success/error_max_structured_output_retries result contract. We pass outputFormat in the documented shape and map the retry-exhaustion subtype, but the documented third outcome — success with no structured_output — is emitted indistinguishably from a schema-less turn.

findings.claim: A schema-bearing run that ends success but produces no structured_output must be surfaced as a failure, not as a clean completion.
findings.quote: A result can also end with subtype `success` but no `structured_output` value, for example when the run completes without the agent producing a structured output. Treat that case as a failure as well.
findings.ourState: The Claude result adapter spreads `{}` when the subtype is success and `structured_output` is undefined, which is byte-identical to the schema-less turn's complete event. Downstream consumers of `structuredOutputSubtype` cannot distinguish 'no schema rode this turn' from 'a schema rode it and the agent produced nothing'.

findings.claim: The schema passed in outputFormat must be JSON Schema draft-07; a newer declared version is rejected.
findings.quote: The SDK validates schemas with JSON Schema draft-07, so schemas that declare a newer version are rejected.
findings.ourState: buildClaudeStructuredOutputOptions forwards `options.outputSchema` verbatim into `{ type: 'json_schema', schema }` with no $schema check or normalization. `grep -ran "draft-07|draft-7|\$schema" packages/shared/src/agent` returns nothing. A caller-supplied 2020-12 schema fails at the SDK boundary rather than at ours, and on the pinned SDK 0.3.183 (< v2.1.205) it is silently ignored rather than reported.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:316-320 (buildClaudeStructuredOutputOptions) and :1248 (call site); SDK pin at packages/shared/package.json `"@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk": "0.3.183"`

pages.summary: Binds the AgentDefinition field set, the Agent tool's background default, and the subagent nesting-depth default. Our definition parser covers all but two fields, but two documented defaults have moved away from ours: nesting depth is now 3 (we cap at 1, with no env override), and an Agent call that omits run_in_background is now background at every depth (we background only depth-1 spawns).

findings.claim: Subagents may nest three layers below the main conversation by default, and the limit is settable via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH.
findings.quote: By default, subagents can spawn subagents of their own, up to three layers below the main conversation.
findings.ourState: DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH is 1 in the spawner and DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG.depth is 1 in the host manifest, deliberately kept in lockstep. A depth-2 spawn is refused with `Subagent depth limit exceeded (1)`. No CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH (or NESSY_ equivalent) reader exists — the only repo occurrences of that identifier are in audit prose under docs/. This was correct when the page documented a default of 1 (v2.1.217–218); v2.1.219 raised it to 3 and made it configurable.
findings.evidence: packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:110 (`export const DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1`) and :518-519 (refusal); packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:107 (`depth: 1`); absence via `grep -ra "SPAWN_DEPTH" --include="*.ts" .` → docs/ prose only

findings.claim: An Agent tool call that omits run_in_background runs as a background subagent, regardless of nesting depth.
findings.quote: An Agent tool call that omits the [`run_in_background`](/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript) input launches a background subagent, and Claude sets `run_in_background: false` when it needs the result before continuing.
findings.ourState: The spawner's background default is `args.background ?? (depth === 1)` — top-level spawns default to background, nested spawns default to foreground. A nested Agent call that omits the input therefore blocks where Claude would detach it.

findings.claim: AgentDefinition.effort accepts an integer as well as a named level.
findings.quote: | `effort`           | `'low' \| 'medium' \| 'high' \| 'xhigh' \| 'max' \| number` | No       | Reasoning effort level for this agent                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
findings.ourState: AgentDefinition.effort is typed `ThinkingLevel` and parsed by normalizeThinkingLevel, which returns undefined for anything outside the string set off|low|medium|high|xhigh|max. A numeric effort is silently dropped (the field is spread only when defined), not rejected and not honored.

findings.claim: AgentDefinition carries an initialPrompt field auto-submitted as the first user turn when the agent is the main-thread agent.
findings.quote: | `initialPrompt`   | `string`                                                    | No       | Auto-submitted as the first user turn when this agent runs as the main thread agent. Ignored when the agent is invoked as a subagent                                                                                                                             |
findings.ourState: Neither AgentDefinition nor the frontmatter key list carries initialPrompt; `grep -ran "initialPrompt" packages apps` matches only docs/ and an unrelated pi test message id. Already recorded as a costed deviation ('documented, not implemented — no main-session-agent surface exists') in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-subagent-frontmatter.md:150, so this is a known gap, not a new one.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:255-271 (frontmatter key list) and :59-121 (AgentDefinition); absence via `grep -ran "initialPrompt" --include="*.ts" packages apps`

pages.summary: Binds the TodoWrite → TaskCreate/TaskUpdate/TaskGet/TaskList migration, the four tools' input shapes, the pending/in_progress/completed/deleted status set, the tool_result { task: { id, subject } } shape, and the id/task_id→taskId and active_form→activeForm key repair. All of it is implemented, including the repair-before-execute rule and the legacy TodoWrite fallback in the renderer.

The full API reference — Options, Query methods, the SDKMessage union, HookEvent, and every built-in tool's input/output schema. Most shapes we consume match. Four divergences: one hook event we have no mapping for at all, terminal_reason never read off the result, two system-message subtypes silently dropped, and the deferred-tool-call round trip implemented only on the Pi backend.

findings.claim: DirectoryAdded is a hook event, fired when /add-dir or the register_repo_root control request adds a directory.
findings.quote: | "DirectoryAdded"
findings.ourState: DirectoryAdded appears nowhere in the repo (`grep -ra "DirectoryAdded" . --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" --include="*.json" --include="*.md"` → 0 hits). It is absent from CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT_MAP and from DEFERRED_EXTERNAL_HOOK_EVENT_REASONS, so a Claude plugin declaring a DirectoryAdded hook is imported with a generic `plugin.format.unknown_hook_event` warning instead of a routed deferral. The map's own doc-comment still says '28 of the 30 documented Claude hook events'; the page now lists 31.

findings.claim: The result message carries terminal_reason naming why the loop ended, across a 19-value vocabulary.
findings.quote: * `terminal_reason`: why the loop ended. One of `"completed"`, `"max_turns"`, `"tool_deferred"`, `"aborted_streaming"`, `"aborted_tools"`, `"hook_stopped"`, `"stop_hook_prevented"`, `"background_requested"`, `"blocking_limit"`, `"rapid_refill_breaker"`, `"prompt_too_long"`, `"image_error"`, `"model_error"`, `"api_error"`, `"malformed_tool_use_exhausted"`, `"budget_exhausted"`, `"structured_output_retry_exhausted"`, `"tool_deferred_unavailable"`, or `"turn_setup_failed"`.
findings.ourState: The Claude result adapter never reads msg.terminal_reason. It derives the reason from stop_reason==='refusal', then from subtype via a 4-entry table, with everything unrecognized collapsing to 'provider_error'. A run ending subtype:'error_during_execution' with terminal_reason:'prompt_too_long' (or hook_stopped, stop_hook_prevented, aborted_tools, blocking_limit, rapid_refill_breaker, image_error, model_error) is reported to the user as an undifferentiated provider error even though the SDK put the specific cause on the same message. The installed SDK 0.3.183 does declare the field (`terminal_reason?: TerminalReason`, 12 values).
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:581-585 and the 4-entry table at :50-57; field confirmed present in node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts

findings.claim: system-subtype messages informational and local_command_output carry hook feedback, status lines and local slash-command output for display.
findings.quote: Generic text banner emitted by the loop. Carries non-error status lines, hook feedback such as a `UserPromptSubmit` hook's block reason, and command output. Render `content` as plaintext at the given `level`.
findings.ourState: adaptSystem is an if/else chain over init, compact_boundary, status and task_notification, with no trailing branch: every other system subtype is dropped without a debug line. Neither 'informational' nor 'local_command_output' appears anywhere in the repo (0 hits each). Both are declared by the installed SDK 0.3.183. A UserPromptSubmit automation that blocks under the Claude backend therefore produces a silent turn — the block reason the SDK emitted is discarded.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:622-656; absence via `grep -ra "'informational'|'local_command_output'" packages apps` → 0 hits; both types declared in node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts

findings.claim: A PreToolUse hook may return permissionDecision 'defer', and the run then ends carrying deferred_tool_use so the host can resume the pending call.
findings.quote: When a `PreToolUse` hook returns `permissionDecision: "defer"`, the result has `stop_reason: "tool_deferred"` and `deferred_tool_use` carries the pending tool's `id`, `name`, and `input`.
findings.ourState: Implemented on the Pi backend only (pi-agent.ts:3868 handles decision==='defer' and emits deferredToolUse). On the CLAUDE backend the PreToolUse translation switch handles allow/modify/block/ask and never emits permissionDecision:'defer', and the result adapter never reads msg.deferred_tool_use — `grep -ran "deferred_tool_use|deferredToolUse" packages apps` returns no hit under agent/backend/claude/ or claude-agent.ts. The SDK 0.3.183 supports both halves (`HookPermissionDecision = 'allow' | 'deny' | 'ask' | 'defer'`, `deferred_tool_use?: SDKDeferredToolUse`).
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1428-1434 (allow/modify/block/ask only); packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:581-619 (no deferred_tool_use read); Pi counterpart at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:3866-3893

pages.summary: Documents the removed V2 session API (unstable_v2_createSession / unstable_v2_resumeSession / unstable_v2_prompt, SDKSession, SDKSessionOptions), removed in Agent SDK 0.3.142 and kept only for callers pinned to 0.2.x. We are on 0.3.183 and use query() with resume/forkSession; `grep -ra "unstable_v2" packages apps` returns 0 hits, so nothing on this page binds a surface we ship.

Binds canUseTool, the AskUserQuestion question/answer envelope and its limits, and the defer escape hatch for long-running approvals. The AskUserQuestion contract is implemented in full (1-4 questions, 2-4 options, 12-char header, answers keyed by question text, freeform response, free-text 'Other'). Two documented mechanisms have no producer: the defer decision on the Claude backend, and the option-preview opt-in.

findings.claim: An approval that may outlive the process should return the defer hook decision so the run can end and resume later from the persisted session.
findings.quote: If a user might take longer to respond than your process can reasonably stay running, return the [`defer` hook decision](/docs/en/hooks#defer-a-tool-call-for-later), which lets the process exit and resume later from the persisted session.
findings.ourState: The defer round trip exists on the Pi backend only. Under the Claude backend the PreToolUse translation emits allow/modify/block/ask and never permissionDecision:'defer', so an approval that outlives the host process has no documented exit — the tool call stays blocked until the query is cancelled.

findings.claim: Option previews exist only when the session opts in through toolConfig.askUserQuestion.previewFormat.
findings.quote: `toolConfig.askUserQuestion.previewFormat` adds a `preview` field to each option so your app can show a visual mockup alongside the label. Without this setting, Claude does not generate previews and the field is absent.
findings.ourState: AskUserQuestionOption declares `preview?: string` and the type comment says it is 'absent unless the session enables preview generation', but nothing in the repo ever enables it: `grep -ran "previewFormat" packages apps docs` returns 0 hits, and no toolConfig key is passed in the Options object built at claude-agent.ts:1191. The field has no producer on either backend.
findings.evidence: packages/core/src/types/message.ts:717 (declaration); packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1191-1266 (Options object, no toolConfig); absence via `grep -ran "previewFormat" packages apps docs` → 0 hits

pages.summary: A comparison index for subagents / agent view / agent teams / dynamic workflows. We ship subagents (`packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/`), forks via `/subtask`, and dynamic workflows; agent view and agent teams do not exist at all, so two of the four rows have no counterpart. Nothing on the page binds an implementation detail we get wrong that is not already covered by the sub-agents/workflows pages.

`claude agents`, the per-user supervisor, `--bg`/`/background`/`/fork`-to-background, `claude attach|logs|stop|respawn|rm|daemon`, `~/.claude/jobs/`, and the JSON listing have no counterpart in this fork — we are a desktop app plus a websocket CLI client, not a terminal agent view. The page does bind two surfaces we DO ship: the `Notification` hook types `agent_needs_input`/`agent_completed` — declared in `packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts` symbol `HOOK_NOTIFICATION_TYPES`, and NOT emitted: the same file's `HOOK_NOTIFICATION_TYPES_WITHOUT_EMITTER` gives the reason for both of them in one sentence, *«Gated upstream on the agent-view surface, which Nessy does not have.»* (the line anchor this clause used to carry is dead and is named in words rather than respelled — it pointed into the DirectoryAdded block; re-read 2026-09-12 for C3.70, and the reading corrects the clause as well as the anchor, because *present* was the wrong word) and `worktree.bgIsolation`, whose documented default we deliberately inverted. **РЕШЕНИЕ 2026-09-11 (владелец, QF6 = B; ledger F31):** фоновая shell-задача, которую пользователь запускает САМ вне сессии — строка, за которой можно наблюдать, к которой можно подключиться и прочитать вывод, без модели в контуре — отказана осознанно, и отказ записан здесь рядом с уже зафиксированным отсутствием `claude --exec` у хоста. Причина одна и она про безопасность, а не про паритет: такая задача НЕ ПРОХОДИТ через хостовый permission-гейт, через который идёт каждый вызов инструмента, — то есть это торг по безопасности, который называют, а не дыра в паритете, которую закрывают. Нативного механизма ни у кого нет: codex и claude SDK дают выполнение shell только как вызов инструмента ВНУТРИ сессии, а единственная машинерия строк процессов в дереве — супервизор Pi. Ячейки F31 читаются `n/a` на всех трёх рантаймах именно поэтому. **РЕШЕНИЕ 2026-09-12 (владелец, QF5 = B; ledger F27):** экран диспетчеризации многих сессий — «что делает каждая, какая ждёт ввода, какая завершилась или упала, с peek, attach, stop, pin, rename и reorder» — отказан осознанно, и отказ записан здесь же, рядом с уже зафиксированным отсутствием `claude agents`. Nessy Desktop не становится консолью диспетчеризации: расхождение со страницей `agent-view` называется, а не лечится как дыра в паритете. Нативного механизма нет ни у кого — у claude супервизор и `claude agents` живут в CLI-процессе, а не в SDK-поверхности, которую хост может поднять; у codex нет ничего; у Pi снимок рантайма Pi-only по построению. Нового экрана и панели на рантайм не будет, и это ровно то, что уже запрещает решение DR-1 по Pi-only инспектору («панель, отсутствующая на двух рантаймах из трёх, читается пользователем как „claude хуже“»). ЧТО ПРИ ЭТОМ ПРИЕХАЛО, чтобы отказ не читался как неизмеренный пробел: список сессий говорит, какая ждёт вас и чего именно она ждёт — P6.270 (`6a8fbb55f` + `c2f8463ff`), `apps/electron/src/renderer/atoms/sessions.ts` символ `sessionAttentionState`; и на заблокированную сессию можно ответить прямо из списка, ровно один раз — P6.589 (`1e63054ec` + `770098404` + `7dda6c1d9`). Обе части — про наблюдаемость уже идущей работы, а не про запуск новой из отдельного экрана. Ячейки F27 читаются `n/a` на всех трёх рантаймах именно поэтому.

findings.claim: A background session moves itself into an isolated git worktree before it edits files; worktree isolation is the default and `worktree.bgIsolation: "none"` is the opt-out.
findings.quote: Every background session, whether started from agent view, `/bg`, or `claude --bg`, starts in your working directory. Before editing files, Claude moves the session into an isolated [git worktree](/docs/en/worktrees) under `.claude/worktrees/`, so parallel sessions can read the same checkout but each writes to its own.
findings.ourState: `WORKTREE_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.bgIsolation` is `'none'`, i.e. the opt-out is our default. This is a RECORDED deliberate deviation, not an oversight: the module note says adopting `"worktree"` would refuse the first edit of every existing session and the release valve (`EnterWorktree`) is Pi-only, so a Claude- or Codex-backed session would meet an unliftable write block.

pages.summary: Agent teams (team lead, teammates, mailbox at `~/.claude/teams/{team}/inboxes/{agent}.json`, shared task list at `~/.claude/tasks/{team}/`, `teammateMode` setting, `--teammate-mode` flag, plan-approval protocol, `SendMessage` team messages) do not exist in this fork. Of the three hook events the page binds we emit `TaskCreated` and `TaskCompleted` (`packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:68-69`) and deliberately defer `TeammateIdle` behind a named diagnostic (`packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters.ts:101` → `plugin.deferred.event_teammate_idle_unsupported`), so an imported Claude plugin that declares it is refused loudly rather than silently dropped. No silent divergence found.

Our subagent system is deep and doc-cited throughout (`packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts`, `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/`), covering scopes, `tools`/`disallowedTools`, `permissionMode` clamping, `model`, `effort`, `maxTurns`, `skills`, `mcpServers` (name form), `color`, `isolation`, background-by-default, forks and the no-nested-fork rule. Six binding statements diverge: the nesting-depth default, both spawn limits, the `hooks` frontmatter field, the `:` ban on names, the `memory` field's runtime, and the output scan's marker line.

findings.claim: A subagent may nest up to three layers below the main conversation by default (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` default 3, raised from 1 in v2.1.219).
findings.quote: By default, a subagent can spawn subagents of its own, up to three layers below the main conversation.
findings.ourState: `DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1` in the spawner and `depth: 1` in `DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG`, kept in lockstep on purpose. Depth 1 is exactly Claude's "nesting off" value. The repo's own note (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md`, R30 row: "default 1 — already matched by P9's depth-1 fix, so this one is closed") is now stale against the page.
findings.evidence: packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:110 and packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:107; refusal path at spawner.ts:518-519 (`Subagent depth limit exceeded (1)`)

findings.claim: A session-wide cap of 200 spawned subagents exists, raisable via `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION`, and the Agent tool fails with `Subagent spawn limit reached` when it is hit.
findings.quote: By default, Claude can spawn at most 200 subagents per session.
findings.ourState: No per-session subagent counter or cap exists anywhere. `orchestrator.maxAgents` (default 1000) is scoped to ONE workflow run only — `packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:49` calls it "maximum `agent()` calls per workflow run" and it is wired solely into the workflow tool (`packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1497` `getMaxAgents`). A session can spawn subagents without bound.
findings.evidence: `grep -ran "MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION|Subagent spawn limit|sessionSpawn" packages apps/electron/src` → no output; packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1497

findings.claim: 20 concurrently running subagents is the default ceiling, configurable via `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`, with the error `Concurrent subagent limit reached`.
findings.quote: By default, when 20 subagents are running in a session, spawning another with the Agent tool fails with `Concurrent subagent limit reached`, and the error tells Claude not to retry.
findings.ourState: One shared semaphore, `DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY = 16`, further narrowed at runtime to `min(concurrency, cpuCores - 2)`. It is also the workflow ceiling, where 16 IS the documented number (`workflows.md`: "Up to 16 concurrent agents"), so the two documented limits are collapsed into one and the subagent side sits 4 below spec. There is no `Concurrent subagent limit reached` error — over-limit spawns queue on the semaphore instead of failing.

findings.claim: A subagent definition may carry a `hooks` frontmatter block whose hooks run only while that subagent is active, with frontmatter `Stop` converted to `SubagentStop` at runtime; the field is ignored for plugin subagents.
findings.quote: Define hooks directly in the subagent's markdown file. These hooks only run while that specific subagent is active and are cleaned up when it finishes.
findings.ourState: `hooks` is not in `UserAgentDefinition` (the frontmatter/JSON shape), not in `AgentDefinition`, and not in the runtime descriptor. A `hooks:` block in an imported Claude agent file is parsed as frontmatter and then silently dropped — no diagnostic, unlike the `TeammateIdle` deferral. `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop` from `settings.json` ARE supported (`packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-runtime.ts:171-172`); only the per-agent frontmatter channel is missing.

findings.claim: A subagent `name` containing `:` is refused at load, because `:` is reserved for plugin-scoped identifiers.
findings.quote: Names can't contain `:`, which is reserved for [plugin-scoped identifiers](/docs/en/plugins) such as `my-plugin:reviewer`.
findings.ourState: `normalizeName` only trims and lowercases; no character validation. Our plugin capability keys DO contain colons (`qualifiedKey` joins with `::`, `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:263`) and become an agent's `name`/`aliases` (`runtime-agent-definitions.ts:153-154`). `resolveAgentDefinition` matches on exact `name` BEFORE searching `aliases`, so a workspace or project markdown agent file may declare a colon-bearing name equal to a plugin's capability key and be selected ahead of the alias lookup. Only the built-in and `fork` names are reserved.

findings.claim: When `memory` is set, the subagent gets a real memory directory: prompt instructions to read/write it, up to the first 200 lines or 25KB of its `MEMORY.md` injected, and Read/Write/Edit force-enabled.
findings.quote: The subagent's system prompt includes instructions for reading and writing to the memory directory.
findings.ourState: `memory` is parsed, validated against `user|project|local`, and carried on the definition and the runtime descriptor — and consumed by nothing. No `agent-memory/<name>/` directory is created, no memory prompt block is composed for a child, and no tool is force-enabled. Our own code comment admits it: "Parsed, validated and carried; the per-agent memory DIRECTORY is not yet provisioned". A read-only agent definition with `memory: project` therefore cannot write the memory it is told it has.

findings.claim: The output scan prepends a marker line when a subagent report imitates a harness tag OR mentions permission settings such as `bypassPermissions` / `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, leaving the text itself unchanged.
findings.quote: **Marker line**: the scan prepends a line starting with `[harness: subagent output matched instruction-shaped pattern(s):` when the report imitates a tag like `<system-reminder>` or mentions permission settings such as `bypassPermissions` or `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.
findings.ourState: `scanSubagentOutput` defangs `<untrusted|system-reminder|nessy_agent_environment` tags and line-leading `Human:`/`Assistant:` by inserting a zero-width space, and strips C0/C1 control characters. It never prepends a marker line, and it has no permission-setting pattern at all — a child report containing `bypassPermissions` or `--dangerously-skip-permissions` reaches the parent with nothing flagged. Two secondary differences on the same sentence pair: we insert U+200B where the page specifies a backslash (invisible vs visible), and we DO remove control characters where the page says "The scan never removes or rewords anything".

pages.summary: Mostly CLI surface we do not ship (`--continue`, `--resume`, `--from-pr`, `-n`, `--fork-session`, the TUI picker, `/export`). We do ship session persistence, branching, `cleanupPeriodDays` retention and a persisted permission mode, and the one binding statement about what a resumed session restores diverges.

findings.claim: A resumed session restores its permission mode, EXCEPT `plan` and `bypassPermissions`, which are never restored.
findings.quote: Permission mode: the mode the session was in. `plan` and `bypassPermissions` are never restored; [bypassing permissions](/docs/en/permission-modes#skip-all-checks-with-bypasspermissions-mode) must be enabled again at launch, with one of its launch flags or `permissions.defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` in [settings](/docs/en/settings#permission-settings).
findings.ourState: The persisted `permissionMode` is restored verbatim. `normalizePersistedSessionPermissionMode` runs only a provider-shape normalization (`normalizePiPermissionMode`) and has no exclusion list; `setPermissionMode(restoreModeKey, managed.permissionMode ?? 'default', { changedBy: 'restore' })` then installs it as-is. There is no bypass re-acceptance gate anywhere (`grep -rani "bypassAccepted|acceptedBypass|bypassDisclaimer"` → no hits), so a session last left in `bypassPermissions` comes back in `bypassPermissions` after an app restart, and a session left in `plan` comes back in `plan`.

pages.summary: Prompt recipes and pointers to other pages; the only implementation-binding lines are restatements of sessions.md / worktrees.md / permission-modes.md contracts (the `default → acceptEdits → plan` Shift+Tab cycle, `--worktree`, `--continue`, `@file`/`@server:resource` mentions). Our mode cycle is a deliberate superset (`explore`, `auto` added; `dontAsk`/`bypassPermissions` excluded from the cycle, `packages/shared/src/agent/mode-types.ts:63,81`) and `@server:uri` MCP resource mentions are implemented (`packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:2336`). No new divergence that is not already filed against its owning page.

Conceptual overview of the agentic loop, tool categories, sessions, context window and permission modes. One binding number on the page — the auto-memory load cap — is only half implemented in our reader.

findings.claim: Auto memory loads the first 200 lines OR 25KB of MEMORY.md, whichever limit is reached first.
findings.quote: The first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md, whichever comes first, load at the start of each session.
findings.ourState: `readMemoryFile` caps at `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200` lines and nothing else — there is no byte cap anywhere (`grep -ran "25 \* 1024|25600|25000" packages/shared/src` finds only unrelated token budgets). A MEMORY.md of 200 long lines loads unbounded bytes into every session's system prompt. sub-agents.md repeats the same rule for per-agent memory ("the first 200 lines or 25KB of `MEMORY.md` in the memory directory, whichever comes first"), so the gap applies on both paths.

pages.summary: Well covered: `CLAUDE_CODE_CERT_STORE` with the documented `bundled,system` default, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, the mTLS triple with re-read-on-settings-change, and managed/user-scope gating in `config/managed-env.ts`. Two proxy-parsing details diverge.

findings.claim: `NO_PROXY` accepts a space-separated list as well as a comma-separated one.
findings.quote: # Bypass proxy for specific requests - space-separated format
findings.ourState: Both NO_PROXY parsers split on commas only. `parseNoProxyRules` calls `splitCommaSeparated` (`str.split(',')`), and the Pi interceptor does `NO_PROXY.split(',')`. `NO_PROXY="localhost 192.168.1.1 example.com .example.com"` therefore yields one rule whose host is the whole string, which matches no hostname — every request goes through the proxy with no error or warning, the opposite of what the operator configured.

findings.claim: When several proxy variables are set, the lowercase `https_proxy` is consulted first.
findings.quote: Lowercase variants also work, and Claude Code uses the first one that's set in the order `https_proxy`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `http_proxy`, `HTTP_PROXY`.
findings.ourState: The Pi interceptor resolves `HTTPS_PROXY || https_proxy || HTTP_PROXY || http_proxy` — uppercase first. Only observable when both spellings are set to different values, in which case we pick the opposite one. (The host-side `network-runtime.ts` writes both spellings from one settings value, so it is unaffected.)

pages.summary: Dynamic workflows are implemented end to end — `meta` literal parsing, project/personal load paths with asymmetric symlink refusal, plugin `workflows/` import, `agent()`/`parallel()`/`pipeline()`/`phase()`, the 16-concurrent and 1000-agent caps, the advisory large-run warning at 25 agents / 1.5M tokens, and `disableWorkflows` as a tighter-wins hard switch. Three binding statements diverge: the workflow-agent permission floor, the `args` global's absent value, and the size-guideline default.

findings.claim: Subagents spawned by a workflow run in `acceptEdits` regardless of the session's permission mode; file edits are auto-approved and only the launch prompt follows the session mode.
findings.quote: The subagents the workflow spawns always run in `acceptEdits` mode and inherit your [tool allowlist](/docs/en/settings#permission-settings), regardless of your session's mode.
findings.ourState: No workflow-specific permission floor exists. Workflow `agent()` calls go through the same `spawnChildSession` as ordinary subagents, which forwards only `args.agentDef.permissionMode` and otherwise omits it so the host inherits the parent's mode. `grep -ran acceptEdits packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/workflow-tool.ts packages/shared/src/workflows/` returns nothing. A workflow launched from a `default`-mode session therefore prompts on every file edit its agents make — for a fan-out of dozens of agents, in a run the page describes as unattended.

findings.claim: A saved workflow invoked without input sees `args` as `undefined`.
findings.quote: If `args` is omitted, the global is `undefined` inside the script.
findings.ourState: The runtime substitutes an empty object: `compiledScript(makeApi(input.args ?? {}))`. A script that branches on `args === undefined` (or on `!args`) to supply defaults never takes that branch, because `{}` is truthy and defined.

findings.claim: The dynamic-workflow size guideline defaults to `medium` (fewer than 15 agents) as of v2.1.219; earlier versions defaulted to `unrestricted`.
findings.quote: The default is `medium`.
findings.ourState: `WORKFLOW_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.sizeGuideline` is `'unrestricted'`. This is a RECORDED deliberate choice with a stated reason (module note: "we keep `unrestricted` because it is what the R4 contract specifies and what preserves the documented 25-agent warning baseline"), but the reason is now argued against a doc version that has moved: at `medium` the warning threshold would be 15, and Claude's own text still says the built-in default leaves it at 25 because Claude treats a chosen value differently from the built-in default. Consequence of ours: no size advice is sent to the model at all (`workflowSizeGuidanceText` returns `undefined` at `unrestricted`).

pages.summary: Implemented: `worktree.baseRef` with the documented `fresh`/`head` values and branch-name refusal, `sparsePaths` via sparse-checkout, `symlinkDirectories`, `isolation: worktree` on subagents, `EnterWorktree`/`ExitWorktree` under their documented wire names, and `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove` hooks including the `WorktreeCreate` exit-code exemption. Two documented behaviours of worktree creation are missing.

findings.claim: A `.worktreeinclude` file at the project root, in .gitignore syntax, causes matching gitignored files to be copied into every worktree Claude creates with git.
findings.quote: To copy them automatically when Claude creates a worktree, add a `.worktreeinclude` file to your project root.
findings.ourState: The string `worktreeinclude` does not occur anywhere in our source (only in a planning spec, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md`, as an unbuilt item). `worktreeCreateCommands` emits only `worktree add`, optional `sparse-checkout set`, and `checkout`; `worktreeSymlinkPlan` handles only `symlinkDirectories`. No `.env`-style gitignored file is ever carried into a new worktree, so every subagent or session worktree starts without the local config the main checkout has.
findings.evidence: packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.ts:74-96 and :112-124; `grep -rai worktreeinclude --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist .` → only the spec doc

findings.claim: Under the default `"fresh"` base, Claude Code refreshes `origin/HEAD` before branching — fetching the default branch when the repo has not been fetched in 24 hours, capped at five seconds, falling back to the cached ref.
findings.quote: For a `"fresh"` base, Claude Code keeps `origin/HEAD` current: when the repository hasn't been fetched in the last 24 hours, it fetches the default branch, capped at five seconds, and uses the locally cached ref if the fetch fails.
findings.ourState: `worktreeBaseShaCandidates` for `baseRef: 'fresh'` emits exactly `git -C <root> rev-parse origin/HEAD` (allowFailure) then local `HEAD`. There is no fetch, no staleness check and no timeout anywhere on the worktree path (`grep -ran "'fetch'" packages/server-core/src` → no hit). A repository whose `origin/HEAD` was last updated weeks ago silently branches every "fresh" worktree off that stale commit — which is the pre-v2.1.208 behaviour the page calls out as changed.

pages.summary: Our fork implements this page's CLAUDE.md/rules/auto-memory contract very thoroughly (path-scoped rules with the brace-expansion budget, claudeMdExcludes, nested/ancestor instruction walk, InstructionsLoaded emission all match). Six concrete divergences remain, all in the memory-file loader: `@`-import position, fenced-block skipping, import depth, the MEMORY.md size caps, HTML-comment stripping, and the `modified` frontmatter timestamp.

findings.claim: MEMORY.md is loaded truncated to whichever comes first of 200 lines or 25 KB.
findings.quote: The first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation.
findings.ourState: Only a 200-line constant exists (`MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200`); there is no byte cap anywhere in the repo. Worse, the LIVE path does not apply even the line cap: pinned memory layers are read through `materializer.readText`, which returns the whole file, and `composePinnedCapabilityContext` pushes that content verbatim. The 200-line `readMemoryFile` is only used by the legacy fallback composer and by the import-scan pass.

findings.claim: `@path` imports are recognised anywhere in a CLAUDE.md line, not only when the line begins with `@`.
findings.quote: To pull in a README, package.json, and a workflow guide, reference them with `@` syntax anywhere in your CLAUDE.md:
findings.ourState: `parseMemoryImportPath` returns null unless the TRIMMED LINE ITSELF starts with `@`. Both of the page's own examples — `See @README for project overview and @package.json ...` and `- git workflow @docs/git-instructions.md` — are silently not imported. Only a whole-line `@path` (the shape our own CLAUDE.md uses) works.

findings.claim: Import scanning must ignore `@…` occurrences inside fenced code blocks and code spans.
findings.quote: Import parsing skips Markdown code spans and fenced code blocks.
findings.ourState: No fence or code-span state is tracked. Both import walkers iterate raw lines and hand each to `parseMemoryImportPath`, so a line inside a ``` fence that begins with `@docs/x.md` is followed and inlined. (A backtick-wrapped `@README` at line start happens to be rejected, but only as a side effect of the leading-`@` gate.)

findings.claim: Recursive imports stop after four hops.
findings.quote: Imported files can recursively import other files, with a maximum depth of four hops.
findings.ourState: `MEMORY_IMPORT_DEPTH_LIMIT = 5`, and both walkers stop at `depth >= 5` starting from depth 0, so five hops are followed.

findings.claim: Block-level HTML comments are removed from instruction files before their content reaches the model.
findings.quote: Block-level HTML comments (`<!-- maintainer notes -->`) in CLAUDE.md files are stripped before the content is injected into Claude's context.
findings.ourState: No HTML-comment stripping exists. The only `<!-- -->` handling in the repo is `stripAutoMemoryMarkers`, which removes exactly the `<!-- nessy:auto:YYYY-MM-DD -->` marker and nothing else; instruction bodies are pushed into the pinned block verbatim.

findings.claim: A memory file that already has YAML frontmatter gets a `modified` ISO-8601 timestamp written on every agent write.
findings.quote: When Claude writes a memory file that begins with YAML frontmatter, Claude Code records the write time in a `modified` frontmatter field as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
findings.ourState: The `remember` handler appends a bullet plus a date marker and never parses or rewrites frontmatter; the string `modified` appears nowhere in the memory subsystem.

findings.claim: A write that pushes MEMORY.md past its read limit still succeeds but returns an error instructing the model to rewrite the index.
findings.quote: If the file is over a limit, the write still succeeds, but Claude Code returns an [error telling Claude to rewrite the index](/docs/en/errors#memory-index-is-over-its-read-limit), because everything past the limit is dropped on the next load.
findings.ourState: `handleRemember` writes and returns `successResponse('Saved memory to …')` unconditionally; there is no post-write size measurement and no near-limit reminder.

pages.summary: The compaction contract is matched almost exactly — `selectReattachedSkills` implements the documented 5,000-token-per-skill / 25,000-token-total budget with oldest-dropped-first and start-of-file truncation, and the pinned capability block is re-injected from disk after every conversation-replacing event. The one unsatisfied claim on this page is the auto-memory load cap, which the live path does not apply.

findings.claim: Auto memory enters context truncated to 200 lines or 25 KB, whichever comes first.
findings.quote: The first 200 lines or 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded into the conversation context.
findings.ourState: No byte cap exists, and the live capability path applies no cap at all: the MEMORY.md pinned layer is read in full via `materializer.readText` and pushed verbatim into the pinned block. Same defect as recorded on memory.md; listed here because this page restates it as a context-budget guarantee.

pages.summary: Effort-level plumbing (per-model narrowing, frontmatter override precedence, xhigh→high clamp on 4.6) matches the page closely and carries verbatim citations. Three divergences: the Opus 5 model id does not exist in our registry, `fallbackModel` is a single string rather than the documented chain, and the default effort is `medium` rather than `high`.

findings.claim: Opus 5 is the model the `opus` alias and the `default` setting resolve to on the Anthropic API, so `claude-opus-5` must exist as a known model id.
findings.quote: * **Max, Team Premium, Enterprise pay-as-you-go, and Anthropic API**: defaults to Opus 5
findings.ourState: `claude-opus-5` occurs zero times in `packages`, `apps` and `scripts` (checked with `grep -ran`, NUL-safe). `MODEL_REGISTRY` tops out at `claude-opus-4-8` / `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-fable-5`; `DEFAULT_MODEL` resolves to the Opus short-name entry, i.e. Opus 4.8. The Bedrock/native alias map also has no `*.anthropic.claude-opus-5` row, and `claude-opus-4-6` is remapped forward to `claude-opus-4-8`.

findings.claim: `fallbackModel` is an ordered array of up to three models tried in turn.
findings.quote: To persist a chain across sessions, set `fallbackModel` in [settings](/docs/en/settings) as an array:
findings.ourState: The stored-config schema types `fallbackModel` as a bare string (`z.string()`, default `''`, trimmed on load), and `PiAgent.getFallbackModel()` normalizes that single value. A settings file written from Claude's page (an array) fails validation rather than configuring a chain; there is no de-duplication, no three-entry cap and no `"default"` expansion.

findings.claim: Default effort is `high` on every effort-capable model (except Opus 4.7, which defaults to `xhigh`).
findings.quote: The default effort is `high` on every model that supports effort, except Opus 4.7, which defaults to `xhigh`.
findings.ourState: One global constant, `DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL = 'medium'`, applies to every model, and there is no per-model default nor the documented cross-session hold on a model's first run. (Already carried in the deviation register at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:100`, but it is a changed default and is reported here as such.)

pages.summary: Almost the whole page is Anthropic-hosted GHES admin setup (GitHub App manifest, cloud/web sessions, teleport, contribution webhooks) — surfaces this fork does not ship. The two parts that do bind us, the `strictKnownMarketplaces` source vocabulary (`github`/`url`/`hostPattern`/`pathPattern`) and `extraKnownMarketplaces` delivery, are implemented with the documented shapes and cited line-by-line.

We ship no OpenTelemetry surface at all — no SDK dependency, no exporter, no metric, event, span or resource attribute from this page. The only OTEL_* strings in the repo are entries in the managed-settings env classification/approval allowlists, which merely let an administrator deliver those variables; nothing consumes them.

findings.claim: Claude Code exports a named set of OTel metrics and log events (`claude_code.session.count`, `claude_code.token.usage`, `claude_code.cost.usage`, `claude_code.tool_decision`, `claude_code.user_prompt`, …) under meter `com.anthropic.claude_code`.
findings.quote: To verify a setup that exports metrics, check your backend for the `claude_code.session.count` metric, which Claude Code emits when a session starts.
findings.ourState: No telemetry emitter exists. `grep -ran` for `opentelemetry` across all workspace `package.json` files and all `src` trees returns nothing outside `node_modules`; `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY`, `otelHeadersHelper`, `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS` and every metric/event name on this page are absent. The only OTEL_* references are five names classified as `'immediate'` in the managed-env delivery table and mirrored in the managed-approval known-safe list.

pages.summary: The page is about Anthropic billing surfaces (plan allowances, Console workspaces, usage credits, `/usage-credits`, spend reports, cloud-provider billing) that this gateway-targeting fork does not have. The two mechanisms it names that we do ship — `/compact` with focus instructions and deferred MCP tool definitions — are present. Agent teams, which the page says are disabled behind `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1`, do not exist here at all and are already recorded as a deliberate deferral (`hooks-runtime.ts` defers `TeammateIdle` for exactly that reason).

Entirely hosted dashboards on claude.ai and platform.claude.com plus the GitHub App attribution pipeline. Nothing on the page binds any code in this repository — no client-side field name, path, default or enum appears.

Describes an official Anthropic marketplace plugin and its report layout, not a Claude Code client surface. The install flow it prescribes uses `/plugin marketplace add|update`, `/plugin install` and `/reload-plugins`; we have the marketplace add/install path (registry-source + marketplace UI) but no `/reload-plugins` equivalent by name.

findings.claim: `/reload-plugins` applies pending plugin changes to the running session without a restart.
findings.quote: Then activate the plugin in the current session with `/reload-plugins`, which applies pending plugin changes without a restart:
findings.ourState: `grep -ran 'reload-plugins|reloadPlugins'` over `packages` and `apps` returns zero hits. Plugin activation here goes through the capability-generation/marketplace UI instead; positive control — the marketplace add/install surface does exist (`apps/electron/src/renderer/playground/registry/marketplace.tsx:437`). Flagged because this exact command is step 2 of the documented install flow for official plugins we support importing.
findings.evidence: apps/electron/src/renderer/playground/registry/marketplace.tsx:437 (present) vs. no match for `reload-plugins` anywhere in packages/ or apps/

pages.summary: The permission architecture claims hold: reads run free, network Bash commands like curl/wget are not auto-approved, the working-directory boundary and fail-closed matching are enforced, and every `ConfigChange`-class hook event exists. The acceptEdits filesystem-command difference is a recorded bank decision, not a defect. The one unrecorded divergence is credential storage.

findings.claim: API keys and tokens go into the OS keychain on macOS.
findings.quote: **Secure credential storage**: API keys and tokens are stored in the macOS Keychain when available, and protected by file permissions on Windows and Linux.
findings.ourState: Credentials are kept in an encrypted file backend on every platform; the manager's own header states the reason — "Uses encrypted file storage for cross-platform compatibility without OS keychain prompts." No `keytar`, Electron `safeStorage` or Keychain call exists in `packages/shared/src/credentials` or `apps/electron/src/main`.

pages.summary: This page binds us only as a plugin-import contract, and every hook event the plugin registers — `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PostToolUse` (Edit/Write/NotebookEdit and Bash), `Stop` — is in our plugin-facing event union, and the `enabledPlugins` map shape it prescribes is read by the activation overlay and the managed-policy path. Its own runtime requirements (Python venv under `~/.claude/security/`, `SECURITY_REVIEW_MODEL`, `SG_AGENTIC_MODEL`, `ENABLE_*_REVIEW` toggles) are the plugin's environment, not ours.

Binds the managed-settings delivery tiers and ~24 managed-only setting keys. Our managed policy schema (MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS) carries a good subset — permission/hook/MCP/marketplace locks, availableModels, requiredMin/MaxVersion, cleanupPeriodDays — but only 2 of the 4 documented delivery mechanisms exist, and five admin keys have no reader at all.

findings.claim: Managed policy reaches devices through four sources in priority order (server-managed, plist/registry, file-based, HKCU registry), and the first non-empty one wins.
findings.quote: Claude Code checks the four sources below in priority order and applies the first one that returns a non-empty configuration.
findings.ourState: Only two sources exist: the server-delivered payload and the on-disk policy file. There is no macOS plist reader and no Windows registry reader (`grep -a` for `HKLM`, `SOFTWARE\\Policies`, `com.anthropic.claudecode` and plist reading finds nothing in our source; the only hits are vendored bundles under apps/electron/resources). The composition module states the two-source assumption as fact, and the winner label type has only `delivered | file | none`, so /status-style channel reporting can never say `(plist)`/`(HKLM)`/`(HKCU)`.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:4 ("We have exactly two, and they are the two the documentation names"), :130 (ManagedPolicyWinnerV1); packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:48

findings.claim: A configured policyHelper executable preempts every other managed source and becomes the only managed configuration for the run.
findings.quote: A configured [`policyHelper`](/docs/en/settings#compute-managed-settings-with-a-policy-helper) preempts all four sources: its output becomes the only managed configuration for the run.
findings.ourState: `policyHelper` appears only inside a doc comment describing Claude's precedence chain; it is not a key in MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS and nothing executes a policy helper.

findings.claim: strictPluginOnlyCustomization is a managed key that forces skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers to come only from plugins or managed settings.
findings.quote: Block skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources, so they can only come from plugins or managed settings
findings.ourState: Absent from the managed policy schema. We ship the neighbouring locks (`allowManagedHooksOnly`, `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`, `allowedMcpServers`/`deniedMcpServers`) but nothing blocks user/project-sourced skills and agents wholesale. `grep -a` over all of packages/ and apps/ hits only two vendored bundles under apps/electron/resources.

findings.claim: minimumVersion is a managed version floor that stops auto-update from installing below an org-wide minimum, and is weaker than requiredMinimumVersion.
findings.quote: Prevent auto-update from installing below an org-wide minimum
findings.ourState: We implement `requiredMinimumVersion`/`requiredMaximumVersion` (refuse to start outside the range) but not `minimumVersion`. Our own gate comment names the difference and stops there, so a managed fleet with an auto-update feed has no floor on what the updater may install.

findings.claim: processWrapper is a managed key that prefixes background agent processes with a required corporate launcher.
findings.quote: Prefix the [background-agent supervisor](/docs/en/agent-view#how-background-sessions-are-hosted), its workers, and the [other covered background processes](/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers) with a required corporate launcher instead of turning agent view off
findings.ourState: No `processWrapper` key and no launcher-prefix path anywhere in source (0 hits repo-wide with `grep -a`, docs included except one spec mention). We spawn the Pi agent subprocess, the session MCP server and the headless server directly, so a corporate-launcher mandate cannot be enforced.

findings.claim: fallbackModel is one of exactly two managed keys whose value replaces lower layers instead of merging.
findings.quote: For [two exceptions](/docs/en/settings#settings-precedence), `fallbackModel` and `availableModels`, the managed value replaces lower layers rather than merging.
findings.ourState: `availableModels` is a managed key; `fallbackModel` is not. Our `fallbackModel` lives only in user-editable workspace defaults and drives Pi's retry-on-error model choice, so an admin cannot pin the fallback.

pages.summary: Almost the whole page is Anthropic-bound telemetry and retention policy that a corporate fork deliberately does not have. The one key that binds us is `cleanupPeriodDays`, and it matches the documented default of 30 days with a minimum of 1; `feedbackSurveyRate`, `skipWebFetchPreflight`, `DISABLE_TELEMETRY`/`DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING`/`DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND` and the api.anthropic.com WebFetch preflight are absent because the traffic they gate does not exist here.

ZDR is an Anthropic-Enterprise server-side posture; the feature-disable table (web sessions, cloud sessions, artifacts, /feedback, Remote Control) and the Fable 5 / `best` alias rules bind surfaces we do not ship. The only client-side keys it names are forceLoginMethod/forceLoginOrgUUID, which we deliberately drop.

findings.claim: ZDR organizations restrict login with the forceLoginMethod and forceLoginOrgUUID managed settings.
findings.quote: To restrict login to your ZDR organization, deploy the `forceLoginMethod` and `forceLoginOrgUUID` managed settings; see [Restrict login to your organization](/docs/en/authentication#restrict-login-to-your-organization).
findings.ourState: Neither key is in the managed policy schema, and the drop is deliberate and pinned by a test that asserts `forceLoginOrgUUID` is stripped as a key 'we do not carry'. Recorded here as a note, not a defect: there is no Anthropic organization to pin. Worth an owner decision only for the `forceLoginMethod: "gateway"` shape, which would map onto our own gateway.

pages.summary: Pure legal/commercial prose — licences, BAA, usage policy, HackerOne. It binds no field, default, path or enum in any implementation, ours or Claude's.

The screen-reader half (--ax-screen-reader, CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER, axScreenReader, CLAUDE_AX_STARTUP_QUIET_MS, OSC 133 markers, terminal bell) describes a TUI and does not bind an Electron GUI. The two settings that do bind a GUI — prefersReducedMotion and the colorblind themes — have no counterpart here.

findings.claim: prefersReducedMotion is a setting that reduces or disables spinners, shimmer and other animation across the interface.
findings.quote: The `prefersReducedMotion` [setting](/docs/en/settings#available-settings) reduces or disables spinners, shimmer, and other animations without changing the rest of the interface.
findings.ourState: No such setting, and no global honouring of the OS signal either: the only `prefers-reduced-motion` media query in the whole source tree covers one markdown extension's task-item animation. The renderer's spinners, shimmer and transitions elsewhere are unconditional.

findings.claim: The theme setting includes colorblind-friendly dark-daltonized and light-daltonized themes.
findings.quote: The `theme` [setting](/docs/en/settings#available-settings) selects the interface colors, including the colorblind-friendly `dark-daltonized` and `light-daltonized` themes.
findings.ourState: Our theme model is light/dark colour overrides plus a `solid`/`scenic` mode; there is no daltonized or otherwise colour-vision-adjusted palette (0 hits for daltonized/colorblind/deuteranopia/protanopia across packages and apps).

pages.summary: The advisor is a server-executed Anthropic tool with an explicit 'Anthropic API only' requirement. We have no advisor surface at all — no advisorModel setting, no /advisor command, no --advisor flag, no CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL, and no main/advisor capability pairing check. The only 'advisor' in our source is a planning heuristic of the same word.

findings.claim: advisorModel is a settings-file key that configures a persistent advisor default, and availableModels restricts which models may be chosen as the advisor.
findings.quote: * **`advisorModel` setting**: configure a persistent default in your [settings file](/docs/en/settings)
findings.ourState: No `advisorModel` key in any settings schema; the identifier appears once, inside a comment in pi-agent.ts. `PlanningAdvisor` in base-agent.ts is an unrelated in-process planning heuristic, not a second model. Our own managed-models comment nevertheless quotes Claude's availableModels text including 'and the advisor', describing a surface we do not have.

pages.summary: Bedrock is out of product — we ship no Bedrock provider and no Mantle endpoint, and the page's model-pin/IAM/service-tier material binds nothing here. It does, however, name two NEW Bedrock routing env vars that our Claude-SDK env sanitizer was written to strip and does not know about.

findings.claim: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE (with ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL and CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH) routes Claude Code requests to an Amazon Bedrock endpoint, in addition to the older CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK path.
findings.quote: Mantle is an Amazon Bedrock endpoint that serves Claude models through the native Anthropic API shape rather than the Amazon Bedrock Invoke API.
findings.ourState: buildClaudeSubprocessEnv inherits the whole ambient `process.env` and then deletes exactly three Bedrock vars — CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL — under the stated invariant 'Bedrock must never be routed through the Claude SDK path'. CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE, ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL and CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH are absent from our entire source tree, so they survive into the subprocess and defeat that invariant.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:239 (env spread from process.env), :257-262 (three-var strip list)

pages.summary: Artifacts publish a page to a private URL on claude.ai, gated on a claude.ai sign-in and the Anthropic model provider. We have no publish path, no Artifact tool, no disableArtifact / CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ARTIFACT / CLAUDE_CODE_ARTIFACT_AUTO_OPEN, and no `Artifact` entry in the permission-rule tool vocabulary. That is the correct posture for this fork — the surface is Anthropic-hosted — so no divergence is recorded.

Claude.ai/Console/cloud-provider login flows are deliberately out of product here (we authenticate per-connection, with the Nessy Gateway JWT as the first-class path). Two things it binds do reach us: the apiKeyHelper credential-script mechanism, which has no counterpart, and the cloud-provider precedence rule, whose selectors we only partly neutralise on the Claude SDK path.

findings.claim: apiKeyHelper is a settings key naming a shell script that returns an API key, refreshed after 5 minutes or on HTTP 401, with the interval tunable via CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS.
findings.quote: * **Custom credential scripts**: configure the [`apiKeyHelper`](/docs/en/settings#available-settings) setting to run a shell script that returns an API key.
findings.ourState: No apiKeyHelper, no equivalent credential-script hook, and no CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS (`grep -a` over packages/ and apps/ hits only two vendored bundles under apps/electron/resources). Rotating/short-lived credentials from a vault have no supported path: the closest thing is the gateway-specific dp flow plus the NESSY_DP_AUTH_TOKEN env bypass, which is scoped to the Nessy Gateway and not to generic API-key or custom-endpoint connections.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/config/llm-connections.ts:943-1065 (env-var credential assembly, no helper path); packages/shared/src/auth/dp/dp-binary.ts (gateway-only alternative)

findings.claim: Cloud provider credentials outrank every other credential whenever CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX or CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY is set.
findings.quote: 1. Cloud provider credentials, when `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, or `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` is set. See [third-party integrations](/docs/en/third-party-integrations) for setup.
findings.ourState: The Claude SDK subprocess env is built by spreading the host's whole process.env and deleting only the Bedrock trio. CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX and CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY are not stripped and appear nowhere in our source, so an ambient value in the user's shell silently outranks the credential the session's LlmConnection configured, on the highest precedence tier the doc defines.

pages.summary: The core config contract is implemented carefully and cites this page throughout: the five autoMode keys with snake_case wire names, per-entry parsing, the $defaults sentinel, classifyAllShell, the deliberate exclusion of project-scope settings, and PermissionDenied. Five documented behaviours diverge: the user scope is never composed, the four inspection subcommands do not exist, $defaults expands to nothing, the denial-review surface is missing, and the default-branch push boundary is still the pre-v2.1.211 one.

findings.claim: Pushes to any branch of the repository you are working in, including the default branch, are allowed by default; the protected-branch default was removed.
findings.quote: Auto mode allows pushes to any branch of the repository you're working in, including the default branch, and pull request creation by default.
findings.ourState: Our classifier prompt still carries the removed boundary: it instructs the judge to keep git actions 'high or critical if they touch a protected/default branch', and a high-risk verdict denies unless user authorization is at least medium. A routine push to main/master is therefore escalated where the documented default allows it. The `protectedBranch` fact the rule keys off has no producer either, so the rule fires on the model's own inference of what 'default branch' means.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/prompts/guardian.ts:171 (rule text), :186 (high-risk verdict rule), :226 (protectedBranch fact, declared and rendered, never set)

findings.claim: The classifier reads autoMode from the developer's own ~/.claude/settings.json in addition to managed settings, and a developer may extend the four lists with personal entries.
findings.quote: A developer can extend `environment`, `allow`, `soft_deny`, and `hard_deny` with personal entries but can't remove entries that managed settings provide.
findings.ourState: resolveAutoMode accepts a `user` scope and composes it correctly, but the single production call site passes only `managed`, and so do both classifyAllShell call sites. There is no reader that puts a user-settings autoMode block into that parameter, so a developer's personal trusted-infrastructure entries can never reach the classifier.

findings.claim: The literal "$defaults" splices the built-in rule list into the array at that position, and omitting it discards the built-in rules for that section.
findings.quote: To keep the built-in rules while adding your own, include the literal string `"$defaults"` in the array.
findings.ourState: The sentinel is parsed and expanded, but the only production call site passes no defaults object, so `$defaults` expands to an empty list. Our built-in rules live as prose inside the guardian system prompt rather than as the four addressable lists the page describes, so neither half of the documented contract holds: including the sentinel adds nothing, and omitting it discards nothing.

findings.claim: Four auto-mode subcommands print the built-in rules, print the effective config with settings applied, critique custom rules, and reset the user's autoMode section.
