findings.quote: The `claude auto-mode` subcommands help you inspect, validate, and reset your configuration.
findings.ourState: The CLI dispatches only help, version, run, validate, doctor and plugin. There is no auto-mode command group, so an admin has no way to print the built-in lists, confirm the effective rules after saving a policy, critique custom rules, or reset. `doctor` reports dropped autoMode entries by field path, which covers validation of malformed input only.

findings.claim: Auto-mode denials are recorded in a Recently denied tab in /permissions, and pressing r marks a denied action for retry.
findings.quote: When auto mode denies a tool call, Claude Code records the denial in `/permissions` under the **Recently denied** tab.
findings.ourState: No denial-history surface exists: `grep -ai` for 'Recently denied' / recentlyDenied / recently-denied across packages and apps returns nothing outside build output, and the only 'Denied' string in the locale catalogue is the sandbox egress posture label. The PermissionDenied hook is implemented, so the programmatic escape hatch the page also names is present; the user-facing review-and-retry loop is not.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1503-1504 (only Denied strings); no matches for the tab anywhere in packages/ or apps/ source

pages.summary: A guidance page, but it binds several concrete surfaces: /btw, the stream-json init event, --no-session-persistence, --allowedTools, CLAUDE.md import syntax, the 8-block Stop-hook override, /goal, /rewind and skill frontmatter. Most are implemented; three headless/interactive surfaces are not.

findings.claim: `/btw` is a command that answers a side question in a dismissible overlay whose answer never enters conversation history.
findings.quote: For quick questions that don't need to stay in context, use [`/btw`](/docs/en/interactive-mode#side-questions-with-%2Fbtw). The answer appears in a dismissible overlay and never enters conversation history, so you can check a detail without growing context.
findings.ourState: No `/btw` surface exists. `grep -ran --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.md' -e '\bbtw\b' packages apps docs docs-site` returns zero hits — the command, the overlay and the out-of-history answer channel are all absent, and it is not recorded as a deferral anywhere in docs/.
findings.evidence: grep -ran --exclude-dir=node_modules --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.md' -e '\bbtw\b' packages apps docs docs-site  → 0 hits

findings.claim: `--output-format stream-json` emits one JSON object per line and the FIRST line is an init event.
findings.quote: The first command prints plain text. The `json` format returns a single JSON object with a `result` field. The `stream-json` format prints one JSON object per line, starting with an init event.
findings.ourState: `apps/cli/src/index.ts:468-471` writes only raw `session:event` payloads (`process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(ev) + '\n')`) inside the event subscription; nothing is emitted before the first server event. `grep -an "'init'\|\"init\"" apps/cli/src/index.ts` → 0 hits. A consumer written against Claude's stream-json contract gets no init frame (and therefore none of its fields, including `mcp_server_errors`).

findings.claim: A headless `-p` run persists a resumable session by default; discarding it is the opt-in.
findings.quote: The run still creates a resumable session unless you pass `--no-session-persistence`.
findings.ourState: Inverted default. `apps/cli/src/index.ts:788` — `if (sessionId && client?.isConnected && !args.noCleanup)` deletes the session at the end of `run`; persistence is the opt-in via `--no-cleanup` (help text at `:2051`). There is no `--no-session-persistence` flag.

findings.claim: Unattended batch invocations scope permissions with `--allowedTools` rather than running unrestricted.
findings.quote: The `--allowedTools` flag restricts what Claude can do, which matters when you're running unattended.
findings.ourState: No `--allowedTools`/`--allowed-tools` flag exists in `apps/cli` (`grep -an 'allowedTools' apps/cli/src/index.ts` → 0 hits), and the headless `run` command defaults to the widest mode: `apps/cli/src/index.ts:842` — `permissionMode: (args.mode ? parsePermissionMode(args.mode) ?? args.mode : undefined) || 'bypassPermissions'`. A fan-out loop therefore has no per-invocation tool scoping and starts from bypass rather than from a prompting mode.

pages.summary: An internal-advocacy playbook aimed at humans; almost everything it references (plan mode, /init, CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, Stop hooks, /permissions) we ship. One command it binds does not exist here.

findings.claim: `/team-onboarding` scans recent sessions, commands and MCP servers and emits a replayable setup guide.
findings.quote: Run `/team-onboarding` in a project you have spent real time in. Claude scans your recent sessions, commands, and MCP servers, then produces a guide a new teammate can paste as their first message to replay your setup. Pin it in the channel.
findings.ourState: No such command or skill. `grep -ran --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.md' -e 'team-onboarding' packages apps docs docs-site` matches only one line inside the coverage map's copied page description (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:281`); there is no implementation and no recorded deferral.
findings.evidence: grep -ran --exclude-dir=node_modules --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.md' -e 'team-onboarding' packages apps docs docs-site  → 1 hit, in a doc-index description only

pages.summary: Read the full 2.1.220→2.1.158 window line by line and extracted every Added/Changed/Renamed/Removed/Deprecated line from the remainder. Most contract items are already implemented and cited in code comments; four recent ones are not, and one is a default this fork still holds at the pre-flip value.

findings.claim: `DirectoryAdded` is a hook event, fired when `/add-dir` or the SDK `register_repo_root` control request adds a working directory mid-session.
findings.quote: Added `DirectoryAdded` hook that fires after `/add-dir` or the SDK `register_repo_root` control request registers a new working directory mid-session
findings.ourState: Absent everywhere. `grep -ran -e 'DirectoryAdded' packages apps` → 0 hits. It is missing from `PluginHookEventName` (packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-runtime.ts:25-54), from `CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT_MAP` (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters.ts:122), and from `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL_HOOK_EVENT_REASONS` (:99) — so an imported Claude plugin declaring it is reported as an unknown event (a typo) rather than as a deferral. The adapter's own comment ("28 of the 30 documented Claude hook events") is now a stale count. This is the exact renamed/new-event failure mode AGENTS.md flags.

findings.claim: The default subagent nesting depth is 3; depth 1 is now the opt-out, not the default.
findings.quote: Subagents can now spawn nested subagents up to depth 3 by default (was 1); set CLAUDE\_CODE\_MAX\_SUBAGENT\_SPAWN\_DEPTH=1 to disable nesting
findings.ourState: Our default is still 1: `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:110` — `export const DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1`, enforced at `:518`. `packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:47` documents `depth | 1 | ... Default is ONE level of delegation`. There is no env override (`grep -ran 'MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH' packages apps` → 0). Note this also invalidates a recorded audit conclusion: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:555` closes the item on the old documented default of 1.

findings.claim: `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` denies non-allowlisted hosts for sandboxed commands without prompting.
findings.quote: Added `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` setting to deny non-allowlisted hosts for sandboxed commands without prompting
findings.ourState: No reader. `grep -ran -e 'strictAllowlist' packages apps` → 0 hits; the key appears only as an unchecked task in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-egress-proxy.md:26`. `packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts` parses the sandbox network block without it, so a managed policy that sets it is silently dropped and the prompt path stays reachable.

findings.claim: A per-session subagent spawn cap (default 200) and a concurrent-subagent cap (default 20) bound runaway delegation.
findings.quote: Added a per-session cap on subagent spawns (default 200, override with `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION`) to stop runaway delegation loops; `/clear` resets the budget
findings.ourState: Neither cap exists. `grep -ran -e 'MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION' -e 'MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS' packages apps` → 0 hits. The spawner bounds only depth (`DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1`) and a global concurrency semaphore (`DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY`, default 16 per packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:46) — a semaphore throttles simultaneity but never caps total spawns, so a session can spawn unboundedly many subagents in sequence.

findings.claim: The headless stream-json init event carries `mcp_server_errors`, listing `--mcp-config` entries skipped by config validation.
findings.quote: Added `mcp_server_errors` to the headless stream-json init event, listing `--mcp-config` entries skipped by config validation; terminal runs print a startup warning
findings.ourState: No init event and no such field. `grep -ran -e 'mcp_server_errors' packages apps` → 0 hits; `apps/cli/src/index.ts:468` streams raw session events with no framing object. Skipped MCP config entries are never surfaced to a headless consumer.

pages.summary: We do implement an MCP channel push (`mcpChannelPushEnabled`, `ChannelPolicy`, `channelsEnabled` managed key), but the headline behaviour — an event arriving while you are away — is dropped, and the admin allowlist key is a different name and shape from the documented one.

findings.claim: A channel event pushed while the user is away reaches the session and Claude reacts to it; several events arriving during a busy turn are delivered together on the next turn.
findings.quote: A channel is an MCP server that pushes events into your running Claude Code session, so Claude can react to things that happen while you're not at the terminal.
findings.ourState: An event arriving while the session is IDLE is silently discarded. `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2436` subscribes with `({ text }) => { ...; canDeliver()?.redirect(text) }`, and `canDeliver()` at `:2399-2405` returns `undefined` unless `managed.isProcessing && agent.isProcessing?.()`. There is no queue and no idle wake for this path: the R3 grouping/idle-wake delivery that DOES cite this contract (`packages/server-core/src/sessions/task-notification.ts:46-51`, "delivered together on the next turn ... one delivery, in arrival order") is wired to monitor events only, never to `subscribeChannel`. Events during a busy turn are also not grouped — each is steered in immediately.

findings.claim: `allowedChannelPlugins` is the managed allowlist key, and each entry is an object naming a plugin and its marketplace.
findings.quote: By default, any plugin on the Anthropic-maintained allowlist can register as a channel. Admins on Team and Enterprise plans can replace that allowlist with their own by setting `allowedChannelPlugins` in managed settings. Use this to restrict which official plugins are allowed, approve channels from your own internal marketplace, or both. Each entry names a plugin and the marketplace it comes from:
findings.ourState: Key renamed and reshaped: `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:237` declares `readonly allowedChannelServers?: readonly string[]` — a flat list of MCP SOURCE names, not `{marketplace, plugin}` objects. `grep -ran 'allowedChannelPlugins' packages apps` → 0 hits, so a managed document written to Claude's shape is rejected/dropped. The rename carries a stated reason in the field's own comment ("Keyed on the SOURCE name, not a plugin key, because the pool's channel gate is per connected source"), so this is a recorded deviation rather than an oversight — recording it as a name divergence, not a defect.

pages.summary: This is the wire contract a third-party channel server implements, and our client does not speak it: the notification method name, the params, the <channel> tag and the whole permission-relay half all diverge. A real Claude channel plugin connected to Nessy would push nothing.

findings.claim: The channel notification method is `notifications/claude/channel`, and its params are `content` (string) and optional `meta` (Record<string,string>).
findings.quote: Your server emits `notifications/claude/channel` with two params:
findings.ourState: Both the method and the payload field are different. `packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:112-114` registers `NotificationSchema.extend({ method: z.literal('claude/channel') })` — no `notifications/` prefix — and the handler at `:357-361` reads `(notification.params as { text?: unknown }).text`, ignoring `content` and `meta` entirely. `grep -ran 'notifications/claude' --exclude-dir=node_modules .` returns zero hits repo-wide, so a conforming channel server's notifications match no handler and are dropped silently. This is the same rename class as the `input.lsp`/`lspServers` bug AGENTS.md records.

findings.claim: The event reaches the model wrapped in a `<channel>` tag whose `source` attribute is the server's name, with each `meta` key as a further attribute.
findings.quote: The event arrives in Claude's context wrapped in a `<channel>` tag. The `source` attribute is set automatically from your server's configured name:
findings.ourState: No wrapping at all. The pool does carry the server slug (`packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:102-105`, `McpChannelMessage { server, text }`), but the consumer throws it away: `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2436` destructures `({ text })` and calls `canDeliver()?.redirect(text)`, which reaches `PiAgent.redirect` (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7086-7095`) and is sent verbatim as a `steer` message. The model cannot tell which channel an event came from, and there is no attribute channel for routing keys like `chat_id` — which makes the documented two-way reply pattern ("passing the chat_id from the tag") unimplementable against us.

findings.claim: A channel declaring `capabilities.experimental['claude/channel/permission']` receives `notifications/claude/channel/permission_request` (request_id/tool_name/description/input_preview) and answers with `notifications/claude/channel/permission` (request_id/behavior).
findings.quote: The outbound notification from Claude Code is `notifications/claude/channel/permission_request`. Like the [channel notification](#notification-format), the transport is standard MCP but the method and schema are Claude Code extensions. The `params` object has four string fields your server formats into the outgoing prompt:
findings.ourState: The entire permission-relay half is absent. `grep -ran 'channel/permission' --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git .` → 0 hits; `grep -ran 'permission_request' packages apps` matches only our own internal renderer event type (`packages/core/src/types/message.ts:962`), which is unrelated. Nothing declares or reads the `claude/channel/permission` capability, nothing emits the outbound request, and nothing accepts a remote verdict — so a channel plugin built to relay approvals gets no prompts and a paused session cannot be unblocked remotely.

pages.summary: Strong parity: the 100-checkpoint cap, first-snapshot pinning, the symlink/hard-link skip taxonomy and the fork-vs-named-subagent restore boundary are all implemented and cite this page. The one divergence is the skill frontmatter this page's subagent-edit rule depends on.

findings.claim: A skill can run in a forked subagent via `context: fork`, and `background: false` in its frontmatter runs that fork in the foreground — which is what decides whether rewind restores its edits.
findings.quote: {/* min-version: 2.1.218 */}A forked skill runs in the background by default; set `background: false` in its frontmatter to run it in the foreground, where the invoking turn waits for the result. Before v2.1.218, forked skills always ran in the foreground.
findings.ourState: Neither key is honoured. `packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.ts:212-221` lists the parsed skill fields and `context`/`background` are not among them; they sit in the separate "documented SKILL.md keys this runtime PARSES NOTHING FROM" block at `:224-236`, whose only effect is suppressing the unknown-field warning. The field's own comment states the gap: "`context: fork` and its dependent `background` need a forked-subagent skill context, which does not exist". So the distinction this page's restore rule turns on cannot be expressed. Already recorded as inert contract #25 in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-contracts.md:97.

pages.summary: The Claude-in-Chrome extension, its native messaging host and the /chrome command are Anthropic-plan-gated and not something this fork ships. But the page also states the plan-mode gating rule for browser tool calls, and we ship a browser tool and plan mode — that rule is not implemented.

findings.claim: In plan mode, read-only browser calls run without a prompt and state-changing browser calls (clicks, typing, navigation, tab/window management, GIF recording) prompt for approval.
findings.quote: In [plan mode](/docs/en/permission-modes#analyze-before-you-edit-with-plan-mode), browser tool calls that only read the page or browser state run without a permission prompt, and calls that change state prompt for approval.
findings.ourState: Every browser command is auto-allowed in plan mode with no inspection of what it does. `packages/shared/src/agent/mode-manager.ts:2207-2210` — inside the branch commented "Safe/Plan mode: check against read-only allowlist" — reads `if (isBrowserToolNameOrAlias(toolName)) { return { allowed: true } }`, and `plan` reaches it because `isInteractiveWritePermissionMode` (packages/shared/src/agent/mode-types.ts:98-100) covers only `default`/`acceptEdits`/`auto`. Our browser tool is a single command-string tool (`BrowserToolSchema`, packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:359-364), so `click`, `type`, `navigate` and `evaluate` all arrive under the same tool name and all auto-run. `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/browser-tools-permissions.test.ts:21` pins the current behaviour ("allows browser_tool in safe mode") without any command-level split. Claude fixed the equivalent bug in 2.1.199 ("Fixed plan mode not prompting for state-changing browser tool calls").

pages.summary: Describes Anthropic's self-hosted `claude gateway` server (OIDC + Postgres + Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry upstreams) and its Claude-account login flow; this fork ships no gateway server and targets the Nestor gateway with its own auth, so the page's product is out of scope. It does specify client-side managed-settings keys, and one of those has no reader here.

findings.claim: `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` is a managed key that makes the client ignore the developer's own customization, including protective hooks, and no lock overrides it.
findings.quote: **`strictPluginOnlyCustomization`**: this key passes the filter regardless of any lock, and it makes Claude Code ignore the developer's own customization, including protective hooks. No lock blocks it.
findings.ourState: No reader. `grep -ran -e 'strictPluginOnlyCustomization' packages apps` → 0 hits; it is not a field of `ManagedPiPolicyV1` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts) and the strict-key parser rejects unknown keys, so an admin document carrying it fails or drops it. Its four sibling locks ARE implemented (`allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` 18 hits, `allowManagedHooksOnly` 32, `allowManagedMcpServersOnly` 6, `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` 38), which is what makes the omission look accidental rather than scoped-out. Listed but unimplemented in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:46.

pages.summary: A reference for every `gateway.yaml` option (listen/oidc/session/store/upstreams/admin/enforcement/models/managed/telemetry/HTTP tuning) of a server we do not ship. Its `managed` and `Precedence with other managed sources` sections do bind our managed-settings tier, and the winner-takes-all rule and the cross-source exception list are already implemented and cited verbatim in our code; one precedence key is not.

findings.claim: An embedding host supplies policy to the sessions it launches through the SDK `managedSettings` option, and `parentSettingsBehavior: "merge"` on the winning admin source is what makes that policy apply.
findings.quote: Embedding hosts such as [Claude Desktop](/docs/en/desktop) can supply policy through the SDK `managedSettings` option.
findings.ourState: We are exactly such a host on the Claude backend, and neither half exists. `grep -ran -e 'parentSettingsBehavior' packages apps` → 0 hits, and `grep -ran -e 'managedSettings' packages/shared/src/agent` → 0 hits, so `packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts` spawns the Claude Agent SDK without passing our managed policy at the parent tier at all. `packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:29` documents the full five-source order including `policyHelper` and the parent tier, but implements only `delivered > file` — so an admin policy is enforced at our own layer and not delivered into the embedded session's own managed tier. Recorded as "inapplicable" in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:92 on the grounds that we have no parent-settings channel; that reasoning covers us as the CHILD, not as the HOST. The Claude provider is build-flag-off by default (`NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE`), which bounds the exposure.

pages.summary: IdP registration, container image, Kubernetes/Cloud Run, logs, health probes, JWT rotation, Postgres tables, upgrades, threat model and troubleshooting for the gateway server — none of which this fork builds or runs. Its Compliance posture section names two client-side egress controls; one is inapplicable to us by construction, the other has no reader.

findings.claim: For strict-egress deployments, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1` suppresses the host process's startup analytics and update checks to Anthropic.
findings.quote: **Host-process traffic**: the host process is the Claude Code CLI, which can send startup analytics and update checks to Anthropic. For strict-egress deployments, set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1` in the gateway's container environment.
findings.ourState: Not set anywhere. `grep -ran -e 'NONESSENTIAL' packages apps` → 0 hits. When `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` is enabled we spawn the Claude Agent SDK as the model backend, and nothing in `packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts` or the subprocess env plumbing sets this variable, so whatever non-essential traffic that SDK makes is unsuppressed. Reported as an unset control, not as measured egress — I did not run a network capture, so the consequence is untested. The sibling control on the same list, `skipWebFetchPreflight`, is genuinely inapplicable: we make no WebFetch domain-safety preflight call at all (`grep -ran 'preflight' packages/shared/src` matches only our unrelated DP-auth preflight).

pages.summary: A deployment walkthrough for the self-hosted Claude apps gateway server (ECS/EKS + RDS + Secrets Manager + Bedrock upstream). Nessy Desktop is a client of a corporate gateway, not a gateway server; nothing on the page binds a surface we ship. The only client-side keys it names (`forceLoginMethod`, `forceLoginGatewayUrl` pushed via managed settings) drive the Claude login picker for a gateway product this fork deliberately does not have.

Same gateway-server product on Cloud Run/GKE. Every contract on the page is `gateway.yaml` (listen/oidc/session/store/upstreams) and GCP infrastructure. No shipped Nessy surface is bound; the `parentSettingsBehavior: "merge"` / `forceLoginGatewayUrl` MDM snippet targets the same absent product.

Server-side per-developer spend caps enforced by the gateway's Postgres-backed admin API (`/v1/organizations/spend_limits`). Purely a gateway-server contract — request shapes, retention tables, pricing tiers. Nessy Desktop ships no gateway server and no admin API.

Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions at claude.ai/code, `--cloud`/`--teleport`, GitHub App auth, session sharing and auto-fix PRs. This fork ships none of it and the Claude subscription flow it requires is deliberately dropped. Nothing in the page binds a local surface we have.

A provider-routing guide (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS`, `ANTHROPIC_AWS_WORKSPACE_ID`, SigV4 vs workspace API key). We do not ship this provider; the gateway this fork targets is Nestor, with its own auth header. Model-alias defaults on the page apply only to that provider's resolution table.

Almost all of the page (network access levels, setup scripts, environment caching, installed toolchains, the default domain allowlist) describes Anthropic-hosted cloud VMs we do not ship. One section binds a surface we DO ship: SessionStart hooks, where the page names the env-persistence file contract; we have no reader for it.

findings.claim: A SessionStart hook can persist environment variables for later Bash commands by writing to the path in `$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`.
findings.quote: To persist environment variables for subsequent Bash commands, write to the file at `$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`.
findings.ourState: No `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`/`NESSY_ENV_FILE` variable is exported to hook processes and no hook output path writes session env. `hook-command.ts` exports `NESSY_PROJECT_DIR`/`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` (and the plugin root/data pairs) but no env file; SessionStart is classified `context-only`, so stdout becomes context and nothing else is consumed.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:164 (env allowlist) and packages/shared/src/automations/hook-decision-contract.ts:85 (SessionStart = context-only); `grep -rani "ENV_FILE" packages apps` → no match, positive control `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` matches

pages.summary: The page documents the `claude` binary. Our `nessy-general-agent` is a different product (a websocket client), so most flags are out of scope, but the subcommand names it does mirror (`plugin`, `doctor`) and the shared enums (`--permission-mode`, `--effort`) are checkable. Permission modes match exactly, including the `manual` alias; two smaller name/enum divergences remain.

findings.claim: The plugin subcommand is reachable under two spellings, `plugin` and `plugins`.
findings.quote: Manage Claude Code [plugins](/docs/en/plugins). Alias: `claude plugins`. See [plugin reference](/docs/en/plugins-reference#cli-commands-reference) for subcommands
findings.ourState: Only the exact string `plugin` is dispatched; `nessy-general-agent plugins list` falls through to the server-URL branch and errors with "No server URL".

findings.claim: `--effort` accepts six values, the sixth being `ultracode`.
findings.quote: Set the [effort level](/docs/en/model-config#adjust-effort-level) for the current session. Options: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, or {/* min-version: 2.1.203 */}`ultracode`.
findings.ourState: `THINKING_LEVEL_IDS` is a closed set of `off/low/medium/high/xhigh/max`; `ultracode` is absent everywhere, so any frontmatter or option carrying it is rejected rather than clamped.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/thinking-levels.ts:33-37 and :70 (`THINKING_TO_EFFORT`); `rg -a ultracode packages apps` → no match

pages.summary: The managed GitHub Code Review service (severity markers, check runs, REVIEW.md, pricing) is inapplicable. The local half is not: we ship the `ReportFindings` tool the page's rendering contract depends on, but not the `/code-review` skill, and our finding schema has no field for the re-report outcome the page requires.

findings.claim: A re-report of previously reported findings carries, per finding, one of three outcomes so the host can mark it fixed / skipped / no change needed.
findings.quote: When Claude fixes reported findings later in the session, it reports them again, and Claude Code marks each finding in the new list as fixed, skipped, or no change needed.
findings.ourState: `ReportFindingsSchema` accepts only `{file, summary, failureScenario, category?}` per finding. There is no outcome/state field, so a second report is indistinguishable from the first and the host cannot render fixed/skipped/no-change. `tools-reference.md` (the source our schema was derived from) never states this requirement — it is stated only here.
findings.evidence: packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:269-281 (FindingSchema + ReportFindingsSchema); `grep -rani "outcome|no_change_needed|'skipped'" packages/session-tools-core/src` → only unrelated task-tool hits

findings.claim: `/code-review` exists as a bundled, user-invocable skill that reviews the current diff and accepts `--fix`, `--comment`, an effort level and a target.
findings.quote: The [`/code-review` command](/docs/en/commands) reviews a diff in your terminal without installing the GitHub App.
findings.ourState: No `/code-review` (nor `/simplify`, `/verify`, `/run`) skill ships. `apps/electron/resources/skills/` contains exactly two bundled skills, `plugin-creator` and `skill-creator`. The `ReportFindings` tool therefore ships with no in-product caller — its own description defers to "active code-review instructions" that nothing supplies.
findings.evidence: `ls apps/electron/resources/skills/*/SKILL.md` → plugin-creator, skill-creator only; packages/shared/src/skills/seed.ts:31-49 (bundle is the sole authority on bundled slugs)

pages.summary: The canonical map of every project/global config file. Most of it we do implement under the `.nessy-agent`/`.agents` namespace — settings, rules, skills, commands, agents, workflows, output styles, themes, the retention sweep, CLAUDE.local.md. Five documented behaviours diverge: skill-vs-command precedence is inverted, command bodies support neither positional placeholders nor the `!` shell line, `.worktreeinclude` has no reader at all, and per-subagent memory directories are parsed but never provisioned.

findings.claim: When a skill and a single-file command share a bare name, the skill wins.
findings.quote: If a skill and command share a name, the skill takes precedence
findings.ourState: Inverted: `selectSkillSlashCommands` treats the explicit command names as `takenNames` and drops the skill from the `/` menu, so `commands/review.md` shadows a `review` skill. The module comment states the opposite rule deliberately ("Explicit commands are authored for this purpose and are the more specific declaration").

findings.claim: Command and skill bodies expand positional argument placeholders `$0`, `$1`, … in addition to `$ARGUMENTS`.
findings.quote: Skills accept arguments: <C>/deploy staging</C> passes "staging" as <C>$ARGUMENTS</C>. Use <C>$0</C>, <C>$1</C>, and so on for positional access
findings.ourState: Split. Runtime SKILL content does expand `$0`/`$1` (quote-aware, with escape rules). Custom slash commands — `.nessy-agent/commands/*.md`, `.agents/commands/*.md`, and plugin prompt-commands — do not: the substitution is a single regex over `$ARGUMENTS|{{args}}`, so `/fix-issue 123` leaves a literal `$0` in the prompt.

findings.claim: A leading `` !`…` `` line in a command or skill file runs a shell command and injects its stdout into the prompt.
findings.quote: The <C>!`...`</C> line runs a shell command and injects its output into the prompt.
findings.ourState: Implemented only for PLUGIN-provided skills on the Pi backend. `materializeRuntimeSkillContext` skips any skill without `pluginRuntime`, so a user or managed skill's `!` line is silently treated as prose; custom slash commands never reach this path at all (their expansion comment states "no shell invocation").
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:2391 — `if (!skill?.pluginRuntime) continue`; gated further by :2386 `runtime?.provider !== 'pi'`; commands path at packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:329-334

findings.claim: `.worktreeinclude` at the project root lists gitignored files to copy into every new worktree, read on `EnterWorktree` and on subagent `isolation: worktree`.
findings.quote: Read when Claude creates a git worktree via <C>--worktree</C>, the <C>EnterWorktree</C> tool, or subagent <C>isolation: worktree</C>
findings.ourState: No reader exists. We ship `EnterWorktree`/`ExitWorktree` and `isolation: worktree`, and worktree settings cover `baseRef`/`symlinkDirectories`/`sparsePaths`/`bgIsolation` — but the `.worktreeinclude` file is never opened, so `.env` and other gitignored files are missing from every worktree we create.
findings.evidence: `grep -ra --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' -l worktreeinclude packages apps scripts` → no match (positive control: same grep for `EnterWorktree` hits packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/worktree.ts); shipped key list at packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts:59

findings.claim: A subagent declaring `memory:` gets a dedicated directory whose MEMORY.md is loaded into its system prompt at start (`.claude/agent-memory/`, `.claude/agent-memory-local/`, or `~/.claude/agent-memory/`).
findings.quote: First 200 lines (capped at 25KB) of MEMORY.md loaded into the subagent system prompt when it runs
findings.ourState: `memory: user|project|local` is parsed, validated and carried on `AgentDefinition`, but no directory is created and no MEMORY.md is read or injected — the field's own doc comment records this ("the per-agent memory DIRECTORY is not yet provisioned"). A subagent authored for cross-session learning gets none.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:91-95 and the scope mapping at :38-44; `grep -ra agent-memory packages apps` → definitions.ts only

pages.summary: The full built-in command table. Nessy is a GUI, so most terminal-only entries are out of scope, and the commands we do ship (`/compact`, `/context`, `/clear`, `/export`, `/init`, `/memory`, `/model`, `/usage`, `/help`, `/agents`, `/subtask`) plus the MCP prompt format `/mcp__<server>__<prompt>` match. The one general parsing rule that binds every skill diverges: we resolve exactly one leading command.

findings.claim: Multiple skill invocations at the start of a message all load, each receiving the trailing text as arguments, up to six.
findings.quote: a skill invocation followed by more skills, such as `/skill-a /skill-b do XYZ`, loads every skill named at the start and passes the trailing text to each as arguments. Up to six skills can be chained.
findings.ourState: Exactly one leading command is matched; everything after it, including a second `/skill-b`, becomes literal argument text. `customSlashCommandInputSubmission` returns a single `{message, customSlashCommandId}` and `resolveCustomSlashCommand` resolves one id, so `/skill-a /skill-b do XYZ` loads only `skill-a` and hands it the string "/skill-b do XYZ".

pages.summary: Admin rollout copy — launch announcements, a drip campaign, FAQ one-liners. The only implementation-binding statements it carries are restatements of contracts owned by other pages (permission-mode setting values `default`/`acceptEdits`/`plan`, `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, `.mcp.json` at project root, `/init`, `/rewind`, sandbox `denyRead`), and every one of them matches our code: `packages/core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:9`, `packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/filesystem-isolation.ts:40`, `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:1067`. Model-name prose (Fable 5, `/model fable`, Opus fallback) is Anthropic product routing our fork does not use.

Describes a CLI screen-control surface we do not ship at all: a built-in MCP server named `computer-use`, per-app approval tiers, a machine-wide lock, macOS Accessibility/Screen Recording grants. Repo-wide `grep -a` for `computer-use`/`computerUse` in packages+apps hits only `packages/codex-protocol/generated/v2/ComputerUseRequirements.ts` — generated Codex wire types with no consumer — and a Pi baseline test fixture name. Nothing on the page binds a surface we do ship; the screenshot-downscaling and per-app tier rules only apply once screen control exists.

Specifies a mandatory-launcher contract for every process the product starts from its own binary (`CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER` env var, the `processWrapper` settings key, and the sibling `CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX` for shell/hook/stdio-MCP commands). We have neither mechanism nor any renamed equivalent, while shipping all three process classes the page covers. Directly relevant to a T-Bank corporate deployment, which is exactly the audience the page is written for.

findings.claim: A launcher path configured through an env var or a top-level settings key must wrap every process the product starts from its own binary; project/local settings must be ignored for it, and the env var must win when both are set.
findings.quote: `CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER` starts every process Claude Code launches from its own binary through your launcher: the background service, every session it hosts in [agent view](/docs/en/agent-view), and Claude Code's relaunches after an update.
findings.ourState: No launcher indirection exists. `grep -a` for `CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER`, `processWrapper`, or any NESSY_-prefixed equivalent across all `*.ts`/`*.tsx` in packages+apps returns zero source hits (only `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:725`). Subprocesses are spawned directly: `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/plugin-runtime-dependencies.ts:238` spawns stdio MCP servers with `spawn(invocation.command, invocation.args, invocation.options)`. `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` (34 keys) carries no launcher key.

findings.claim: A second, distinct wrapper wraps the shell commands the agent runs on the user's behalf — Bash tool calls, hooks, and the commands that start stdio MCP servers — passing each as a single shell-quoted string in $1.
findings.quote: [`CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX`](/docs/en/env-vars) wraps the shell commands Claude runs on your behalf, such as Bash tool calls, hooks, and the commands that start stdio MCP servers, and passes each one as a single shell-quoted string in `$1` for the wrapper to re-evaluate.
findings.ourState: No shell-prefix mechanism. `grep -a` for `SHELL_PREFIX`/`shellPrefix` across packages+apps returns zero hits. Shell commands run unwrapped at `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:16320` (`const child = spawn(command, {`).

pages.summary: The configuration-diagnosis contract. Our hook matcher already implements the `,`-as-`|` separator rule (`packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:318`), `--safe-mode` exists (`apps/cli/src/index.ts:129`), `disable-model-invocation` frontmatter is parsed (`packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.ts:215`), skills load from folder+SKILL.md, and settings precedence matches. Three named diagnostic surfaces on this page have no reader here.

findings.claim: `/context` reports context-window occupancy broken down into seven named categories, with the source each subagent loaded from.
findings.quote: The `/context` command shows everything occupying the context window for the current session, broken down by category: system prompt, system tools, MCP tools, custom subagents with the source each loaded from, memory files, skills, and conversation messages.
findings.ourState: No category dimension exists anywhere. `grep -a` for `contextBreakdown`/`contextCategories`/`categoryBreakdown` across all `*.ts`/`*.tsx` in the repo returns zero hits (including tests). `ContextUsageSnapshot` carries only totals — `inputTokens`, `contextWindow`, `percent`, auto-compact thresholds — and no `/context`-equivalent surface exists. Tracked open as parity row R11.

findings.claim: A `--debug <category>` flag turns on live per-subsystem evaluation logging, naming `hooks` and `mcp` as categories.
findings.quote: Start a session with `claude --debug hooks` and trigger the tool call.
findings.ourState: The CLI has no `--debug` flag at all, categorised or otherwise. `apps/cli/src/index.ts` `printHelp()` lists Connection flags (`--url`, `--token`, `--workspace`, `--timeout`, `--tls-ca`, `--json`, `--safe-mode`) and LLM flags; `grep -a "'--debug'"` in `apps/cli/src/index.ts` returns nothing. We ship the hook/automation subsystem the flag exists to debug.

findings.claim: The setup checkup covers five things: installation health, invalid settings files, unused extensions, duplicate subagent names in the same directory, and derivable checked-in CLAUDE.md content.
findings.quote: | `/doctor`        | Setup checkup: installation health, invalid settings files, unused extensions, duplicate [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) names in the same directory, and checked-in `CLAUDE.md` content Claude can derive from the codebase, with proposed fixes |
findings.ourState: `nessy-general-agent doctor` covers managed-settings validation, rejected settings layers, mandated-plugin findings and agent-definition validity. `grep -ai "unused"` across `apps/cli/src/doctor.ts` and `packages/shared/src/config/config-doctor.ts` matches only the doc sentence quoted in comments — no unused-extension check and no CLAUDE.md-trim check is implemented. Deliberate scoping is recorded in the audit (R30b); listing it here so the delta stays visible.

pages.summary: We register an OS-wide URL scheme (`nessy://`, the expected brand rename of `claude-cli://`) but diverge from the page's two load-bearing safety rules: the handler accepts one path only and never executes anything on its own. Ours accepts an action namespace including destructive verbs and auto-sends the prompt to the model when `send=true`.

findings.claim: The handler accepts exactly one path (`open`), and a deep link can only choose a directory and pre-fill the prompt box — nothing is sent or executed until the user presses Enter.
findings.quote: A deep link never executes anything on its own. The link only chooses a directory and fills the prompt box.
findings.ourState: `nessy://action/new-session?input=…&send=true` sends the prompt straight to the model with no user confirmation — `const shouldSend = parsed.params.send === 'true'` then `window.electronAPI.sendMessage(session.id, parsed.params.input!, …)`. The scheme is registered OS-wide via `app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient(DEEPLINK_SCHEME)` (`apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:197`), and the same handler also routes `delete-session/{id}`, `flag-session/{id}`, `rename-session` and `oauth` (`apps/electron/src/main/deep-link.ts:22-24`), so a link on any web page reaches them. There is no external-origin gate and no `Prompt from an external link` warning line.

findings.claim: Registration of the URL-scheme handler can be prevented entirely by a settings key, and enforced fleet-wide from managed settings.
findings.quote: To prevent registration entirely, set [`disableDeepLinkRegistration`](/docs/en/settings) to `"disable"` in `settings.json`.
findings.ourState: Registration is unconditional at app start with no setting consulted. `grep -a` for `disableDeepLinkRegistration` across the repo returns zero hits, and `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` carries no equivalent. Given the auto-send finding above, this is the missing off-switch for it.

pages.summary: The Desktop reference, and the densest binding page of the ten. Permission-mode setting values, the 20-session cross-session default, worktree-per-session isolation, plugin/connector surfaces and `enabledPlugins` all match. Six divergences: the entire `.claude/launch.json` preview-server contract is unimplemented, three Desktop-specific managed keys have no reader, `.worktreeinclude` is absent, `claude_desktop_config.json` is not read, and cross-session messaging lacks the unattended-session gate.

findings.claim: Preview servers are configured from `.claude/launch.json` at the session folder root, with a fixed field set (`name`, `runtimeExecutable`, `runtimeArgs`, `port` defaulting to 3000, `cwd`, `env`, `autoPort`, `program`, `args`, `url`), a top-level `autoVerify` flag that is on by default, `autoPort` tri-state port-conflict handling, a `PORT` env var handed to the server, and a rule that a localhost `url` must be origin-only with a matching port.
findings.quote: Claude automatically detects your dev server setup and stores the configuration in `.claude/launch.json` at the root of the folder you selected when starting the session.
findings.ourState: No reader, no writer, no equivalent. `grep -rna -a "launch\.json\|autoVerify\|autoPort" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' packages apps` returns 0 lines; `runtimeExecutable` appears only in this repo's own `.claude/launch.json`, which is consumed by the Claude Code harness, not by our product. Our Browser pane ships a single `browser_tool` whose `navigate` subcommand takes a bare URL and starts nothing — there is no dev-server start/stop, no auto-verify-after-edit, and no port-conflict policy.

findings.claim: Two managed settings keys govern the Browser pane: `browserExternalPageTools` set to `"disabled"` removes Claude's tools on external pages, and `disableBrowserExternalNavigation` set to the JSON boolean `true` blocks external navigation entirely while leaving localhost previews working.
findings.quote: | `disableBrowserExternalNavigation`         | set to `true` to turn off external browsing in the [Browser pane](#browse-external-sites) entirely. Neither users nor Claude can navigate to external sites, and localhost dev server previews are unaffected. The value must be the JSON boolean `true`; the string `"true"` is ignored.
findings.ourState: Neither key is read. `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` lists 34 keys and contains neither; `grep -a` for both names across all `*.ts` in the repo hits only the docs spec file. We ship the surface they govern: `browser_tool navigate` accepts any URL with no allowlist, no domain check and no managed off-switch — `grep -a "domain\|allowlist"` over `browser-tool-runtime.ts` and `browser-tools.ts` returns nothing.

findings.claim: `managedMcpServers` pushes MCP server configurations to all users, each entry naming a transport of `"http"`, `"sse"` or `"stdio"` plus an optional per-server `toolPolicy` map, and is the documented delivery path for third-party deployments that receive no admin-console settings.
findings.quote: | `managedMcpServers`                        | push MCP server configurations to all users in a third-party deployment. Each entry specifies a transport of `"http"`, `"sse"`, or `"stdio"`, connection details, and optionally a `toolPolicy` map that restricts which tools in that server users can invoke.
findings.ourState: Our managed policy can only restrict — `allowedMcpServers` / `deniedMcpServers` (`managed-policy.ts:129-130`) — never push a server definition, and carries no per-server tool restriction. `grep -a managedMcpServers` across the repo hits only the docs spec. Our fork is precisely the third-party deployment shape the key exists for.

findings.claim: Gitignored files are copied into a new worktree by declaring them in a `.worktreeinclude` file at the project root.
findings.quote: To include gitignored files like `.env` in new worktrees, create a [`.worktreeinclude` file](/docs/en/worktrees#copy-gitignored-files-into-worktrees) in your project root.
findings.ourState: We ship per-session worktree isolation (`WorktreeLeaseService`, namespace resolved by `resolveWorktreeNamespace`) but no include mechanism: `grep -a worktreeinclude` across the whole repo hits only `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md`. A session's worktree therefore never receives `.env` or any other gitignored file. (Our worktree root is a deliberate documented divergence — `<parent>/.nessy-worktrees/<slug>/` rather than `.claude/worktrees/` — and is not reported here.)

findings.claim: Local sessions load MCP servers from `claude_desktop_config.json` in addition to `~/.claude.json` and `.mcp.json`, and that definition wins on a name collision.
findings.quote: The Desktop app loads MCP servers from `claude_desktop_config.json` into local Code tab sessions, alongside servers from `~/.claude.json` and `.mcp.json`.
findings.ourState: Not read. `grep -a claude_desktop_config` across all `*.ts`/`*.tsx` in the repo returns zero hits. We do read the sibling sources — project `.mcp.json` at `native-sources.ts:1067`, and `~/.claude.json` is maintained at `packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:44` — so this is the one Claude MCP source of the three that has no importer.

findings.claim: Cross-session messaging is gated on whether a human is watching: an unattended run can neither send nor receive one.
findings.quote: Claude can't send cross-session messages from a session nobody is watching, such as a scheduled-task run, and can't deliver messages into one.
findings.ourState: `handleSendAgentMessage` validates only that the target id is non-empty and is not the caller's own session; there is no attended/unattended check on either the sender or the recipient. `grep -a "unattended\|isWatched\|attended"` over `packages/session-tools-core/src` returns nothing. Our `SchedulerTick` automations create exactly the unwatched sessions the rule exists for, and they carry the tool. The sender-envelope and 20-session-default halves of the same section do match (`tool-defs.ts:839`, `send-agent-message.ts:35-41`).

pages.summary: An iOS Simulator pane we do not ship: device streaming, per-device consent, four panes per session, 10-minute detach shutdown, and the two managed controls `disableMobileSimulatorTools` and `requireCoworkFullVmSandbox`. `grep -ai "simulator\|simctl\|xcodebuild"` across packages+apps hits only test fixtures and a third-party `xcodebuildmcp` plugin manifest in adapter conformance tests. Both managed keys bind only once the pane exists, so nothing on the page constrains a surface we ship.

Anthropic's own Linux distribution channel — an apt repository at downloads.claude.ai, a named signing key and fingerprint, a `.deb` pool, and `sudo apt install claude-desktop`. We ship Linux as AppImage (`apps/electron/electron-builder.yml:204`), so the whole install/update/uninstall contract is a different channel by construction. The one cross-cutting item that could have bound us — the Wayland GlobalShortcuts caveat on the Quick Entry hotkey — does not: `grep -a globalShortcut` over `apps/electron/src` returns zero hits, so we register no global hotkey on any platform.

An onboarding walkthrough for installing the Anthropic desktop app and running a first session. Every implementation-binding statement it makes is a pointer into desktop.md and is audited there: the three permission modes (`packages/core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:9`), @mention and attachments, `/`-invoked skills, the diff indicator, the plugin browser, pane arrangement, and scheduled tasks. Its environment list (Cloud, SSH, WSL) names surfaces our fork deliberately does not ship — `grep -a sshHost` across packages+apps returns zero hits.

A local persistent scheduler. Our `automations.json` + `SchedulerService` covers the durable half — a minute-aligned poll, cron matching, per-task `permissionMode`, run history, and self-management via `automation_create`/`automation_update`/`automation_list` — but three documented behaviours of the run loop have no implementation. Storage layout (`automations.json` vs `~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/<name>/SKILL.md`) and tool naming (`automation_update` vs `update_scheduled_task`) are internal-shape differences and are not reported.

findings.claim: On app start or wake, each task is checked for runs missed in the last seven days, and exactly one catch-up run fires for the most recently missed time.
findings.quote: If it did, Desktop starts exactly one catch-up run for the most recently missed time and discards anything older.
findings.ourState: No catch-up of any kind. `SchedulerService.start()` aligns to the next minute boundary and then fires `setInterval(… , 60_000)`; a tick that did not happen because the app was closed is simply never emitted, and `grep -ai "catch-up\|catchup\|missedRun\|lastRun"` over `packages/shared/src/automations` and `packages/shared/src/scheduler` returns zero non-test hits. A daily 9am task on a machine that was off at 9am never runs that day.

findings.claim: Each task starts at a deterministic per-task offset of a few minutes after its scheduled time so concurrent tasks do not hit the API together.
findings.quote: Each task gets a small delay of a few minutes after the scheduled time to stagger API traffic. The delay is deterministic: the same task always starts at the same offset.
findings.ourState: No stagger. `tick()` builds one payload at the minute boundary and hands it to a single `onTick`, so every automation whose cron matches that minute starts simultaneously. `grep -ai jitter` over `packages/shared/src/automations` and `packages/shared/src/scheduler` matches only webhook retry backoff (`webhook-utils.ts:371`), never task start time. Operationally this points a thundering herd at the Nestor gateway on any shared cron minute.

findings.claim: A per-task toggle gives each scheduled run its own isolated Git worktree, rather than running against the working directory's current state including uncommitted changes.
findings.quote: Enable the worktree toggle when creating the task to give each run its own isolated Git worktree, the same way [parallel sessions](/docs/en/desktop#work-in-parallel-with-sessions) work.
findings.ourState: The automation schema carries `permissionMode` but no isolation field: `grep -a "permissionMode\|worktree\|isolat"` over `packages/shared/src/automations/schemas.ts` matches `permissionMode` only. `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove` exist as observable hook events (`automations/types.ts:74-75`) but nothing lets a scheduled automation request a worktree, so every scheduled run mutates the live checkout, uncommitted changes included.

pages.summary: Describes running a Claude Code Desktop session inside a WSL 2 distribution on Windows — environment picker, per-distribution folder trust, Linux-path folder browsing, per-distribution recents. Nessy Desktop ships a Windows Electron build but has no WSL session concept anywhere in the codebase.

findings.claim: The desktop app's session/environment picker lists installed WSL 2 distributions and can start a session whose agent process, tools and git run inside the distribution, with per-distribution-and-folder workspace trust.
findings.quote: On Windows, the Code tab can run a session inside a WSL 2 distribution instead of on Windows itself.
findings.ourState: No WSL support of any kind. The only occurrence of the string "WSL" in the whole TS/TSX tree is a prose comment about bubblewrap sandboxing; there is no distribution enumeration, no `\\wsl.localhost` path handling, and no per-distribution trust key, even though the repo ships a Windows build (apps/electron/scripts/build-win.ps1).

pages.summary: Covers installing the CLI into a Dev Containers image via the Anthropic devcontainer feature, persisting ~/.claude across rebuilds, egress firewalls and --dangerously-skip-permissions. Nessy ships no devcontainer feature and no equivalent CLI-in-container flow; the policy claims it makes (managed settings at highest precedence, ability to forbid bypass mode) are already satisfied.

308-row variable reference plus the precedence rules for shell vs settings-file `env` blocks. Nessy mirrors many rows under NESSY_ names (expected), but has no settings-file `env` mechanism at user scope, and two documented defaults (subagent spawn depth, subagent output truncation) diverge.

findings.claim: Environment variables can be set from a settings file under an `env` key at user, project, local and managed scope; values there are re-applied to a running session when the file changes and override the inherited shell value.
findings.quote: Add variables under the `env` key in a `settings.json` file, creating the file if it doesn't exist.
findings.ourState: An `env` block exists only on the MANAGED policy tier (`readonly env?: Readonly<Record<string,string>>`, applied by `applyManagedEnv`). There is no user-scope settings `env` block: the only other `env` record in the config schema is the per-MCP-stdio-server `env`. At project scope `env` is a deliberately FORBIDDEN section (project-config.ts:138), which is a recorded security decision — the user-scope gap is not.

findings.claim: The subagent nesting-depth default is 3 as of v2.1.219 — a subagent can spawn its own subagents by default, and 1 is the value that turns nesting off.
findings.quote: Number of [subagent layers](/docs/en/sub-agents#let-subagents-spawn-their-own-subagents) allowed below the main conversation {/* min-version: 2.1.219 */}(default: 3).
findings.ourState: Default depth is 1 in both places that carry it, i.e. Claude's "nesting off" value is our default, so a subagent cannot spawn a subagent unless the host explicitly raises `orchestrator.depth`. There is also no `NESSY_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` env override. The repo's own parity note (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:559) records this row as CLOSED against the old default of 1.

findings.claim: Subagent output over the cap is truncated, but the full output is written to disk and the truncated response carries the path; the cap is tunable via TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH (default 32000, maximum 160000).
findings.quote: When truncated, the full output is saved to disk and the path is included in the truncated response
findings.ourState: Truncation is a hard byte cut at 32 KiB with the overflow discarded — the trailing marker is a bare `[Output truncated to 32KB for the parent context.]` with no file path — and there is no env override (no `NESSY_TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH`; 0 hits for TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH repo-wide).

findings.claim: With ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH unset, all MCP tools are deferred by default; the 10%-of-context threshold belongs to the opt-in `auto` value only.
findings.quote: Unset: all MCP tools deferred by default, but loaded upfront on Google Cloud's Agent Platform, when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points to a non-first-party host, or on a Microsoft Foundry deployment hosted on Azure.
findings.ourState: Unset resolves to `{kind:'default'}`, which defers only when a workspace preference is on AND a 48-tool COUNT threshold is exceeded — not unconditionally. This is a deliberate, reasoned deviation documented at length in the module header (client-side tool_search/tool_load tools rather than Claude's `defer_loading` API beta), recorded here only so the divergence stays visible.

pages.summary: Error reference covering retries, auth, network, request, CLI, plugin, tool and background-session errors. Most CLI-flag sections bind flags we don't ship (--settings, --bg, --print, --permission-prompt-tool, --resume), but three refusals that protect surfaces we do ship are absent, and one error-message contract differs.

findings.claim: A write that leaves the auto-memory index MEMORY.md over 200 lines or 25KB returns an error to the model naming the overflow, because everything past the limit is silently dropped on every subsequent load.
findings.quote: Claude wrote to the [auto memory](/docs/en/memory#auto-memory) index `MEMORY.md` and left it over one of its read limits: 200 lines or 25KB.
findings.ourState: We have the read limit (`MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200`) and we DO silently truncate at load (`readFileSync(...).split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)`), but the write path (`appendMemory`) performs no post-write size check and returns no error or reminder — exactly the pre-v2.1.210 behaviour the page describes as the defect. There is also no 25KB byte limit and no frontmatter/HTML-comment exclusion.

findings.claim: When every entry in a subagent's `tools` frontmatter list fails to match a usable tool, the spawn is refused with a diagnostic grouping the entries by cause, rather than launching a toolless subagent.
findings.quote: Every entry in the subagent's [`tools` list](/docs/en/sub-agents#supported-frontmatter-fields) failed to match a usable tool, so Claude Code refused to launch the subagent: with no tools, it couldn't act.
findings.ourState: `allowedTools()` filters the declared list against `disallowedTools` only and hands the result straight to the child restrictions. Unrecognised names, names not available to subagents, and names matching nothing in the session are all passed through unvalidated, and an empty result is not detected — the child launches with no usable tools and no error.

findings.claim: A `pkill` whose pattern matches the agent's own process is refused before it runs; the pattern is probed with `pgrep` and the refusal is returned in the Bash tool result.
findings.quote: Claude Code tests the pattern with `pgrep` before running `pkill` and refuses when its own process ID is in the result.
findings.ourState: `pkill` is only classified as a dangerous command that requires a permission decision — there is no self-PID probe. `pgrep` appears nowhere in the tool/permission path (only in build scripts and a shellguard corpus fixture), so in a mode that does not prompt, a matching pattern can terminate the agent process mid-turn.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/core/pre-tool-use.ts:1751; packages/shared/src/agent/core/permission-manager.ts:46; grep -ra --include="*.ts" -ln "pgrep" . → no hit under packages/*/src runtime paths

findings.claim: --json-schema is gated by three distinct, separately-worded checks: unparseable JSON, valid JSON that is not an object, and JSON Schema compilation failure.
findings.quote: Claude Code runs two checks before schema compilation: it rejects a value that isn't parseable JSON with `Error: --json-schema is not valid JSON`, and valid JSON that isn't an object with `Error: --json-schema must be a JSON object`.
findings.ourState: All three failure classes collapse into one message, `--json-schema is not a valid JSON Schema (<reason>)`, with the underlying reason parenthesised rather than colon-separated. The non-object case is detected (in compileStructuredOutputSchema) but reported under the schema-compilation wording; `format` is correctly accepted as an annotation, so only the message contract diverges.

pages.summary: Defines fast mode's supported models, the `fastMode` / `fastModePerSessionOptIn` settings keys, the org availability check and its skip variables. We ship a fast-mode request rewriter, and its model allowlist is exactly the one model Claude removed fast mode from.

findings.claim: Fast mode applies to Opus 5 and Opus 4.8; Opus 4.7 is no longer served at fast speed and the API rejects fast-mode requests for it.
findings.quote: Fast mode is supported on Opus 5 and Opus 4.8. It is not available on Sonnet, Haiku, or other models.
findings.ourState: `shouldEnableFastMode` matches the single literal `claude-opus-4-7` and nothing else, so it targets only the removed model and never fires for Opus 4.8 (which IS in our catalogue, models-pi.ts:92) or Opus 5. When FEATURE_FLAGS.fastMode is turned on, every request it modifies sets `body.speed='fast'` plus the `fast-mode-2026-02-01` beta header on a model the API now rejects, while the two supported models get no speedup at all.

findings.claim: Fast mode for Opus 4.7 has a dated removal, so code keyed to that model is stale rather than merely narrow.
findings.quote: Fast mode for Opus 4.7 was deprecated on June 25, 2026, and removed on July 24, 2026.
findings.ourState: The feature-flag comment still describes the feature as "Opus 4.7 fast mode (speed:\"fast\" + beta header). 6x pricing" — both the model and the pricing characterisation are stale (the page gives flat $10/$50 per MTok on Opus 5 / 4.8). There is also no `fastMode` or `fastModePerSessionOptIn` settings key and no `/fast` toggle.

pages.summary: A capability matrix across claude.ai subscription plans, Anthropic Console, Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud's Agent Platform and Microsoft Foundry. Every row is scoped to providers and plans this fork deliberately does not ship; the only statement touching a surface we have (tool search off by default on a non-first-party base URL) is already a recorded deviation covered under env-vars.

Conceptual comparison of CLAUDE.md, skills, subagents, agent teams, MCP, hooks and plugins, but it carries the cross-feature layering rules verbatim. Our hook-type set (command/http/prompt/agent/mcp) matches; the skill name-collision precedence does not, and one visibility settings key has no reader.

findings.claim: When a skill of the same name exists at more than one level, the USER-scope definition wins over the project-scope one (managed > user > project).
findings.quote: **Skills and subagents** override by name: when the same name exists at multiple levels, one definition wins based on priority (managed > user > project for skills; managed > CLI flag > project > user > plugin for subagents).
findings.ourState: Skill collisions are resolved by `scopeSpecificity`, which ranks project(3) > workspace(2) > global(1) > builtin(0) for every non-MCP capability kind including skills — the inverse of the documented skill order for the user-vs-project pair. A repo checking in `.nessy-agent/skills/deploy` silently shadows the user's own `deploy` skill; on Claude it would not. The surrounding comment cites mcp.md for the MCP arm only, so the skill arm appears unexamined.

findings.claim: A settings key `skillOverrides` hides or narrows a skill you did not write, without editing the skill file.
findings.quote: For a skill you didn't write, set [`skillOverrides`](/docs/en/skills#override-skill-visibility-from-settings) in settings to do the same without editing its file.
findings.ourState: No reader anywhere in the source tree — the identifier appears only in two planning documents under docs/superpowers/. `disable-model-invocation` frontmatter IS supported (packages/shared/src/capabilities/types.ts), so the file-authored half of the mechanism exists and only the settings-side override is missing.

pages.summary: Specifies the CLI's alternate-screen TUI renderer: the `/tui` command, the `tui` setting, CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER / CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE / CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS / CLAUDE_CODE_SCROLL_SPEED / CLAUDE_CODE_ALT_SCREEN_FULL_REPAINT, the `wheelScrollAccelerationEnabled` setting and transcript-mode keys. Nessy's UI is an Electron renderer and apps/cli is a thin websocket client with no TUI, so none of it binds a surface we ship (0 hits for any of these identifiers).

Explains the Claude apps gateway and third-party LLM gateways, developer-vs-provider credentials, and how ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN / ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL interact with claude.ai subscription billing. Nessy targets one corporate gateway (Nestor-Token against a fixed URL prefix) by design and ships no Anthropic gateway sign-in, so nothing here binds our implementation.

Specifies the anthropics/claude-code-action v1 inputs (prompt, claude_args, plugin_marketplaces, plugins, trigger_phrase, use_bedrock, use_vertex), the beta→v1 migration table and the /install-github-app flow. This fork deliberately keeps GitHub product surfaces absent and uses GitLab CI, so no input or flag here maps onto anything we ship.

The page is a GitLab-CI recipe for invoking the `claude` CLI in a job; we ship no Claude-in-CI integration and our `.gitlab-ci.yml` is build/release infrastructure with different ownership. The only lines that bind a surface we ship are the CLI flags (`-p`, `--permission-mode`, `--allowedTools`, `--debug`, `max_turns`, `timeout_minutes`), all of which are reported once against `headless` rather than duplicated here.

Most terminology maps cleanly: the six permission modes plus `manual` alias, settings-layer precedence, `.claude/rules/` path-scoped rules, agent colors/memory/isolation, plugin `plugin:skill` namespacing and MCP tool search are all present and doc-cited in code. Two definitional invariants are not implemented: the auto-memory byte cap and the home-directory trust exception.

findings.claim: The MEMORY.md index load is capped by BOTH a line count and a byte size; we cap only lines, so a 200-line file with long lines loads unbounded into every session's context.
findings.quote: The first 200 lines or 25 KB of the `MEMORY.md` index loads at the start of every session.
findings.ourState: `readMemoryFile` slices to `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200` lines and applies no byte limit; no 25 KB (or any) size constant exists in the memory subsystem.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:8 (`MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200`), :29-32 (`readMemoryFile` — `split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)`, no byte check); `grep -ran "25_000\|25600\|25 \* 1024" packages/shared/src/agent/memory` returns nothing

findings.claim: Trusting your home directory must be session-scoped and re-prompt on every launch; in our fork a home-directory grant persists to disk like any other project.
findings.quote: Acceptance is saved per project directory, except your home directory, where trust is held for the current session only and the prompt reappears on each launch.
findings.ourState: `ProjectTrustStore.record`/`resolve` persist any grant whose identity `persistence` is `'stable'`; `persistence` is decided purely by whether the platform can stat the root, with no home-directory carve-out anywhere in `projects/` or `capabilities/`.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/capabilities/project-trust-store.ts:114-125 (`resolve` returns a persisted `'stable'` decision), :135-157 (`record`); packages/shared/src/projects/project-identity.ts:112-132 (`process-only` only on stat failure); `grep -rain "homedir\|process.env.HOME" packages/shared/src/projects packages/shared/src/capabilities` returns nothing

pages.summary: We ship a real goal subsystem (`GoalService` + a `Goal`/`GoalGet` session tool, budgets, evaluator-at-settlement, continuation prompt, persisted `PiGoalStateV1`), and the fixture explicitly source-refs this page. Three contract points diverge: there is no `/goal` command surface at all, an affirmative evaluator verdict does not clear the goal, and the condition length limit is different.

findings.claim: `/goal` is a user-facing command with set / no-arg status / clear semantics and five clear aliases; we expose the goal only as a model-invocable session tool, so a user cannot set, inspect or clear a goal.
findings.quote: `stop`, `off`, `reset`, `none`, and `cancel` are accepted as aliases for `clear`.
findings.ourState: The built-in slash-command union has no `goal` member (`'agents' | 'automations' | 'compact' | 'context' | 'create-skill' | 'create-plugin' | 'export' | 'init' | 'memory' | 'model' | 'clear' | 'help' | 'subtask' | 'usage'`), and `GoalCommand` is reachable only through the `mcp__session__Goal` tool binding.

findings.claim: A `yes` from the evaluator must clear the goal; ours records an advisory `complete_suggested` and leaves the goal active until the model separately calls `Goal complete` with evidence, so a satisfied condition can keep spending turns.
findings.quote: **Yes**: Claude Code clears the goal and records an achieved entry in the transcript.
findings.ourState: `evaluateAtSettlement` commits `lastEvaluation` with verdict `complete_suggested` and keeps `status: 'active'`; only an explicit `{ action: 'complete', evidence }` command reaches `terminalGoal`. The evaluator prompt itself states "Advisory goal check only."
findings.evidence: packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/goal-service.ts:246-259 (commit keeps status, verdict `complete_suggested`), :149-153 (`action === 'complete'` is the only path to `terminalGoal`), :476 ("Advisory goal check only.")

findings.claim: Documented condition length limit is 4,000 characters; ours accepts twice that, so a condition a user writes against our limit is rejected by Claude and an imported condition is silently accepted here.
findings.quote: The condition can be up to 4,000 characters.
findings.ourState: `MAX_CONDITION = 8_192`, enforced by `requiredText(command.condition, 'condition', MAX_CONDITION)`.

pages.summary: We ship no Vertex/Agent Platform provider path — `CLOUD_ML_REGION`, `ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_BASE_URL`, `VERTEX_REGION_*`, `gcpAuthRefresh`, `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING` and `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` are absent, and `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX` exists only as a managed-env routing category. The one claim that touches a surface we do ship, the Vertex tool-search fallback, is already deliberately handled: `tool-search-settings.ts` records that our deferral is client-side and therefore has no platform fallback, and names the Nessy Gateway as the non-first-party host Claude's rule would have downgraded.

`nessy-general-agent run` is our non-interactive surface and it matches several contract points precisely — `--output-format text|json|stream-json`, `--json-schema` with draft-07 gating and `format` accepted-but-unenforced, and `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` (aliased, 600000 default, `0` = unbounded). Five things diverge: the SIGTERM exit code, the absent `--bare` flag, the unbounded stdin read, several missing flags, and a stream shape that carries none of the documented CI-gating fields.

findings.claim: A SIGTERM'd non-interactive run must exit 143; ours exits 130 for both SIGINT and SIGTERM, so a supervisor cannot tell an operator interrupt from a shutdown signal.
findings.quote: If you stop a `claude -p` run with SIGTERM, for example from `kill`, a process supervisor, or an SDK host closing the session, Claude Code aborts the in-progress turn, terminates the process tree of any running Bash command, runs [`SessionEnd` hooks](/docs/en/hooks#sessionend), and exits with code 143.
findings.ourState: One `onSignal` handler is registered for both `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM` and ends in `process.exit(130)`.
findings.evidence: apps/cli/src/index.ts:796-804 (`process.on('SIGINT', onSignal); process.on('SIGTERM', onSignal)` with `process.exit(130)` at :801)

findings.claim: No `--bare` flag exists, and the page states bare mode is slated to become the default for `-p`; `--safe-mode` is a different documented flag with different semantics (it does not skip OAuth/keychain reads and does not restrict the tool set).
findings.quote: `--bare` is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for `-p` in a future release.
findings.ourState: `parseArgs` has no `--bare` case and the help text lists no such flag; the nearest surface is `--safe-mode`, which is Claude's separate `CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE` flag and is implemented as an empty-capability-input funnel, not as a startup-cost/tool-set profile.
findings.evidence: apps/cli/src/index.ts:77-165 (flag switch), :2031-2036 (help text for `--safe-mode`); packages/shared/src/config/safe-mode.ts:1-45; `grep -rain -- "--bare" packages apps docs` returns nothing

findings.claim: Piped stdin is read unbounded into memory; the documented 10 MB cap and its clear-error/non-zero-exit behavior are absent.
findings.quote: As of Claude Code v2.1.128, piped stdin is capped at 10MB. If you exceed the cap, Claude Code exits with a clear error and a non-zero status.
findings.ourState: `readPrompt` loops `Bun.stdin.stream().getReader()` to `done`, pushing every decoded chunk into an array, with no running byte count and no cap.

findings.claim: The documented permission and tool flags for a non-interactive run are missing, and the mode flag is spelled differently — a script written against the documented names silently gets none of them (unknown flags fall into `rest`).
findings.quote: To set a baseline for the whole session instead of listing individual tools, pass a [permission mode](/docs/en/permission-modes).
findings.ourState: `run` accepts `--mode`, not `--permission-mode`, and has no `--allowedTools`, `--append-system-prompt`, `--append-system-prompt-file`, `--system-prompt`, `--continue`, `--resume`, `--settings`, `--mcp-config`, `--agents`, `--plugin-dir`, `--plugin-url`, `--include-partial-messages` or `--forward-subagent-text`. Unrecognized flags are pushed to `rest` and ignored rather than rejected. The `run` default mode is `bypassPermissions`.

findings.claim: `--output-format stream-json` emits our raw `session:event` objects, so none of the documented CI-gating fields exist — a plugin or MCP server that failed to load cannot be detected from the stream.
findings.quote: The key is omitted when there are no errors, so a CI gate can fail on a non-empty array.
findings.ourState: `sendAndStream` writes `JSON.stringify(ev)` for each `session:event` (`text_delta`, `tool_start`, `tool_result`, `complete`, …). There is no `system/init` event and no `plugin_errors`, `mcp_server_errors`, `capabilities`, `api_retry`, `total_cost_usd` or terminating `result` message anywhere in the repo.
findings.evidence: apps/cli/src/index.ts:457, :469-470 (raw event passthrough), :516-535 (`complete` handling); `grep -rain "mcp_server_errors\|plugin_errors\|api_retry\|total_cost_usd" packages apps` finds `total_cost_usd` only in unrelated files and the other three not at all

pages.summary: Most of this page is terminal-TUI input handling that our Electron composer replaces by design. Two background-Bash lifetime protections and three session/input settings do bind surfaces we ship (we do ship `bash_background`, gated by `NESSY_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS`) and have no reader at all. **РЕШЕНИЕ 2026-09-11 (владелец, QF11 = B; ledger F36):** поиск по истории промптов между сессиями отказан. Страница, дословно (`interactive-mode.md#reverse-search-with-ctrl+r`, перечитано 2026-09-11): *«In fullscreen rendering, `Ctrl+R` opens a search dialog instead: type to filter, press `Up` and `Down` to move through matches, and press `Ctrl+S` to cycle the scope through this session, this project, and all projects.»* Цена названа честно и не урезана: ОБЛАСТЬ ТАМ И ЕСТЬ ФИЧА, поэтому отказ от межсессионного вызова отказывает документированной возможности целиком, а не её углу. Что остаётся: узкая история композера — в памяти, на время жизни композера, внутри одной сессии; на диск не попадает ничего ни на одном пути, поэтому написания переменных «никогда не сохранять» сохраняют ровно тот смысл, который у них уже есть. Причина записана там, где решается поведение — `apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/double-escape.ts`, секция «THE DIVERGENCE»: ref истории сбрасывается при переключении сессии (композер при смене сессии НЕ перемонтируется), и промпт, набранный в одном разговоре, не должен всплыть в другом. Нативного рычага не остаётся неподключённым: ни один рантайм не публикует межсессионного хранилища промптов, которое хост мог бы прочитать — композер наш, а собственная история промптов вендора принадлежит его CLI-REPL, а не размещённой SDK-сессии.

findings.claim: Neither background-shell reap limit exists: no memory-pressure termination on idle sessions and no cap on subagent-owned background commands, so a subagent's runaway shell can outlive the session indefinitely.
findings.quote: Background commands owned by a [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) are instead terminated after 60 minutes, configurable in milliseconds with [`CLAUDE_SUBAGENT_BG_SHELL_MAX_MS`](/docs/en/env-vars).
findings.ourState: We ship `bash_background` with a single documented off switch (`NESSY_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS`).
