pages.summary: We ship no JetBrains plugin and no IDE integration of any kind. The page's one machine-readable surface — the built-in `ide` MCP server, its `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` tool, the `~/.claude/ide/<port>.lock` file and the `X-Claude-Code-Ide-Authorization` header — has no counterpart here (`grep -a` for all four returns nothing), which is consistent rather than a defect since nothing in our product would connect to it. The `acceptEdits`/IDE-config security warning likewise binds no surface we ship.

The entire page describes a user-editable keybindings configuration file and its context/action vocabulary. We have a hardcoded renderer action registry with its own four-value scope model and no config file at all, so the surface the page binds does not exist here.

findings.claim: There is no keybindings configuration file, no `bindings`/`context` schema, no `namespace:action` vocabulary, no chord support and no `null`-to-unbind; the registry's user-override map is declared but never written from any source.
findings.quote: Run `/keybindings` to create or open your configuration file at `~/.claude/keybindings.json`.
findings.ourState: `ActionRegistryProvider` holds `userOverrides` as an in-memory `useRef(new Map())` annotated "future: load from config" — it is only ever read, never populated. Scopes are `'global' | 'navigator' | 'chat' | 'sidebar'`, not the 19 documented contexts, and no `/keybindings` command exists in the slash-command union.
findings.evidence: apps/electron/src/renderer/actions/registry.tsx:23-24 ("User hotkey overrides (future: load from config)"), :31 (declaration), :61-62 and :116 (the only reads); apps/electron/src/renderer/actions/types.ts:1 (`ActionScope`); apps/electron/src/renderer/components/ui/slash-command-menu.tsx:17

pages.summary: Four of the page's five settings are implemented and doc-cited — `worktree.sparsePaths` (cone sparse-checkout with `--no-checkout` first), `worktree.symlinkDirectories`, `permissions.additionalDirectories` with the documented never-loads-skills/CLAUDE.md asymmetry, and per-directory instruction layering with `.claude/rules/`-shaped path scoping. Two contract points diverge: the scope model for `claudeMdExcludes`, and the `extensions.worktreeConfig` cleanup.

findings.claim: `claudeMdExcludes` is read from one user-level config file only; a project- or local-scoped exclusion list has no effect and nothing merges across scopes, so the documented team-defaults-plus-personal-overrides pattern silently does nothing.
findings.quote: You can set `claudeMdExcludes` at any [settings scope](/docs/en/settings#configuration-scopes): user, project, local, or managed. Arrays merge across scopes, so a team can set project-level defaults while individuals add local overrides.
findings.ourState: `getConfiguredInstructionExcludes()` calls `loadStoredConfig()`, which reads only `CONFIG_DIR/config.json`, and merges just the two key spellings within that one file. The one injection point that could carry another scope, `env.instructionExcludes`, is set by no production caller — only by tests.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/memory/instruction-excludes.ts:60-82 (`getConfiguredInstructionExcludes`); packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:147 (`const CONFIG_FILE = join(CONFIG_DIR, 'config.json')`), :788 (`loadStoredConfig`); packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:890 (`env.instructionExcludes ?? getConfiguredInstructionExcludes()`), with `grep -ran "instructionExcludes" packages apps` showing no non-test writer

findings.claim: We enable git's `extensions.worktreeConfig` by running `sparse-checkout set` in a linked worktree but never unset it when the last worktree is removed, leaving the main checkout in the state the doc says causes go-git tools to fail.
findings.quote: Claude Code removes that entry after the last worktree is removed, but only if Claude Code added it.
findings.ourState: The lease `remove` handler runs exactly one command, `git -C <root> worktree remove <path>`; there is no `git config --unset extensions.worktreeConfig`, no ownership marker recording that we added it, and no last-worktree bookkeeping. `worktree-settings.ts` documents the side effect but nothing acts on it.
findings.evidence: packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10210-10213 (the whole `remove` handler); packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.ts:85-95 (`sparse-checkout set --cone` is what enables it); packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts:38-44 (the side effect, noted only); `grep -ran "worktreeConfig" packages apps` matches that comment alone

pages.summary: This is the closest page to what our fork actually is — a client pointed at an organization-run gateway. `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is honored throughout and is a managed-env `routing` key; the subscription-vs-credential distinction is moot because Claude subscription flows are opt-in here. The one credential mechanism the page names that we do not implement is `apiKeyHelper`.

findings.claim: `apiKeyHelper` is not implemented anywhere; a managed settings file distributed to a fleet in Claude's documented shape cannot supply or rotate a gateway credential through it.
findings.quote: While a [gateway credential variable](/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect#set-the-credential-variable) or `apiKeyHelper` is active, a developer's claude.ai subscription isn't used: the credential replaces the subscription login for that session, and the subscription's usage limits don't apply.
findings.ourState: No reader, resolver or settings key named `apiKeyHelper` exists in any package; the sole repo-wide match is prose in a doc-verification spec. Gateway credentials arrive only via `resolveAuthEnvVars` from a stored `LlmConnection` plus the `~/.nessy/dp_auth_creds.json` JWT prefill.
findings.evidence: `grep -rain "apiKeyHelper" packages apps docs` matches only docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:682; packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:892-905 (the credential path that would host it)

pages.summary: Developer-facing gateway configuration. The coverage map (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:259) marks this page "вне продукта… страница не открывалась" — never opened — yet it binds the surface this fork is built around: a corporate LLM gateway on an egress-restricted network. Four documented knobs have no reader in our source.

findings.claim: A gateway credential may come from a command Claude Code runs (`apiKeyHelper`), cached 5 minutes by default, re-run on HTTP 401, and sent in both `Authorization` and `x-api-key`. `CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS` overrides the cache lifetime.
findings.quote: An `apiKeyHelper` is a command Claude Code runs to fetch your gateway credential, instead of reading it from a static environment variable.
findings.ourState: No `apiKeyHelper`, no helper-TTL setting, and no generic "run a command to mint the credential" seam anywhere in first-party code. `grep -rain "keyhelper|credentialhelper|apiKeyCommand" packages apps` hits only vendored bundles (`packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js`, the Pi SDK's copy of Claude's settings validator) — no reader of our own. The one rotating-credential path we ship is hard-wired to the `dp` binary + `~/.nessy/dp_auth_creds.json` (`packages/shared/src/auth/dp/`); a user pointing a custom endpoint at any other gateway must paste a static key that expires.

findings.claim: `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1` turns off background traffic outside the gateway path, and its first named effect is that auto-updates stop.
findings.quote: It disables auto-updates, so plan for another update path, such as your package manager or managed distribution.
findings.ourState: No reader for the variable (already registered once via `tools-reference.md` in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:319), and — the part that page did not cover — no off switch for the updater at all: `autoUpdater.autoDownload = true` and `autoUpdater.autoInstallOnAppQuit = true` are unconditional module-level assignments with no env, config, or managed-policy gate. On a network that only allows egress to the gateway, the app still probes and downloads from the S3 feed every launch.
findings.evidence: apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts:127 (`autoUpdater.autoDownload = true`), :130; `grep -ain "disable|skip|NESSY_" apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts` finds no gate

findings.claim: When a gateway enforces an output limit below the model's, the remediation is a client-side output cap via `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`.
findings.quote: Also set `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` below the gateway model's output limit
findings.ourState: No equivalent under any spelling. `grep -rain "MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS|maxOutputTokens" packages apps` returns only error-code strings and two comments that explicitly say the field is dropped as "capacity, not consumption". There is no way to cap requested output tokens below a gateway model's limit.
findings.evidence: packages/core/src/types/message.ts:464 and packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:94 — the only hits, both dropping the field

findings.claim: The auto-compaction window override is clamped at both ends: at least 100,000 tokens and at most the model's context window.
findings.quote: To prevent it, set `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` to the gateway's limit; the value is clamped to at least 100,000 tokens and at most the model's context window, so a gateway limit below 100,000 can't be matched and `/compact` remains the recovery there.
findings.ourState: Our counterpart `NESSY_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` is accepted over `1 … Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`. The upper clamp is honoured downstream (`Math.min(configuredWindow ?? modelWindow, modelWindow)`); the 100,000 floor is not, so `NESSY_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=1` yields a threshold that fires compaction on every turn. More permissive than documented rather than less, so recorded as a behavioural delta, not a defect.

pages.summary: The wire contract for gateway operators. Previously read (coverage map row 144, 15 deviations recorded under plan 2026-07-29-observability-and-cost.md), but its § Model discovery was not audited — `grep -arn -i "model discovery|GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY|/v1/models" docs/superpowers/plans/` returns nothing. Two concrete divergences live there. Headers, attribution block and custom headers are conformant or recorded.

findings.claim: The gateway model-list request must not follow redirects; a redirect is a failure specifically so the credential is not forwarded to the redirect target.
findings.quote: The request is `GET /v1/models?limit=1000` with a 3-second timeout, and any redirect is treated as failure so the credential can't leak to a redirect target.
findings.ourState: Both model-list fetches use bare `fetch(url, { headers })` with no `redirect` option, so the WHATWG default `"follow"` applies. The Nessy Gateway fetch carries the user's JWT in the custom header `Nestor-Token`, and the fetch spec strips only `Authorization`/`Cookie`/`Proxy-Authorization` across an origin change — a custom header rides the redirect intact. The Anthropic-format fetch has the same shape with `x-api-key`. A gateway (or a captive proxy in front of one) that answers `/v1/models` with a 30x hands the credential to whatever host it names.

findings.claim: Discovery keeps every entry whose `id` begins with `claude` **or** `anthropic`.
findings.quote: Claude Code reads `id` and the optional `display_name` from each entry in the response's `data` array, and ignores entries whose `id` doesn't begin with `claude` or `anthropic`:
findings.ourState: Our Anthropic-format discovery filter is `m.id.startsWith('claude-')` only — no `anthropic` branch, and it additionally requires the hyphen. The two dominant LLM-gateway products namespace Anthropic models as `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` (LiteLLM, OpenRouter) or `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6-v1:0` (Bedrock-proxying gateways); every such id is dropped, so the picker comes back empty against a gateway whose model list Claude Code would populate. Path ships only in `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE=1` builds.

pages.summary: Admin checklist for deploying a third-party gateway to a Claude Code fleet — gateway-side configuration, credential issuance, MDM distribution and per-model routing checks. Nothing here binds our client beyond what llm-gateway-connect and llm-gateway-protocol already bind; the two client-side rules it does restate are satisfied. Coverage map row 145 also marks it never-opened, so this is the first read.

findings.claim: A managed `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` outranks a developer's shell export because the client applies it over the process environment.
findings.quote: A managed `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is enforced and cannot be overridden by a developer's shell export, since Claude Code applies it over the process environment and lower-precedence settings.
findings.ourState: Conformant — recorded as a positive control rather than a divergence. `applyManagedEnv` writes managed values into `process.env` unconditionally ("a managed value overwrites the ambient one") and registers the name in `managedOriginNames` so lower tiers can tell an admin value from an operator export; `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is classified `routing`.

pages.summary: Setup for Claude models hosted on Azure via Microsoft Foundry — `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY`, `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_RESOURCE`/`_BASE_URL`/`_API_KEY`/`_AUTH_TOKEN`, Entra ID default credential chain, Azure RBAC. We ship no Foundry provider (the only Azure surface is the Pi `azure-openai-responses` card, an OpenAI endpoint, `packages/shared/src/config/models-pi.ts:163`), so none of it binds. Its one cross-cutting claim, `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H`, is recorded against prompt-caching instead to avoid a duplicate row.

The Claude iOS/Android app as a thin client into cloud sessions, Remote Control and Dispatch — all Anthropic-hosted or claude.ai-identity surfaces this fork does not ship. The only thing in it that touches a vocabulary we own is the permission-mode name list (Manual, Accept edits, Plan, Auto, Bypass permissions), and every one of those already resolves through our fixed table in packages/shared/src/agent/mode-types.ts, with `manual` retained as a permanent read-path alias.

The live contract for a surface we do ship (packages/shared/src/prompts/output-styles.ts). Frontmatter parsing, the `keep-coding-instructions: false` subtraction and the trusted-root rule are conformant and carry the page's citations inline. The remaining divergences were all already harvested into the deviation register (13 rows, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:224-236); the two sharpest are restated here because they change model behaviour rather than surface shape.

findings.claim: Every output style, built-in or custom, is re-asserted during the conversation, not only at session start — a second injection point beyond the system prompt.
findings.quote: All output styles trigger reminders for Claude to adhere to the output style instructions during the conversation.
findings.ourState: The style block is composed exactly once, into the system prompt, and never re-injected. `resolveOutputStyleComposition` has a single non-test caller (`getSystemPrompt`), and the per-turn context builders (`buildVolatileContextParts` / `buildStableContextParts`) carry no style block. On a long conversation the style decays with distance from the prefix and nothing pulls it back. Registered as register row :232.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts:438-445 is the only production call site of `resolveOutputStyleComposition`; `grep -arn "formatOutputStylePrompt|resolveOutputStyleComposition" packages apps` finds no other

findings.claim: The built-in set is Default plus three named styles, one of which is an autonomy posture that is explicitly stronger than auto mode and independent of permission mode.
findings.quote: **Proactive**: Claude executes immediately, makes reasonable assumptions instead of pausing for routine decisions, and prefers action over planning.
findings.ourState: Our four built-ins are Default, Concise, Explanatory and Reviewer. Neither Proactive nor Learning (with its `TODO(human)` marker convention) exists, and Concise/Reviewer have no Claude counterpart, so a `.md` authored against the documented set names a style that does not resolve — which `NO_OUTPUT_STYLE` silently reads as "add nothing". Registered as register rows :224 and :225.

findings.claim: Project styles are collected from every nested `.claude/output-styles/` between the working directory and the repository root, with the directory closest to the working directory winning a name collision.
findings.quote: Project output styles load from every `.claude/output-styles/` between the working directory and the repository root. {/* min-version: 2.1.178 */}As of v2.1.178, when more than one of these nested directories defines a style with the same name, Claude Code uses the one closest to the working directory.
findings.ourState: `outputStyleDirectories` samples the two endpoints only — the workspace root and the working directory — and never walks the path between them, so a style shipped in an intermediate package directory is invisible. Precedence is also inverted relative to the page: later directories overwrite earlier ones, i.e. the working directory wins over the workspace root, which matches "closest to the working directory" for the two we do read. Registered as register row :230.

findings.claim: `force-for-plugin` makes a plugin's style apply automatically whenever the plugin is enabled, overriding the user's own `outputStyle` selection, with the first enabled plugin winning.
findings.quote: Plugin output styles only: apply this style automatically whenever the plugin is enabled, without requiring users to select it. Overrides the user's `outputStyle` setting. If multiple enabled plugins set this, Claude Code uses the first one loaded.
findings.ourState: Parsed and surfaced but deliberately never honoured: the adapter records a per-bundle `output-style-force` deferral with reason `plugin.deferred.claude_output_style_force_for_plugin`, and the resolver's comment states the refusal ("applying a style the user did not select is the one thing this surface must not do"). Recorded here as a documented-field divergence, not a defect — it is a reasoned security decision, registered twice (:233 and :248).

pages.summary: Product landing page: install methods per surface (native installer, Homebrew, WinGet, VS Code, Desktop, Web, JetBrains), a capability tour, and a surface-chooser table. Every binding statement is about installing or reaching Anthropic-hosted surfaces we do not ship. The features it names that we do have — CLAUDE.md/auto memory, skills, hooks, subagents, dynamic workflows — are each bound by their own page. Already read in a prior pass (coverage map row 148, 8 deviations under B1); nothing new surfaced on re-read.

A comparison matrix of the surfaces Claude Code runs on (CLI, Desktop, VS Code, JetBrains, Web, Mobile) and the away-from-terminal mechanisms (Dispatch, Remote Control, Channels, Slack, scheduled tasks). Pure routing prose — no field names, defaults, paths or precedence rules. Its one claim about the desktop surface, that Desktop supports gateway providers through a third-party inference configuration rather than `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, describes Anthropic's desktop app, not ours.

Audited before (coverage map row 14, 🟩, 1 deviation recorded), and the two big structural rows — project-context layering and TTL auto-selection — are already registered. The § Disable prompt caching table was missed: none of its five environment variables has a reader anywhere in the repository.

findings.claim: Prompt caching can be turned off entirely or per model family by setting one of five environment variables to `1`: `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING`, `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_HAIKU`, `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_SONNET`, `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_OPUS`, `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_FABLE`.
findings.quote: To turn it off, set one of these environment variables to `1`:
findings.ourState: No reader for any of the five, under the documented spelling or a `NESSY_`-prefixed one, and no config toggle either. `grep -rain "promptcach|prompt_cach" packages apps` returns only the `extendedPromptCache` TTL toggle and the interceptor's `cache_control` rewriters — every one of which upgrades or strips a TTL, none of which can remove the breakpoint. There is no way to disable caching for a model or provider while debugging, which is the page's stated use.
findings.evidence: grep -rain "DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING|PROMPT_CACHING_1H|PROMPT_CACHING_5M" packages apps scripts → no hits; the full toggle surface is packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:129 and packages/shared/src/unified-network-interceptor.ts:367,437

findings.claim: The one-hour TTL is opted into with `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1`, and `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1` forces the five-minute TTL back regardless of authentication — specifically so a managed-settings `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` can be overridden locally.
findings.quote: Set `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1` to force the five-minute TTL regardless of authentication.
findings.ourState: Our counterpart is a single boolean, `extendedPromptCache` (default `false`), reachable only through the desktop Settings → AI toggle and its RPC pair. Neither env spelling is read, so there is no local override of a policy-delivered value and no way to set the TTL on the headless server or in CI. The auto-selection half of this section is already registered (deviation-register.md:406); the two override variables are not.

pages.summary: A copy-paste prompt catalogue rendered from an inline JSX component — roughly 90 prompt records with `slots`, `roles`, `sdlc` phase and `nextHref` fields, plus a closing prose section on prompt patterns. The record schema belongs to the docs site's own React component, not to any client contract: no settings key, file path, event name, tool name or default appears on the page. Checked the full 1389 lines for slash-command or flag definitions; the only command-shaped strings are cross-references to `/memory` and a suggested user-authored `/changelog` skill.

Onboarding tutorial for the terminal CLI: install script, claude.ai/Console login, first session, essential shell/session commands. The only implementation-binding statements are the permission-mode names, and those are present.

Remote Control pairs a local session with claude.ai/Claude mobile through Anthropic-hosted infrastructure and requires a claude.ai OAuth login — a surface this fork deliberately does not ship (`disableRemoteControl`, Trusted Devices, `/rc`, mobile push all absent by design). One adjacent statement binds a surface we do ship: the notification presence gate.

findings.claim: The notification presence gate has a documented escape hatch: a marker-file path in CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE suppresses notifications whenever the file exists, extending suppression beyond "the focused window" to "the user is at the machine".
findings.quote: As of v2.1.181, you can set [`CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE`](/docs/en/env-vars) to a marker file path to extend this to any time you are at the machine, even in another window: notifications are skipped while the file exists.
findings.ourState: Our PushNotification presence gate is window-focus only. `showAgentNotification` returns exactly three suppression reasons — `'window-focused' | 'notifications-disabled' | 'unsupported'` — and reads no presence-marker file and no env override. A user at the machine in another window still gets notified.
findings.evidence: apps/electron/src/main/notifications.ts:105 (reason union) and :117 (the only presence branch); repo-wide `grep -rain -e 'CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE' -e 'presenceFile'` over packages/ apps/ returns 0 hits

pages.summary: Routines are saved configurations executing on Anthropic-managed cloud infrastructure with schedule/API/GitHub triggers, the `/fire` endpoint under the `experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01` beta header, cloud environments and claude.ai connectors. Nothing here binds a surface this fork ships; our durable scheduling is the local automations tier, which `desktop-scheduled-tasks.md` governs, not this page.

The cron half is at parity and cited line-by-line in our source: CronCreate/CronList/CronDelete, the 5-field dialect with L/W/?/MON/JAN rejected and vixie OR semantics, 8-char IDs, the 50-task cap, 7-day expiry with a final fire, ID-derived jitter, the once-a-second tick behind an idle gate, the symlink refusal, and a CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON kill switch. The `/loop` half — the bundled skill, `loop.md`, and `ScheduleWakeup` — is entirely absent.

findings.claim: `/loop` is a bundled skill that runs a prompt repeatedly on a fixed interval or a Claude-chosen one.
findings.quote: The `/loop` [bundled skill](/docs/en/commands) is the quickest way to run a prompt on repeat while the session stays open.
findings.ourState: No `loop` skill exists. The bundled-skill tier is real and populated — `bundledSkillSlugs` seeds `resources/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md` — but ships only `plugin-creator` and `skill-creator`. (Note: the plan that deferred this recorded "no built-in tier" as the blocker; that reason is now stale, the tier exists.)
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/skills/seed.ts:41 (`bundledSkillSlugs`); `ls apps/electron/resources/skills` → `plugin-creator`, `skill-creator`; `grep -rain '/loop' packages apps` returns only comments, e.g. packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/cron-tools.ts:74

findings.claim: A `loop.md` file replaces the built-in maintenance prompt, read project-first then user, re-read each iteration, truncated past 25,000 bytes.
findings.quote: A `loop.md` file replaces the built-in maintenance prompt with your own instructions.
findings.ourState: No reader for `loop.md` at either scope. `grep -rain "'loop.md'" packages apps` returns one hit, in an unrelated system-prompt import test fixture.

findings.claim: A self-paced loop ends itself by calling ScheduleWakeup with stop: true, which cancels the pending wakeup immediately.
findings.quote: Claude calls the [`ScheduleWakeup` tool](/docs/en/tools-reference) with `stop: true`, which cancels the pending wakeup immediately.
findings.ourState: No ScheduleWakeup tool. The session tool registry defines CronCreate/CronList/CronDelete and no wakeup tool; there is no self-paced loop for it to re-arm, and no per-task no-jitter flag the dynamic loop would need. Recorded as a deliberate deferral with a costed follow-up.

pages.summary: Install methods, binary signing and uninstall are inapplicable (we ship a signed Electron DMG/NSIS with electron-updater, not a native installer). pages.summary: Ultraplan hands a plan to a Claude Code on the web session and requires a claude.ai cloud account, a GitHub repo and a cloud environment; it is explicitly unavailable on third-party providers. Nothing on the page binds a surface we ship: the plan-approval dialog's extra option, the `◇/◆ ultraplan` status indicator and the teleport-back dialog all live inside the cloud handoff.

`/code-review ultra` and the `claude ultrareview` subcommand run a reviewer fleet in Anthropic's cloud sandbox, require claude.ai auth, and are unavailable on third-party providers and under Zero Data Retention. The concrete numbers it binds (500 changed files / 8,000 changed lines, `--timeout` default 30, exit codes 0/1/130, free-run and usage-credit billing) all describe the remote service and its CLI wrapper, neither of which this fork ships.

The whole surface is missing. The page binds a settings object (`voice.enabled`, `voice.mode` in `hold`/`tap`, `voice.autoSubmit`), a keybinding action `voice:pushToTalk` in the `Chat` context defaulting to `Space`, a three-word auto-submit threshold, 15s-silence / 2-minute recording caps, and a 20-language allowlist keyed off the `language` setting. None of it exists in this repo; `pushToTalk`, `autoSubmit` and `voice:` have 0 hits outside dist bundles and audio-mimetype tests. The page is CLI/VS-Code scoped, so this is plausibly a product scope decision rather than a defect — but it is undeclared: no plan, deviation-register row or audit row covers it.

findings.claim: A `bin/` directory at the plugin root is added to the Bash tool's PATH while the plugin is enabled, making its executables invokable as bare commands.

findings.ourState: We detect `bin/` files and reason about which ones a manifest command already reaches, but we never extend the Bash tool's PATH from a bundle. An executable that no capability references by path is classified unrunnable and left deferred, so a plugin whose command/agent/hook invokes its helper as a bare name fails. The code states the deviation in its own comment.

findings.claim: Hook output above 50K is written to disk and replaced with a path plus a preview, rather than being injected into context or dropped.
findings.quote: Hook output over 50K saved to disk with a path + preview instead of injected into context
findings.ourState: We buffer hook stdout+stderr to a hard 8,192-byte ceiling and silently discard the remainder (a `truncated: true` flag is set on the result but no content is preserved and nothing is written to disk). Because `getHookCommandPreToolDecision` JSON-parses that same truncated stdout, a hook that emits a decision object larger than 8 KiB has its JSON cut mid-object and its decision is lost entirely — a fail-open on any hook with a verbose payload.

One real divergence, and it is a contradiction inside our own tree.

findings.claim: A `PreCompact` hook can stop a compaction, either by exiting 2 or by returning a top-level `decision: "block"`.
findings.quote: PreCompact hooks can block compaction by exiting with code 2 or returning {"{"}"decision":"block"{"}"}
findings.ourState: PreCompact cannot block anything, and the two halves of our own contract disagree. `hook-decision-contract.ts` lists PreCompact in `TOP_LEVEL_BLOCK_EVENTS`, so its parsed output is allowed to carry `block`/`deny` + `reason` — but the frozen event table declares it `kind: 'observational'`, and its single emission site awaits `options.emit('PreCompact', …)` whose signature returns `Promise<void> | void`, so any decision the parser produced is discarded before compaction proceeds. A hook author writing the documented blocker sees it accepted and parsed, and the context is compacted anyway.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:83 (`kind: 'observational'`) vs packages/shared/src/automations/hook-decision-contract.ts:49 (PreCompact in TOP_LEVEL_BLOCK_EVENTS); emission at packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:151 with the void-returning `emit` declared at :28

findings.ourState: Not implemented, and recorded as a deliberate deferral in the CLI module header: prune, transitive `enable` and dependent-blocking `disable` all need a dependency graph plus an auto-installed provenance bit that does not exist yet. `store.prune()` (management-service-v2.ts:626) is store GC, not this verb.

pages.summary: Week-19 digest: plugins from .zip/URL, cross-project Ctrl+R, plus 13 wins. `worktree.baseRef` with the documented `fresh` default and `autoMode.hard_deny` are both implemented exactly (worktree-settings.ts:72, managed-policy.ts:469); session id reaches Bash subprocesses as `NESSY_SESSION_ID`. Two items bind surfaces we ship and are absent: the effort channel into hooks/Bash, and OTEL_* subprocess isolation.

findings.claim: Hooks receive the session's active effort level, both as an `effort.level` field in the hook JSON input and as a `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` environment variable; Bash tool commands can read the same variable.
findings.quote: Hooks now receive the active effort level via the `effort.level` JSON input field and the `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` environment variable, and Bash tool commands can read $CLAUDE_EFFORT
findings.ourState: `SdkAutomationInput` — the exact object serialised to hook stdin by `hookCommandStdinPayload` — has no `effort` member of any spelling, and the hook env builder emits only NESSY_EVENT/NESSY_EVENT_DATA/NESSY_SESSION_ID/NESSY_SESSION_NAME/NESSY_WORKSPACE_ID plus payload fields. `CLAUDE_EFFORT`/`NESSY_EFFORT` exist ONLY as skill-body substitution placeholders (runtime-skill-content.ts:136), never as a real env var, so neither a hook nor a Bash command can read one.

findings.claim: Bash, hook, MCP and LSP subprocesses no longer inherit OTEL_* environment variables from the host process.
findings.quote: Subprocesses such as Bash, hooks, MCP, and LSP no longer inherit OTEL_* environment variables, so OTEL-instrumented apps run via the Bash tool no longer pick up the CLI's own OTLP endpoint
findings.ourState: Every subprocess inherits the host env wholesale. MCP stdio filters only a fixed 12-entry credential blocklist that contains no OTEL_ key; the Pi subprocess (which hosts the Bash tool) spawns with `...process.env`; the hook runner env is built from the full `process.env`. `grep -ran -a "OTEL_" packages apps` finds no scrubbing site at all — only settings/telemetry readers.

pages.summary: Week-20 digest: agent view, /goal, fast mode on Opus 4.7, plus 11 wins. Hook `args: string[]` exec form, `continueOnBlock`, and `terminalSequence` (with the OSC allowlist) are all implemented; `claude plugin details` lists LSP servers; the root-level `SKILL.md`-with-no-`skills/` layout is handled (claude.ts:626). Two name/env contracts diverge.

findings.claim: The Agent tool's `subagent_type` resolves case-insensitively AND separator-insensitively, so "Code Reviewer" reaches the agent named code-reviewer.
findings.quote: Agent tool subagent_type now matches case- and separator-insensitively, so "Code Reviewer" resolves to code-reviewer
findings.ourState: `resolveAgentDefinition` normalises with `normalizeName` = `name.trim().toLowerCase()` only. No separator folding: spaces and underscores are not collapsed to hyphens, so "Code Reviewer" normalises to "code reviewer", misses both the name match and the author-declared alias list, and throws `Unknown agent "Code Reviewer"`. This is the same class as the Task→Agent rename that broke every turn.

findings.claim: MCP stdio servers receive CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR in their spawn environment, the same as hooks, and configs may reference ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} inside commands.
findings.quote: MCP stdio servers now receive CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR in their environment, matching hooks, and plugin configs can reference ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} in commands
findings.ourState: Only half. Plugin-supplied MCP servers get the project dir via `claudeCompatPluginEnv` (`NESSY_PROJECT_DIR` + `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`). Native and project `.mcp.json` stdio servers take the non-plugin branch, whose env is `{...processEnv, ...getProxyEnvVars(), ...config.env}` — no project-dir variable is injected, so `${NESSY_PROJECT_DIR}`/`${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` in a project `.mcp.json` command expands from `process.env` and resolves to nothing.

pages.summary: Week-21 digest: auto mode on Pro, /usage attribution, /code-review, plus 12 wins. `worktree.bgIsolation` ships with both documented values (worktree-settings.ts:20) — our default is `none` rather than Claude's `worktree`, which the module header records as a deliberate, reasoned divergence. `allowAllClaudeAiMcps` is a recorded inapplicable (no claude.ai connector surface). The plugin dependency verbs are the open item.

findings.claim: Plugin enable/disable is dependency-aware: disabling refuses while an enabled dependent exists, and enabling force-enables transitive dependencies.
findings.quote: claude plugin disable now refuses when another enabled plugin depends on the target, and claude plugin enable force-enables transitive dependencies
findings.ourState: Neither verb exists in the CLI (only `validate`, `list`/`ls`, `details`), and the module header names both as deliberately-not-implemented pending a dependency graph and an auto-installed provenance bit. Enablement itself is scope policy (`policyStore.resolveScopes(...).global`) with no dependent check on either direction.

pages.summary: Week-22 digest: Opus 4.8, dynamic workflows, security-guidance plugin, fast mode on Opus 4.8, plus 13 wins. Opus 4.8 is in the model table with its Bedrock/EU/global aliases and 4.6→4.8 upgrade mapping (config/models.ts:17,62); `ultracode` is the workflow trigger constant; `defaultEnabled: false` is honoured with marketplace-entry precedence; skill/command `disallowed-tools` is fully implemented (the AGENTS.md trap note about skills is now stale). Three items diverge, one of them a live default.

findings.claim: Fast mode's default model moved to Opus 4.8; Opus 4.7 and 4.6 keep the old price and Opus 4.6 fast mode is deprecated.
findings.quote: Fast mode now defaults to Opus 4.8 at $10/$50 per MTok: 2x the standard rate for about 2.5x the speed. Opus 4.7 and 4.6 stay at $30/$150. Opus 4.6 fast mode is deprecated.
findings.ourState: `shouldEnableFastMode` returns true for exactly one literal — `model === 'claude-opus-4-7'`. A session on `claude-opus-4-8` (which IS in our model table and IS the current default upstream) never gets the fast-mode beta header, so the fast toggle is silently inert on the model fast mode now defaults to. Stale pin, not a policy decision — the comment still reads "Only activates for Opus 4.7".

findings.claim: A SessionStart hook can return `reloadSkills: true` to make skills it installed available in the same session, and `/reload-skills` re-scans skill directories without a restart.
findings.quote: New /reload-skills command re-scans skill directories without restarting, and SessionStart hooks can return reloadSkills: true to make skills they install available in the same session
findings.ourState: `reloadSkills` has zero occurrences in any .ts/.tsx in the repo (grep -ran -a, node_modules excluded) — the only hit anywhere is a docs file listing it as an open R9 item. The hook output parser reads `additionalContext`, `updatedInput`, `updatedToolOutput`, `worktreePath`, `retry`, elicitation `action`/`content` and the universal five, and ignores anything else, so a SessionStart hook that installs a skill cannot surface it this session.

findings.claim: A `MessageDisplay` hook event fires per assistant message and lets a hook transform or hide the displayed text.
findings.quote: New MessageDisplay hook event lets hooks transform or hide assistant message text as it is displayed
findings.ourState: Not emitted. `PluginHookEventName` carries 28 of the documented events plus two of our own and deliberately excludes `MessageDisplay`; a plugin declaring it imports as a recorded deferral (`plugin.deferred.event_message_display_unsupported`) rather than registering a hook that can never fire. Reason on record: no per-message display interception channel exists.

pages.summary: Week-23 digest: auto mode on third-party providers (inapplicable — we ship none), safer automatic edits, /plugin list, managed version gates, plus 11 wins. The protected-path floor is implemented verbatim including the per-mode table and the bypassPermissions carve-out (protected-paths.ts:136-:157, :191); `requiredMinimumVersion`/`requiredMaximumVersion` and the `workflow`→`ultracode` keyword rename both landed; Stop/SubagentStop `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` is honoured.

findings.claim: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES values are attached as labels on emitted metric datapoints.
findings.quote: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES values are now attached as labels on metric datapoints, so you can slice usage metrics by custom dimensions like team or repo
findings.ourState: We ship OTLP usage metrics, but `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` is read nowhere in the repo (grep -ran -a across packages/ and apps/ → 0 hits). The metrics module reads only the exporter selectors, endpoints, headers, timeout, protocol and export interval, so no custom resource dimension reaches a datapoint.

findings.claim: `plugin list` accepts `--enabled` / `--disabled` to show only plugins in that state.
findings.quote: The new /plugin list command prints your installed plugins inline, without opening the /plugin menu, and is also available as claude plugin list from the shell. In the interactive form, add `--enabled` or `--disabled` to show only plugins in that state.
findings.ourState: `plugin list` (and its `ls` shorthand) exists and prints name/version/marketplace/global-enable-status, but `runList(options)` takes no argv and parses no flags; `--enabled`/`--disabled` are silently ignored.

pages.summary: Week-24 digest: /cd, nested subagents, safe mode, plus 12 wins. Safe mode is implemented with both the native `NESSY_SAFE_MODE` and the `CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE` compat spelling (config/safe-mode.ts:63,66); `disableBundledSkills`, `enforceAvailableModels`, the session-title `language` setting, and tool-name globs in deny rules all exist. The five-level nesting cap is not a divergence — our `DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1` matches Claude's documented default spawn depth, which the cap merely bounds. The fallback chain does diverge.

findings.claim: `fallbackModel` holds an ordered list of up to three models, each tried in turn when the primary is overloaded or unavailable.
findings.quote: fallbackModel configures up to three fallback models tried in order when the primary is overloaded or unavailable, and --fallback-model now applies to interactive sessions too
findings.ourState: `fallbackModel` is a single string in both the schema (`z.string()`) and the default (`''`), and the runtime does exactly one hop: `getRetryFallbackModel` returns that one id, `setModel`s to it, and retries once with `fallbackModelRetry: true` — a second failure has nowhere to go. There is no `fallbackModels` array anywhere in the repo.

pages.summary: Week-25 digest: Artifacts (claude.ai-hosted, inapplicable), match-by-input-parameter, /config key=value, plus 11 wins. The `Tool(param:value)` rule form is implemented correctly including the deny/ask-only restriction and the `*` value wildcard (claude-permission-rules.ts:118-:138); `attribution.sessionUrl` and `CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE` bind claude.ai/mobile surfaces we do not ship; agent teams are a recorded deferral (R23). One sandbox setting key has no reader.

findings.claim: A `sandbox.allowAppleEvents` opt-in setting lets sandboxed commands send Apple Events on macOS.
findings.quote: New sandbox.allowAppleEvents opt-in setting lets sandboxed commands send Apple Events on macOS
findings.ourState: No occurrence of `allowAppleEvents` (or `AppleEvent` at all) anywhere in the repo. `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS` is a closed seven-entry list — excludedCommands, deniedReadRoots, deniedWriteRoots, additionalWritableRoots, allowUnsandboxedCommands, network, filesystem — and unknown keys are rejected/stripped, so an admin or user who writes the documented key gets a validation drop rather than the opt-in. We do ship the macOS sandbox this governs.

pages.summary: Week-26 digest: `claude mcp login/logout`, shell-mode responses, plus 11 wins. `autoMode.classifyAllShell` is implemented, and org model restrictions already reach the picker/model selection. Three items bind surfaces we ship and are absent: the shell-mode response default, the sandbox credential block, and the CLI MCP auth verbs.

findings.claim: Output from a `!`-prefixed command now gets a model response by default; `respondToBashCommands: false` in settings.json restores the old context-only behavior.
findings.quote: To keep the earlier behavior, where the output is added to context without a response, set respondToBashCommands to false in settings.json.
findings.ourState: We ship `!` shell mode in the composer, and it is stuck on the pre-change behavior: `runShellCommand` spawns the command, records the result and returns — it never queues a turn — and `respondToBashCommands` has zero occurrences in the repo, so there is neither the new default nor the escape hatch.

findings.claim: A `sandbox.credentials` setting blocks sandboxed commands from reading credential files and secret environment variables, with `files` and `envVars` sub-keys.
findings.quote: New sandbox.credentials setting blocks sandboxed commands from reading credential files and secret environment variables
findings.ourState: `credentials` is not a member of `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS`, so the key is stripped as unknown. The name appears in this repo only as a shape ANALOGY in two comments ("an individual invalid entry in `files` or `envVars` is stripped… a wholly invalid `credentials` value is dropped") borrowed to describe tolerant parsing of `sandbox.network` and of the permission DSL — the setting itself has no reader and no enforcement.

findings.claim: `claude mcp login <name>` runs a configured server's OAuth flow from the shell and `claude mcp logout <name>` clears its stored credentials, without opening a session.
findings.quote: New `claude mcp login <name>` and `claude mcp logout <name>` commands authenticate a configured MCP server from your shell instead of the interactive /mcp menu.
findings.ourState: The CLI has no `mcp` subcommand at all (no `case 'mcp'` in the dispatcher); its verbs are session/doctor/plugin/run. MCP OAuth itself exists in-app (plugins/mcp-credentials.ts, mcp-token-refresh.ts), so this is a missing shell surface over a capability we have, not a missing capability.

pages.summary: Week-27 digest. The three highest-risk items are already matched: the subagent `background` frontmatter field and background-by-default scheduling, the `manual` synonym for the `default` permission mode, the hyphenated-identifier hook-matcher exact-match rule, and the AskUserQuestion no-auto-continue default. Two turn-level resilience behaviours (stream idle watchdog, rate-limit auto-retry) are absent, and two built-in-catalogue items differ.

findings.claim: A response stream that emits no events for 5 minutes must be aborted and retried; the watchdog is on by default for every provider and is disabled by an env var.
findings.quote: The streaming idle watchdog is now on by default for all providers: it aborts and retries when a response stream produces no events for 5 minutes (CLAUDE\_ENABLE\_STREAM\_WATCHDOG=0 to disable)
findings.ourState: No streaming idle watchdog exists on any provider path. There is no abort-and-retry on stream silence and no on/off knob for one. The only 'watchdog' in the agent layer is the stdio-death watchdog for the Pi subprocess (pi-agent.ts:6053), which fires on process death, not on a silent stream; the compact RPC has an unrelated 300s timeout.
findings.evidence: grep -ra -F over packages/ apps/ (node_modules excluded) for STREAM_WATCHDOG / streamWatchdog / idleWatchdog returns 0 hits; nearest neighbour is packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6053

findings.claim: A transient server rate-limit error that is not the account usage limit must be retried automatically with backoff rather than ending the turn.
findings.quote: Transient server rate-limit errors unrelated to your usage limit are now retried automatically with backoff for subscribers instead of failing the turn
findings.ourState: Both backends classify a rate limit and surface it to the user instead of retrying. claude-agent.ts carries the explicit comment 'Rate limit errors - don't retry immediately, surface to user' and then yields typed_error + complete; pi-agent.ts returns a `rate_limited` diagnostic with a manual 'Retry' action and retryDelayMs 5000. No backoff loop, and no distinction between a transient server 429 and the account usage limit. (Backoff retry does exist elsewhere — MCP connect, webhooks, session mirror — so the absence is specific to the model turn.)

findings.claim: The built-in Explore agent resolves its model from the main session (clamped to Opus) rather than running on a fixed small model.
findings.quote: The built-in Explore agent now inherits the main session's model (capped at Opus) instead of running on Haiku
findings.ourState: There is no built-in Explore agent. BUILTIN_AGENT_DEFINITIONS is scout/planner/worker/reviewer, each pinned to a `tier` ('small'/'medium'/'big') that resolves the child model; 'explore' exists here only as a permission-mode name, not an agent. So the inherit-from-session-capped-at-Opus rule has no counterpart on the read-only exploration agent (`scout`, tier 'small').

findings.claim: Multiple leading skill invocations in one message all load, bounded at five.
findings.quote: Stacked skill invocations like /skill-a /skill-b do XYZ now load all leading skills (up to 5), not only the first
findings.ourState: Skill invocation is marker-based (`[skill:name]`), and every occurrence in the message is collected in text order with no cap — parseSkillMentionOccurrences returns all matches and resolveSkillReferences maps every one. A skill-derived slash command expands to that same marker, so stacking works, but the documented ceiling of 5 is not enforced anywhere (we are more permissive, not less).

findings.claim: A `/dataviz` skill ships in the bundled skill set.
findings.quote: New /dataviz skill gives chart and dashboard design guidance, with a runnable color-palette validator
findings.ourState: The bundled skill directory contains exactly two skills, plugin-creator and skill-creator. No dataviz skill and no colour-palette validator anywhere in the tree.
findings.evidence: ls apps/electron/resources/skills → plugin-creator, skill-creator; grep -ra -F dataviz over packages/ apps/ (node_modules excluded) → 0 hits

pages.summary: Week-28 digest. EnterWorktree's outside-the-namespace confirmation and the 'no human input has occurred' wording in background-task notifications are both present. The /doctor tier change and both auto-mode hardening items are not.

findings.claim: `/doctor` is a fix-capable setup checkup (installation health, unused skills/MCP/plugins against context cost, CLAUDE.md dedup and trim, slow hooks) that proposes changes and asks for confirmation, and it answers to `/checkup` as well.
findings.quote: /doctor now diagnoses issues and can fix them, instead of printing a read-only report. It checks installation health, finds unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost, deduplicates local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones, proposes trimming CLAUDE.md content Claude could derive from the codebase, and flags slow hooks. It reports findings first and asks for confirmation before changing anything. /checkup is its alias.
findings.ourState: `doctor` is a CLI subcommand only (`nessy-general-agent doctor`), explicitly read-only — it renders a settings/managed-policy/agent-definition report and an exit code, with no fix flow and no confirmation step. There is no `checkup` alias (the word appears only in prose), no in-session `/doctor` slash command in the composer's command set, and none of the unused-extension, CLAUDE.md-dedup/trim or slow-hook checks. The narrowed scope is a recorded decision in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-doctor-surface.md (status: closed), which predates this tier change.
findings.evidence: apps/cli/src/doctor.ts:2 ('the read-only configuration checkup'), apps/cli/src/index.ts:2149, packages/shared/src/config/config-doctor.ts:21-32; grep -ra -F checkup finds no command registration

findings.claim: Auto mode must block writes that tamper with session transcript files.
findings.quote: Auto mode now blocks tampering with session transcript files, and asks before running rm -rf on a variable it can't resolve from context
findings.ourState: No rule anywhere names session transcript files as a protected target. Transcripts live at <configDir>/sessions/<ws>/<id>/session.jsonl, and the sandbox deny list deliberately excludes that directory because it doubles as the supervised process's scratch/TMPDIR root — so a Bash write there is unguarded. The file-tool protected-path floor does fire on the `.nessy-agent` segment, but in auto mode its outcome is 'routed to the classifier', and the guardian prompt carries no transcript-tampering instruction.
findings.evidence: packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation/self-config-deny.ts:31-34 ('The whole config dir. SESSIONS_DIR … is <configDir>/sessions' — listed under 'NOT here, deliberately'); packages/shared/src/prompts/guardian.ts (no transcript rule; lines 128-130 mention the transcript only as untrusted evidence)

findings.claim: An `rm -rf` whose target is a variable the model cannot resolve from context must prompt.
findings.quote: Auto mode now blocks tampering with session transcript files, and asks before running rm -rf on a variable it can't resolve from context
findings.ourState: The removal circuit breaker deliberately does the opposite: an unresolvable removal target does not fire. The module states 'rm -rf "$(cat targets.txt)" has an unresolvable target and does not fire', and its 'Known limits' section confirms `${HOME:?}`, `$(echo ~)` and `rm -rf *` are not detected — every limit 'fail[s] toward NOT prompting'. The guardian prompt's rm -rf guidance (lines 150, 177) is about inspecting a specific local path, not about an unresolved variable.

findings.claim: `/cd` offers directory-path completion, and `/commit-push-pr` auto-allows `git push` to the repo's configured push remote as well as `origin`.
findings.quote: /cd now suggests directory paths as you type, matching /add-dir
findings.ourState: Neither command exists. The composer's command set is the permission modes plus agents, automations, compact, context, create-skill, create-plugin, export, init, clear, help, memory, model, subtask, usage — no `/cd`, no `/add-dir`, no `/commit-push-pr`.

pages.summary: Week-29 digest, and the densest binding page of the four. The `/fork`→`/subtask` rename and the MCP two-minute auto-background threshold are both already correct here, as is the repository-root persistence of 'always allow' rules. Six settings/env/flag surfaces named on this page have no reader in our source at all, including both session-wide runaway-loop caps.

findings.claim: Subagent spawns are capped per session at a default of 200, tunable by env var.
findings.quote: Session-wide caps stop runaway loops: WebSearch calls and subagent spawns each default to 200, tunable with CLAUDE\_CODE\_MAX\_WEB\_SEARCHES\_PER\_SESSION and CLAUDE\_CODE\_MAX\_SUBAGENTS\_PER\_SESSION
findings.ourState: The spawner enforces only a DEPTH limit (DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1, error 'Subagent depth limit exceeded'). There is no per-session spawn COUNT budget and no concurrency limit — a depth-1 loop can spawn unboundedly. Neither MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION nor MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS has a reader.
findings.evidence: packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:110 and :518-519; grep -ra -F for MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION / MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS over packages/ apps/ → 0 source hits

findings.claim: WebSearch calls are capped per session at a default of 200, tunable by env var.
findings.quote: Session-wide caps stop runaway loops: WebSearch calls and subagent spawns each default to 200, tunable with CLAUDE\_CODE\_MAX\_WEB\_SEARCHES\_PER\_SESSION and CLAUDE\_CODE\_MAX\_SUBAGENTS\_PER\_SESSION
findings.ourState: We do ship a `web_search` tool (DDG-backed with a fallback provider), and it has no per-session call budget of any kind. The cap and its env var have no reader.
findings.evidence: packages/pi-agent-server/src/tools/search/create-search-tool.ts:61; grep -ra -F MAX_WEB_SEARCHES over packages/ apps/ → 0 hits

findings.claim: Administrators disable auto mode with a `disableAutoMode` setting.
findings.quote: Auto mode no longer needs the CLAUDE\_CODE\_ENABLE\_AUTO\_MODE opt-in on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry; administrators can turn it off with disableAutoMode
findings.ourState: The managed-policy reader has no `disableAutoMode` key. Auto mode can only be removed by omitting it from `cyclablePermissionModes` or by the disabled-permission-mode list — there is no key of that name an administrator can set. The five `disableAutoMode` hits in the repo are all inside vendored/built bundles (pi-agent-server/dist, electron resources), not our source.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:405-420 (policy interface) and :662 (disabledPermissionModeList); grep -ra -F -l disableAutoMode lists only dist/resource bundles

findings.claim: A `processWrapper` setting / `CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER` env var forces every process the binary spawns (background service, agent-view sessions) through a required wrapper executable.
findings.quote: New corporate launcher support: CLAUDE\_CODE\_PROCESS\_WRAPPER or the processWrapper setting runs the processes Claude Code starts from its own binary, such as the background service and agent view sessions, through a required wrapper executable
findings.ourState: No reader for either name. Our own process spawns — the Pi subprocess supervisor, the session MCP server, background agent sessions — launch their executables directly with no wrapper indirection and no setting to require one. This is the exact surface a corporate deployment (which is what this fork is) would need.
findings.evidence: grep -ra -F for PROCESS_WRAPPER / processWrapper over packages/ apps/ (node_modules excluded) → 0 hits; spawn sites in packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts take the binary path unwrapped

findings.claim: Screen-reader mode is reachable three ways: a CLI flag, a `CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER` env var, and an `axScreenReader` setting.
findings.quote: Turn it on per session with a flag, per shell with the CLAUDE\_AX\_SCREEN\_READER environment variable, or everywhere with the axScreenReader setting.
findings.ourState: None of the three exists. Our CLI does render in-place spinner frames on a TTY (the exact 'spinners and in-place redraws' the mode is meant to replace) and exposes only `--no-spinner`/`--disable-spinner`, which suppresses the animation but does not switch to labelled linear output. No `axScreenReader` settings key, no env var, no flag.
findings.evidence: apps/cli/src/index.ts:266-275 (spinner) and :116-118 (--no-spinner); grep -ra -F for axScreenReader / AX_SCREEN_READER → 0 hits

findings.claim: A flag and env var include subagent text and thinking blocks in stream-json output.
findings.quote: `--forward-subagent-text` and CLAUDE\_CODE\_FORWARD\_SUBAGENT\_TEXT include subagent text and thinking blocks in stream-json output
findings.ourState: We ship stream-json output (`--output-format stream-json` in the CLI) but no way to include subagent text or thinking blocks in it. Neither the flag nor the env var has a reader.
findings.evidence: apps/cli/src/index.ts (streamJson output format); grep -ra -F for forward-subagent-text / FORWARD_SUBAGENT_TEXT over packages/ apps/ → 0 hits

findings.claim: `claude auto-mode reset` restores the default auto-mode configuration, with `--yes` to skip confirmation.
findings.quote: New claude auto-mode reset restores the default auto-mode configuration, and `--yes` skips the confirmation prompt
findings.ourState: No `auto-mode` CLI subcommand and no reset path for auto-mode configuration. The CLI's subcommand set does not include it.
findings.evidence: grep -ra -F 'auto-mode reset' over packages/ apps/ → 0 hits; apps/cli/src/index.ts command dispatch has no auto-mode branch

findings.claim: `/fork` now means 'copy this conversation into a new background session with its own agent-view row', distinct from the in-session forked subagent, which is `/subtask`.
findings.quote: /fork now copies your conversation into a new background session with its own row in claude agents while you keep working; the in-session forked subagent it used to launch is now /subtask
findings.ourState: The rename half is correct — `/subtask` is registered and `/fork` is deliberately NOT registered for the fork engine, with the reasoning recorded in the module (registering it would ship the opposite command). The new `/fork` feature itself (whole-session copy into a separate background session with its own budget) is not implemented; the module records this as a known absence.
findings.evidence: packages/shared/src/slash-commands/subtask.ts:16 ('`/fork` copies the whole session into a separate background session, which we do not have') and :23-25

pages.summary: The digest index: a one-paragraph summary per week from W13 to W29 plus the weekly-digest framing. Its W27–W29 claims are covered by the three pages above. Reading the older weeks' summaries turned up three implementation-binding statements about surfaces we ship — the fallbackModel arity, the `claude mcp login`/`logout` pair, and plugin loading from .zip/URL — that diverge; the rest (Tool(param:value) parameter rules, conditional `if` hooks, the Monitor tool, `--safe-mode`, `worktree.baseRef`, `$CLAUDE_EFFORT`, sub-agent spawn depth default 1) all check out against our code.

findings.claim: `fallbackModel` holds an ordered list of up to three models tried in sequence.
findings.quote: **`--safe-mode`** starts Claude Code with all customizations disabled for troubleshooting; and **`fallbackModel`** configures up to three fallback models tried in order.
findings.ourState: `fallbackModel` is a single string in both the schema and the defaults, documented as 'Pi model ID to retry once after model/network drain errors. Empty disables fallback.' — one model, one retry, no ordered list. The Zod schema is `fallbackModel: z.string()` and the normalizer coerces anything non-string to ''.

findings.claim: A configured MCP server can be authenticated and de-authenticated from the shell, outside the interactive menu.
findings.quote: **`claude mcp login`**: authenticate a configured MCP server from your shell instead of the interactive `/mcp` menu, and clear its stored credentials later with `claude mcp logout`.
findings.ourState: The CLI has no `mcp` subcommand at all, so neither `login` nor `logout` exists. MCP OAuth is reachable only through the app's interactive surfaces; there is no shell path to authenticate a server or to clear its stored credentials.
findings.evidence: apps/cli/src/index.ts command dispatch (doctor / plugin validate|list|details / run / help / version — no mcp branch); grep -ra -F 'mcp login' over packages/ apps/ → 0 hits

findings.claim: Plugins load for the current session from a local `.zip` archive via `--plugin-dir` and from a remote archive via `--plugin-url`.
findings.quote: **Plugins load from `.zip` archives and URLs**: `--plugin-dir` now accepts `.zip` files, and `--plugin-url` fetches a plugin archive for the current session.
findings.ourState: Neither flag has a reader in our source. Plugin installation goes through the marketplace/install service (which does handle .zip and .mcpb archives internally), but there is no session-scoped side-load of a plugin from a local archive path or a URL. The only `plugin-dir` hits in the tree are inside vendored bundles and the Codex binaries.
findings.evidence: grep -ra -F -l 'plugin-dir' over packages/ apps/ → only dist/vendor bundles; grep -ra -F 'plugin-url'/'pluginUrl' → 0 hits; apps/cli/src/index.ts exposes only `plugin validate|list|details`

flagged.quote: | `DirectoryAdded`                                       | No         | Yes            | A working directory is added during a session                                                                                          | Install dependencies for a repository added mid-session                                                     |
flagged.ourState: `DirectoryAdded` does not exist anywhere in the repo (`grep -ran DirectoryAdded packages apps docs scripts` → 0). `PluginHookEventName` enumerates 30 names and its own doc comment accounts for exactly two documented events as deliberate deferrals (`MessageDisplay`, `TeammateIdle`) — DirectoryAdded is unaccounted for. The surface it would fire on does exist: we ship session-scoped `addDirectories` grants (`pi-agent.ts:3189`).
flagged.evidence: packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-runtime.ts:25 (union), :156 (PLUGIN_HOOK_EVENTS list); grep -ran "DirectoryAdded" packages apps docs scripts → 0 hits

flagged.claim: Setup hooks receive a `trigger` field whose value is `init` or `maintenance`.
flagged.quote: In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), Setup hooks receive a `trigger` field set to either `"init"` or `"maintenance"`:
flagged.ourState: Our Setup emission carries `source: 'pi-runtime'` and no `trigger` at all, and it fires on every Pi session start rather than only under `--init-only` / `-p --init` / `-p --maintenance`.

flagged.claim: FileChanged input carries `file_path` (absolute path) and `event` (`change` | `add` | `unlink`).
flagged.quote: In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), FileChanged hooks receive `file_path` and `event`.
flagged.ourState: We emit `path` (only when a path was captured) and `change_kind` set to the mutating TOOL NAME, never `file_path` or `event`. The stdin payload is the event input verbatim (`hookCommandStdinPayload` spreads `...input`), so a hook doing `jq -r .file_path` reads null.

flagged.claim: CwdChanged input carries `old_cwd` and `new_cwd`.
flagged.quote: In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), CwdChanged hooks receive `old_cwd` and `new_cwd`.
flagged.ourState: We emit `cwd` and `previous_cwd`. Neither documented key is produced anywhere (`grep -ran 'old_cwd\|new_cwd' packages apps` → 0 outside docs).

flagged.claim: StopFailure input carries `error`, and that field is what the matcher filters on.
flagged.quote: In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), StopFailure hooks receive `error`, optional `error_details`, and optional `last_assistant_message`. The `error` field identifies the error type and is used for matcher filtering.
flagged.ourState: We emit `error_code` only. The MATCHER path was fixed (`getMatchValueForSdkInput` reads `input.error_code ?? input.error` and maps it through `STOP_FAILURE_DOCUMENTED_ERROR`), but the payload a hook reads on stdin still has no `error` key, and `error_details` / `last_assistant_message` have no producer.

flagged.claim: ConfigChange input carries `source` (the configuration type that changed) and optionally `file_path`.
flagged.quote: In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), ConfigChange hooks receive `source` and optionally `file_path`. The `source` field indicates which configuration type changed, and `file_path` provides the path to the specific file that was modified.
flagged.ourState: We emit `config_keys` and `config_digest`; neither `source` nor `file_path` is produced, so the documented matcher vocabulary (`user_settings`, `project_settings`, `local_settings`, `policy_settings`, `skills`) can never match — `getMatchValueForSdkInput` deliberately leaves ConfigChange unmatched for that reason.

flagged.claim: UserPromptExpansion input carries `expansion_type`, `command_name`, `command_args`, `command_source` and the original `prompt`, and the matcher filters on `command_name`.
flagged.quote: In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), UserPromptExpansion hooks receive `expansion_type`, `command_name`, `command_args`, `command_source`, and the original `prompt` string.
flagged.ourState: Our UserPromptExpansion emission carries only `source: 'pi-before-agent-start'`, `lifecycle_version` and `correlation_id`, and fires once per turn rather than per command expansion. None of the five documented fields has a producer (`grep -ran expansion_type packages apps` → 0).

flagged.claim: PreCompact input carries `custom_instructions`; PostCompact input carries `compact_summary`.
flagged.quote: In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), PostCompact hooks receive `trigger` and `compact_summary`. The `compact_summary` field contains the conversation summary generated by the compact operation.
flagged.ourState: Both emissions carry `trigger` and a Nessy `source` only. `compact_summary` and `custom_instructions` have no producer anywhere in the repo.

flagged.claim: `prompt_id` is a common input field on every hook event, correlating hook output with OpenTelemetry `prompt.id`.
flagged.quote: | `prompt_id`       | UUID identifying the user prompt currently being processed.
flagged.ourState: `SdkAutomationInput` has no `prompt_id` field and no emitter sets one (`grep -ran 'prompt_id\|promptId' packages apps --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` → 0).

flagged.claim: `effort` is a common input field (an object with a `level` field) on tool-context events, and the same value reaches hook commands as `$CLAUDE_EFFORT`.

flagged.claim: The 8-consecutive-block Stop cap can be raised with an environment variable.
flagged.quote: If your hook legitimately needs more than eight iterations to converge, raise the cap with [`CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP`](/docs/en/env-vars).
flagged.ourState: The cap is a hardcoded module constant with no environment override in any spelling (`grep -ran 'STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP' packages apps` → 0): `const MAX_CONSECUTIVE_HOOK_BLOCKS = 8;`.

flagged.claim: In plan mode, a protected-path write is allowed when bypass permissions are available for the session, and routed to the classifier when auto mode is available during planning — not simply prompted.
flagged.quote: | `plan`                   | Prompted. {/* min-version: 2.1.217 */}In sessions with [bypass permissions](#skip-all-checks-with-bypasspermissions-mode) available, allowed. {/* min-version: 2.1.218 */}Otherwise, with [auto mode](#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode) available during planning, routed to the classifier |
flagged.ourState: `protectedPathOutcome` is a three-branch total function keyed on mode alone: `bypassPermissions` → allow, `dontAsk` → deny, everything else → prompt. It has no notion of "bypass available" or of auto-during-plan, and the file's own quoted copy of the table predates both rows. (The `auto` row's classifier routing is a separately recorded deliberate deviation documented in the same file.)

flagged.claim: `Bash(*)` is equivalent to a bare `Bash`, and as a deny rule BOTH forms remove the tool from Claude's context.
flagged.quote: `Bash(*)` is equivalent to `Bash` and matches all Bash commands. As a deny rule, both forms remove the tool from Claude's context.
flagged.ourState: `Bash(*)` parses to `{ kind: 'bash', pattern: '*' }` — a pattern matcher, not a tool matcher. Context removal is decided by `isWholeCapabilityDeniedByPermissionDsl`, which only inspects `rule.matcher.kind === 'tool'`, so a `deny: ["Bash(*)"]` leaves the Bash tool definition in the model's context and denies every call it makes instead of hiding the tool. Same for `PowerShell(*)`.

flagged.claim: `Skill(<name pattern>)` is a supported rule format that matches by skill name.
flagged.quote: | `Skill(deploy *)`              | Skill                     | [Skill name matching](/docs/en/skills#restrict-claude’s-skill-access) |
flagged.ourState: `parseClaudeRuleString` has no `Skill` case; `Skill(deploy *)` contains no `param:` colon, so it falls through to the `default:` branch and returns an inert warning ("uses a specifier form no permission check matches; the rule is ignored"). There is no `skill` matcher kind in `CompiledMatcher`, so an imported Claude `deny: ["Skill(deploy *)"]` silently grants the skill.

flagged.claim: `blockedMarketplaces` is a managed-only setting: a blocklist of marketplace sources checked before download.
flagged.quote: | `blockedMarketplaces`                          | Blocklist of marketplace sources. Blocked sources are checked before downloading, so they never touch the filesystem.
flagged.ourState: No reader (`grep -ran blockedMarketplaces packages apps` → 0). `ManagedPiPolicyV1` implements the sibling keys `strictKnownMarketplaces` and `extraKnownMarketplaces` but has no denylist field, so an admin can pin an allowlist but cannot block a single source.
flagged.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:141,158 (the two marketplace fields that do exist)

flagged.claim: `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` is a managed-only setting that blocks skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers from user and project sources; it accepts `true` or an array naming a subset.
flagged.quote: | `strictPluginOnlyCustomization`                | Block skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources, so they can only come from plugins or managed settings. `true` locks all four surfaces; an array such as `["skills", "hooks"]` locks only the named ones.
flagged.ourState: No reader (`grep -ran strictPluginOnlyCustomization packages apps` → 0). We implement the per-surface locks `allowManagedHooksOnly`, `allowManagedMcpServersOnly` and `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`, but nothing locks user/project SKILLS or AGENTS to plugin-or-managed origin.

flagged.claim: With sandboxing enabled, `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` defaults to `true` and makes sandboxed Bash commands run without prompting even against a bare `Bash` ask rule.
flagged.quote: When you enable sandboxing and leave `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` at its default of `true`, sandboxed Bash commands run without prompting even if your permissions include a bare `Bash` ask rule, or the [equivalent `Bash(*)` form](#match-all-uses-of-a-tool): the sandbox boundary substitutes for that whole-tool prompt.
flagged.ourState: The key has no reader (`grep -ran autoAllowBashIfSandboxed packages apps` → 0) and does not appear in our sandbox settings schema, which carries only `excludedCommands`, the four filesystem root lists and the two domain lists.

flagged.claim: `disableSideloadFlags` and `pluginTrustMessage` are managed-only settings governing CLI sideload flags and the plugin trust warning.
flagged.quote: | `pluginTrustMessage`                           | Custom message appended to the plugin trust warning shown before installation
flagged.ourState: Neither key has a reader (`grep -ran 'disableSideloadFlags\|pluginTrustMessage' packages apps` → 0), and neither appears in `ManagedPiPolicyV1`. We do ship plugin install with a trust step and marketplace pinning, so both bind a surface we have.

flagged.claim: A tool result's `content` array may carry `resource` and `resource_link` blocks in addition to text/image/audio, and the runtime converts a resource link into a text block naming the link.
flagged.quote: The `content` array in a tool result accepts `text`, `image`, `audio`, `resource`, and `resource_link` blocks. You can mix them in the same response.
flagged.ourState: The MCP proxy's result reducer handles exactly `text`, `image` and `audio`. A `resource` block's payload (`resource.text` / `resource.blob`, the actual content) and a `resource_link` block are both skipped by the loop, so in any result that also contains a text block the resource content is silently lost — the `JSON.stringify(result)` fallback only fires when zero parts were extracted.

flagged.claim: The canonical tool name is `TaskStop`; permission rules and hook matchers match the canonical name only, and the transcript label `Stop Task` does not match.
flagged.quote: For example, the tool labeled `Stop Task` in the transcript has the canonical name `TaskStop`. Permission rules and [hook matchers](/docs/en/hooks) match the canonical name only, so a rule written as `Stop Task` doesn't match.
flagged.ourState: The binding spells it `stopTask` on every permission-visible axis — `binding('stop_task', 'stop_task', 'stopTask', 'stopTask')` gives semanticId `stop_task`, permissionName/bindingName `stopTask`. `PERMISSION_RULE_TOOL_NAMES` is derived from permissionName+descriptorId, so `TaskStop` is not a known tool: an imported `deny: ["TaskStop"]` matches nothing AND raises the unknown-tool typo warning. A `taskstop` alias exists only for SUBAGENT tool lists (`runtime-agent-definition.ts:95`), not for permission rules or hook matchers.

flagged.claim: The sandbox write/deny path keys are nested under `sandbox.filesystem` and named `allowWrite`, `denyWrite`, `denyRead`, `allowRead`.
flagged.quote: Paths in `filesystem.allowWrite`, `filesystem.denyWrite`, `filesystem.denyRead`, `filesystem.allowRead`, and `credentials.files` support these prefixes:

flagged.quote: To point Claude Code at your proxy, set the proxy ports in [sandbox settings](/docs/en/settings#sandbox-settings):

flagged.claim: `allowAppleEvents`, `enableWeakerNetworkIsolation`, `enableWeakerNestedSandbox`, `network.allowUnixSockets`, `network.allowAllUnixSockets`, `network.allowLocalBinding` and `network.allowMachLookup` are sandbox settings.

flagged.claim: `"streamable-http"` is accepted as an alias for `"http"` in `.mcp.json` and other JSON config files.
flagged.quote: In `.mcp.json` and other JSON config files, `"streamable-http"` is accepted as an alias for `"http"`.
flagged.ourState: `parseProjectMcpServer` branches on `type === 'http' || type === 'sse'`, then `'ws'`, then `undefined|'stdio'`, and returns `null` for anything else — the caller logs `Ignoring .mcp.json server "<name>": unsupported MCP server config` and drops it. The Claude plugin adapter has the same closed set. The alias exists only inside the vendored Pi/session-MCP bundles under `apps/electron/dist`, never in our own parser.

flagged.claim: MCP tool results larger than 25,000 tokens are persisted to disk, and the limit is raised with `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS`.
flagged.quote: When a tool result is larger than 25,000 tokens, the full output is saved to a file and the tool result is replaced with an error message that names the file path, so the agent can read the output back in portions.
