flagged.claim: A `managed-mcp.json` file at a system path takes exclusive control: only its servers load, and `claude mcp add` is refused.
flagged.quote: If you deploy a `managed-mcp.json` file, Claude Code loads only the servers that file defines. Users cannot add, modify, or use any other MCP servers, including plugin-provided servers.
flagged.ourState: No reader for the file at any of the three documented system paths (grep -a for `managed-mcp.json` hits docs and comments only). There is no exclusive-control mode and therefore no way to express the documented "disable MCP entirely" pattern — `deniedMcpServers` blocks only what it names. Recorded in docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:91.

flagged.claim: Claude Code answers `roots/list` with the launch directory plus every additional working directory, and sends `notifications/roots/list_changed` when that set changes.
flagged.quote: Claude Code answers `roots/list` with the session's launch directory plus every [additional working directory](/docs/en/permissions#working-directories) you've granted with `--add-dir`, `/add-dir`, or the `additionalDirectories` setting.
flagged.ourState: The MCP client is constructed with `capabilities: options?.elicitationHandler ? { elicitation: { form: {}, url: {} } } : {}` — the `roots` capability is never advertised, so `roots/list` is never requested and no `list_changed` roots notification is emitted. A server that scopes its own filesystem access via roots gets nothing. Confirmed absent repo-wide with `grep -a`.

flagged.claim: `"streamable-http"` is a valid value of the `type` field wherever MCP servers are configured in JSON.
flagged.quote: When configuring MCP servers via JSON in `.mcp.json`, `~/.claude.json`, or `claude mcp add-json`, the `type` field accepts `streamable-http` as an alias for `http`.
flagged.ourState: Our `.mcp.json` parser and the Claude plugin adapter both accept only `stdio|http|sse|ws`; an entry copied verbatim from an MCP server's own documentation is dropped with `unsupported MCP server config`.

flagged.claim: `headersHelper` runs a command at connection time whose stdout JSON is merged into the connection headers, with `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME`/`CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL`/`CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` in its environment and a 10-second timeout.
flagged.quote: If your MCP server uses an authentication scheme other than OAuth, such as Kerberos, short-lived tokens, or an internal SSO, use `headersHelper` to generate request headers at connection time.
flagged.ourState: Not implemented for any transport. Both readers detect the field and emit a warning (`"headersHelper" is not implemented for any transport; it was ignored`) and a deferred-capability record; the server still connects with static headers only.

flagged.claim: Project-scoped `.mcp.json` servers require per-server approval before use, resettable with `claude mcp reset-project-choices`.
flagged.quote: For security reasons, Claude Code prompts for approval before using project-scoped servers from `.mcp.json` files.
flagged.ourState: The only gate is whole-workspace trust; inside a trusted project every `.mcp.json` server is materialized without an individual approve/reject step, and none of `enabledMcpjsonServers`, `disabledMcpjsonServers`, `enableAllProjectMcpServers` or a reset command exists.

flagged.claim: The MCP server startup timeout is 30 seconds by default and is raised with the `MCP_TIMEOUT` environment variable in milliseconds.
flagged.quote: The server took longer than the default 30-second startup timeout. A stdio server's first run can be slow while `npx` downloads the package. Increase the limit with the [`MCP_TIMEOUT`](/docs/en/env-vars) environment variable, in milliseconds:
flagged.ourState: The 30 s default matches (`MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`), but it is a compile-time constant overridable only through a programmatic `connectTimeoutMs` option — there is no `MCP_TIMEOUT` (or Nessy-prefixed) env reader, so an operator cannot raise it.

flagged.claim: A project-scoped server awaiting approval is reported as pending, and a rejected one is attributed to `disabledMcpjsonServers`.
flagged.quote: `claude mcp get <name>` shows rejected servers as `✘ Rejected (see disabledMcpjsonServers in settings)`.
flagged.ourState: No pending/rejected state exists for project MCP servers; workspace trust is the whole gate and `disabledMcpjsonServers` has no reader. Same root cause as the mcp.md finding.

flagged.claim: Marketplaces and their installed plugins auto-update in the background after startup, on by default for official Anthropic marketplaces and off by default for third-party and local ones.
flagged.quote: Official Anthropic marketplaces have auto-update enabled by default. Third-party and local development marketplaces have auto-update disabled by default.
flagged.ourState: No background marketplace or plugin update path exists — `grep -a` for `pluginAutoUpdate|autoUpdatePlugins|backgroundPluginUpdate|updateMarketplaces|refreshMarketplace` across `packages/` and `apps/` returns nothing, and the only `autoUpdate` hits are the Electron app updater. `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` and `FORCE_AUTOUPDATE_PLUGINS` are likewise unread. Consequently the per-entry default the doc specifies is unobservable.
flagged.evidence: packages/shared/src/plugins/store-v2.ts:154 (update journal exists; nothing schedules against it)

flagged.claim: `pluginSuggestionMarketplaces` is a managed allowlist gating whether a plugin's marketplace-entry `relevance` block can surface as a contextual install suggestion.
flagged.quote: When your administrator has allowlisted the marketplace via the [`pluginSuggestionMarketplaces`](/docs/en/settings#available-settings) managed setting, plugins marked as relevant to your current working directory are pinned at the top with a **suggested for this directory** label.
flagged.ourState: Neither the setting nor a contextual-suggestion surface exists; the `relevance` field is dropped at catalog parse. Recorded as a deliberate deferral in the deviation register (line 183).

flagged.claim: Installing a plugin that declares dependencies resolves and installs them automatically, fetching each at the highest `{plugin-name}--v{version}` git tag that satisfies the range.
flagged.quote: When you install a plugin that declares dependencies, Claude Code resolves and installs them automatically and lists which dependencies were added at the end of the install output.
flagged.ourState: No auto-install and no tag enumeration. The module header records the reason: no marketplace source in this repo enumerates git tags, so resolving a range against "whatever the catalog currently holds" would make `~2.1.0` silently mean latest. A declared dependency that is not already installed surfaces as `dependency-unsatisfied` and disables the dependent plugin.

flagged.claim: A cross-marketplace dependency is refused unless the root marketplace lists the target in `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn`.
flagged.quote: To allow it, the maintainer of the root marketplace adds the target marketplace name to `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn` in `marketplace.json`.
flagged.ourState: The field is not carried past catalog parse and no `cross-marketplace` error exists; the adapter comment records that with nothing auto-installed there is no install to refuse, and the `marketplace` field on each dependency is carried so the check has its input the day auto-install lands.

flagged.claim: Every subprocess the Bash/PowerShell tool and hook commands spawn carries an environment marker announcing that it is running inside the coding agent; third-party CLIs gate behaviour on it.
flagged.quote: Claude Code sets the [`CLAUDECODE`](/docs/en/env-vars) environment variable to `1` for every command it runs through the Bash and PowerShell tools, and for [hook](/docs/en/hooks) commands.
flagged.ourState: Nessy sets no equivalent marker in tool subprocesses. The only `CLAUDECODE` references in the repo REMOVE it from a child env (`apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:62` strips it to dodge the Claude SDK nesting guard) and there is no `NESSYCODE`/`NESSY_CODE` replacement anywhere. This is not the ordinary brand-prefix rename: the variable is read by third-party tools, not by us, so no NESSY_-prefixed name substitutes for it, and CLIs that adapt their output for agent use (non-interactive mode, no colour, machine-readable output) do not adapt for Nessy.

flagged.claim: A marketplace plugin entry may carry `category`, `tags`, `relevance` (marketplace-specific) plus any manifest field including `license`, `keywords`, `repository`.
flagged.quote: You can include any field from the [plugin manifest schema](/docs/en/plugins-reference#plugin-manifest-schema), such as `description`, `version`, `author`, `commands`, and `hooks`, plus these marketplace-specific fields: `source`, `category`, `tags`, `strict`, and `relevance`.
flagged.ourState: `MARKETPLACE_ENTRY_CARRIED_FIELDS` carries only the path fields plus `displayName`, `description`, `version`, `author`, `homepage`, `defaultEnabled`, `dependencies`. `category`, `tags`, `relevance`, `license`, `keywords` and `repository` are dropped at catalog parse and never reach the adapter — grep for `'category'`/`'tags'`/`'license'`/`'keywords'` in that file returns zero. `category` and `tags` are the documented organisation/search axes, so a marketplace that categorises its plugins loses that in our Discover list.

flagged.claim: A pre-populated, read-only plugins directory can be pointed at with an environment variable so container/CI images start with marketplaces and plugin caches already present, with a second variable to install directly into that path at build time.
flagged.quote: Set the `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR` environment variable to point at this directory.
flagged.ourState: No seed-directory concept exists. `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR`, `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR`, `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_KEEP_MARKETPLACE_ON_FAILURE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS` and `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_PREFER_HTTPS` all return zero hits under `--include='*.ts'` repo-wide, and there is no NESSY_-prefixed equivalent for any of them. The offline/airgap escape hatch the page recommends (`KEEP_MARKETPLACE_ON_FAILURE`) therefore has no counterpart, which matters for a corporate-network fork.

flagged.claim: A plugin may ship a `settings.json` at its root whose `agent` key activates one of the plugin's own subagents as the main thread, and whose values outrank a `settings` block in `plugin.json`.
flagged.quote: Plugins can include a `settings.json` file at the plugin root to apply default configuration when the plugin is enabled. Currently, only the `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` keys are supported.
flagged.ourState: The file is detected and recorded as a deferral only — `CLAUDE_RETAINED_SURFACE_FIELDS` carries `{ externalKind: 'settings', field: 'settings', defaultPath: 'settings.json' }`, which pushes a `plugin.deferred.claude_settings` row and nothing else. Neither key is read anywhere: `grep -ran "subagentStatusLine" --include='*.ts' .` returns zero hits repo-wide. A plugin whose whole purpose is to change the main thread's agent installs and silently does nothing.

flagged.claim: A folder under a skills directory containing `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` loads as a plugin named `<name>@skills-dir` with no marketplace and no install step, discovered in place rather than copied into the cache.
flagged.quote: Any folder under a skills directory that contains a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` manifest is loaded as a plugin named `<name>@skills-dir` on the next session, with no marketplace and no install step.
flagged.ourState: Not implemented. `grep -ran "skills-dir"` over the repo hits only plan/spec prose — including `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:197` which itself records "skills-dir plugins undetected (B1, still not started)". Skill discovery walks `.claude/skills` at project and ancestor depth (`native-sources.ts` line ~1065, tagged `d${depth}`) but never checks a skill folder for a plugin manifest, so a bundle laid out this way contributes its SKILL.md and silently drops its agents, hooks and MCP servers.

flagged.claim: Eight optional LSP fields govern server lifecycle and diagnostics injection, two of them with defaults (`restartOnCrash` defaults to `true`, `diagnostics` defaults to `true`).
flagged.quote: `restartOnCrash`        | Whether to restart the server after it crashes. Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to leave a crashed server stopped instead of restarting it
flagged.ourState: All eight are parsed as declared-but-unread: `CLAUDE_UNREAD_LSP_FIELDS` lists `transport`, `initializationOptions`, `settings`, `startupTimeout`, `shutdownTimeout`, `restartOnCrash`, `maxRestarts`, `diagnostics`, and the reader emits a `plugin.format.claude_lsp_fields_unread` warning naming them. The capability that reaches the runtime carries only `command`, `args`, `languages`, `env`, `workspaceFolder`. An author who sets `diagnostics: false` to suppress automatic diagnostic injection, or `restartOnCrash: false` on a server that crash-loops, gets neither.

flagged.claim: `userConfig` values are substituted as `${user_config.KEY}` into MCP and LSP server configs and (for non-sensitive values) into skill and agent content.
flagged.quote: Each value is available for substitution as `${user_config.KEY}` in MCP and LSP server configs and hook commands.
flagged.ourState: The option schema, the sensitivity split, the storage-source restriction and the `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY>` export are all built; the `${user_config.*}` substitution into MCP/LSP configs and skill/agent content is not, and the surface carries its own deferral row `plugin.deferred.claude_user_config_substitution`. A plugin whose MCP server config references `${user_config.api_endpoint}` therefore starts with the literal placeholder.

flagged.claim: Omitting the `skills` option enables every discovered user and project skill from the filesystem locations `settingSources` names; passing a list or `[]` is the only way to narrow it.
flagged.quote: When omitted, discovered Skills are enabled and the Skill tool is available, matching CLI behavior.
flagged.ourState: `buildClaudeSessionOptions` returns only `systemPrompt`, `settingSources` and (for a child) `maxTurns`; `skills` is never set, and `settingSources` is spelled `['user', 'project', 'local']`. So every `SKILL.md` under `~/.claude/skills/` and `<cwd>/.claude/skills/` is enabled inside a Claude-backend session, chosen by the SDK rather than by Nessy's capability resolver — the resolver's own visibility state, `enabled:false` policy and skill listing do not reach that set. Conformant with this page; the divergence is that Nessy has a second, authoritative skill-gating system that the Claude backend does not project onto the SDK.

flagged.claim: Dynamic context uses an inline `` !`<command>` `` placeholder that may appear anywhere in the body, whose output replaces the placeholder in place, with a ` ```! ` fenced block for multi-line commands.
flagged.quote: The `` !`<command>` `` syntax runs shell commands before the skill content is sent to Claude.
flagged.ourState: `runtimeSkillContextCommand` recognises a different syntax: a bare `!command` that must be the FIRST non-empty top-level body line, backticks not part of the form, fenced blocks skipped as prose, and a second `!` line throwing `runtime-skill-context-command-ambiguous`. Output is appended (`outputs.join('\n\n')`) rather than substituted at the placeholder. The docs' own example skill (`- PR diff: !`gh pr diff``, three placeholders inside list items) yields zero substitutions here; a skill whose first line IS `` !`git diff HEAD` `` passes the backticks through to the Bash permission evaluator as part of the command string.

flagged.claim: Dynamic context injection applies to skills and custom commands from user, project, plugin and additional-directory sources.
flagged.quote: To disable this behavior for skills and custom commands from user, project, plugin, or [additional-directory](#skills-from-additional-directories) sources, set `"disableSkillShellExecution": true` in [settings](/docs/en/settings).
flagged.ourState: Two divergences on one line. (1) Our executor runs only for skills with `skill.pluginRuntime` set and only when `runtime?.provider === 'pi'` — a user or project skill, and any skill on the Claude backend, never executes its command. (2) `disableSkillShellExecution` has no reader anywhere in the repo, so the managed-settings kill switch the page recommends for exactly this capability cannot be applied.

flagged.claim: A settings key overrides per-skill visibility from settings rather than frontmatter, with four states, absent meaning `on`, and `off` also hiding the skill from SDK and Remote-Control command lists.
flagged.quote: The `skillOverrides` setting controls skill visibility from your [settings](/docs/en/settings) instead of the skill's own frontmatter.
flagged.ourState: No reader. `grep -ran "skillOverrides"` over the repo hits only two planning documents (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-session-scheduling.md:193` and the r-queue verification spec). None of the four states exists, so the only way to hide a skill checked into a shared repo is to edit its SKILL.md.

flagged.claim: The skill listing has a character budget that scales with the model's context window, is raisable by a settings key or an environment variable, and caps each entry's combined `description` + `when_to_use` at 1,536 characters.
flagged.quote: To raise the budget, set the [`skillListingBudgetFraction`](/docs/en/settings#available-settings) setting (e.g. `0.02` = 2%) or the `SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET` environment variable to a fixed character count.
flagged.ourState: None of `skillListingBudgetFraction`, `SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET` or `skillListingMaxDescChars` has a reader. The 1,536 constant exists (`MAX_DERIVED_DESCRIPTION_CHARS`) but is applied only as a ceiling on a description DERIVED from the body, not to the listing entry; the listing path instead clamps each catalog entry's description at a hard 512 chars (`capability-catalog.ts:107`, `clampedText(input.description, 'description', 512, …)`) with no context-window scaling and no per-entry cap of 1,536.

flagged.claim: Four frontmatter fields govern where and how a skill runs: `context: fork`, `background` (default `true` for a fork as of v2.1.218), `hooks` scoped to the skill's lifecycle, and `shell: bash|powershell` for inline command blocks.
flagged.quote: Add `context: fork` to your frontmatter when you want a skill to run in isolation.
flagged.ourState: All four are explicitly parsed-and-dropped: `IGNORED_SKILL_FIELDS` maps `context` → 'skills do not run in a forked subagent context here', `background` → "it only applies with 'context: fork', which is not implemented", `hooks` → 'per-skill hook scopes are not implemented', `shell` → 'inline shell blocks always run under bash'. The list is deliberate and documented in-file; a skill that sets `context: fork` runs inline in the main conversation instead of in an isolated subagent, which is a behaviour inversion rather than a no-op.

flagged.claim: A skill in a nested `.claude/skills/` below the working directory loads lazily under a directory-qualified name when Claude touches a file in that subtree, and both variants stay available when names clash.
flagged.quote: The nested one appears under a directory-qualified name, `apps/web:deploy`.
flagged.ourState: Not implemented. Skill discovery walks `.claude/skills` at the working directory and its ANCESTORS (`skillRecords(join(dir, PROJECT_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR), projectScope, \`d${depth}\`, …)`), which satisfies the parent-directory half, but there is no descendant scan, no lazy load on file touch, and no directory-qualified naming — `grep -ran "directory-qualified\|qualified name"` under `packages/` returns nothing relevant. A monorepo package's own skills are unreachable unless the session starts in that package.

flagged.claim: Auto memory under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/` and claude.ai MCP connectors load regardless of `settingSources`, and each has a named opt-out that the host must set.
flagged.quote: Because the inputs above are read regardless of `settingSources`, an SDK process can pick up host-level configuration and per-directory memory.
flagged.ourState: `buildClaudeSessionOptions` sets `settingSources: ['user', 'project', 'local']` and nothing else. None of `autoMemoryEnabled`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY`, `disableClaudeAiConnectors`, `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS` or `strictMcpConfig` appears anywhere in the repo (repo-wide `grep -ran` excluding node_modules returns zero). Consequences for this fork specifically: a Claude-backend session writes memories into `~/.claude/projects/`, outside Nessy's config dir and outside its capability inventory; and when the opt-in Claude Pro/Max login is used, the user's claude.ai MCP connectors attach to the session without passing Nessy's MCP source approval, which `mcpServers: {}` explicitly does not suppress.

flagged.claim: With `settingSources` including `"project"`, hooks from the workspace's own `.claude/settings.json` execute inside the SDK session with no extra configuration.
flagged.quote: If you already have hooks in your project's `.claude/settings.json` and you set `settingSources: ["project"]`, those hooks run automatically in the SDK with no extra configuration.
flagged.ourState: We opt into `'project'` and `'local'` unconditionally, so a cloned repository's `.claude/settings.json` hooks run in a Claude-backend session. Nessy has its own project-trust gate for exactly this class of content — `native-sources.ts:995` reads project resources only when `context.projectTrustState === 'trusted'` — but that gate governs the Nessy capability runtime, not the Claude SDK subprocess, which reads the same files independently. The two trust boundaries disagree for the same directory.

flagged.claim: File checkpointing must be turned on per-session through the SDK option; when it is not, the session performing a rewind has no checkpoint data and the rewind cannot restore anything.
flagged.quote: The SDK sets the `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_SDK_FILE_CHECKPOINTING` environment variable internally only when `enable_file_checkpointing` (Python) or `enableFileCheckpointing` (TypeScript) is enabled on the session performing the rewind; the bare CLI never sets it.
flagged.ourState: `enableFileCheckpointing` occurs 0 times in `claude-agent.ts` (verified with `grep -ac`, so a NUL byte cannot be hiding it). The SDK query options object built around `claude-agent.ts:1245` passes `cwd`, `includePartialMessages`, `tools`, `permissionMode`, `allowDangerouslySkipPermissions`, `hooks` and the turn-shape options — never `enableFileCheckpointing`. Nessy's own `createFileCheckpoint` has only two non-test callers (Pi's local tool runtime and the Nestor Cloud executor); Claude's Write/Edit/NotebookEdit calls all execute inside the SDK subprocess, so nothing on the Claude path writes a checkpoint.

flagged.claim: A background subagent that stops producing output is caught by a stall watchdog, which aborts it, marks the task failed and surfaces the error to the parent with any partial result.
flagged.quote: For background subagents only, `CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS` sets a stall watchdog that fires when a `run_in_background` subagent stops producing output; it is not a total-runtime deadline.
flagged.ourState: No stall or idle watchdog exists for background subagents. `runBackground`/`runAllAndSeal` is bounded only by the abort signal; there is no output-idle timer. Repo-wide `grep -ran 'STALL|stallTimeout|watchdog'` over `packages/shared/src`, `packages/pi-agent-server/src` and `packages/server-core/src` returns no match, while the same sweep for `NESSY_*TIMEOUT*` returns `NESSY_ASK_USER_TIMEOUT_MS`, `NESSY_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT` and `NESSY_BROWSER_OPEN_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS` — so the grep is a working positive control, not a false absence.

flagged.claim: With the `project` setting source enabled, project instructions are discovered at either `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/CLAUDE.md` in the working directory.
flagged.quote: The SDK reads CLAUDE.md when the matching setting source is enabled: `'project'` loads `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/CLAUDE.md` from the working directory, and `'user'` loads `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.
flagged.ourState: The project instruction-file set is `PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES = ['AGENTS.md', 'CLAUDE.md', 'CLAUDE.local.md']`, joined against each ancestor/nested directory only. `.claude/` is read for `rules/` (`CLAUDE_RULES_DIR`) and for permission files, but never for `CLAUDE.md`: `grep -ran "CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, 'CLAUDE|'\.claude', 'CLAUDE"` over `packages` returns nothing, and the only two hits for the literal `.claude/CLAUDE.md` in `.ts` files are prose comments (capabilities/types.ts:199, base-agent.ts:972). A repo whose instructions live at `.claude/CLAUDE.md` contributes no project context.

flagged.claim: Setting the telemetry enable switch plus at least one exporter makes the agent export spans, metrics and structured log events over OTLP to a collector.
flagged.quote: Telemetry is off until you set `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1` and choose at least one exporter.
flagged.ourState: There is no telemetry emitter. `grep -ran 'startSpan|tracer|trace_id|traceparent|TRACEPARENT'` over `packages` and `apps` returns zero non-test hits, and no `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY`, `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS`, `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` or `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` reader exists. The only OTEL surface is a five-entry allowlist/classification of exporter-transport variables used by the managed-settings approval dialog, which passes them through without anything consuming them. `packages/shared/src/agent/runtime-telemetry.ts` is an in-process per-turn record, not an OTLP export. (The Claude backend inherits the process env, so an operator who exports the variables would get telemetry from the SDK's own `claude` subprocess; the Pi and Codex runtimes, which are the shipped defaults, emit nothing.)

flagged.claim: A result message with `subtype: "success"` can still be a failure: `is_error` is true and `api_error_status` carries the HTTP status when the agent loop finished but the final API call errored.
flagged.quote: On `subtype="success"` it is `True` when the final model request failed, meaning the agent loop completed but the last API call returned an error.
flagged.ourState: `adaptResult` resolves the terminal reason from `stop_reason` and `subtype` only: `msg.subtype === 'success' ? undefined : ...`. Neither `is_error` nor `api_error_status` is read anywhere on the Claude path (`grep -an 'is_error|api_error'` over `backend/claude/event-adapter.ts` matches only the assistant-message `error` field at :295 and the auth `msg.error` at :660; `claude-agent.ts` has no hit at all). A turn that ends `subtype: "success", is_error: true, api_error_status: 529` is emitted as `{ type: 'complete', usage }` with no `terminalReason` and no error event, i.e. indistinguishable from a clean success.

flagged.claim: The store's `load()` and `list_subkeys()` calls during resume materialisation are bounded by a per-call timeout, defaulting to 60 seconds.
flagged.quote: Per-call timeout for `session_store.load()` and `list_subkeys()` during resume materialization, in milliseconds
flagged.ourState: Only `append` is timed out — `appendWithEnvelope` races the call against `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000`. The load path has no timeout at all: `restoreSessionFromMirror` does a bare `await store.load(...)`, and `restoreMissingMirroredSessions` calls it in a serial loop over every session directory during the pre-listing boot sweep. A mirror root on a stalled network mount therefore hangs session listing at startup indefinitely instead of failing after a bounded wait. (The quoted sentence is the `load_timeout_ms` row on agent-sdk/python.md; session-storage.md documents the same `load` call but does not restate the bound.)

flagged.claim: The SDK's resumable transcripts live under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so relocating that variable relocates the resume corpus.
flagged.quote: Sessions are stored under `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl`, or under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl` if you set the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable, where `<encoded-cwd>` is the absolute working directory with every non-alphanumeric character replaced by `-` (so `/Users/me/proj` becomes `-Users-me-proj`).
flagged.ourState: buildClaudeSubprocessEnv sets env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to <workspaceRoot>/claude-config whenever NESSY_WORKSPACE_ID is present, with no migration of any pre-existing projects/ transcripts and no per-workspace fallback lookup. The function's own doc-comment enumerates the hazards as 'TWO HAZARDS :356 NAMES, BOTH CHECKED AND CLEAR' — credentials and settings — even though the env-vars sentence it quotes says 'All settings, session history, and plugins are stored under this path'. Session history is the third hazard and is not addressed.
flagged.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:255 (`if (workspaceConfigDir) env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR = workspaceConfigDir;`), hazard list at packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:196; no migration — `grep -ran "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR" --include="*.ts" packages apps` returns only options.ts and plugins/data-paths.ts

flagged.claim: The set of dispatchable slash commands is discovered from the system/init message's slash_commands array.
flagged.quote: Only commands that work without an interactive terminal are dispatchable through the SDK; the `system/init` message lists the ones available in your session.
flagged.ourState: The init branch of the Claude event adapter captures only `msg.tools`; `slash_commands` has no reader anywhere in the repo (`grep -ra "slash_commands" packages apps` → 0 hits). The session therefore cannot tell the user, or itself, which commands the running CLI actually offers.
flagged.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:625 (init branch reads `msg.tools` only); absence confirmed with `grep -ra "slash_commands" packages apps` (0 hits)

flagged.claim: /clear is an SDK-dispatchable command that resets conversation context, alongside /compact.
flagged.quote: The `/clear` command resets the conversation to an empty context, so subsequent prompts start with no prior conversation history.
flagged.ourState: ClaudeAgent's dispatch allowlist is `const SDK_SLASH_COMMANDS = ['compact'] as const;`. Every other slash command — /clear, /context, /usage — falls through to buildTextPrompt and is sent as an ordinary context-wrapped prompt rather than dispatched as a command.

flagged.claim: A schema-bearing run that ends success but produces no structured_output must be surfaced as a failure, not as a clean completion.
flagged.quote: A result can also end with subtype `success` but no `structured_output` value, for example when the run completes without the agent producing a structured output. Treat that case as a failure as well.
flagged.ourState: The Claude result adapter spreads `{}` when the subtype is success and `structured_output` is undefined, which is byte-identical to the schema-less turn's complete event. Downstream consumers of `structuredOutputSubtype` cannot distinguish 'no schema rode this turn' from 'a schema rode it and the agent produced nothing'.

flagged.claim: Subagents may nest three layers below the main conversation by default, and the limit is settable via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH.
flagged.quote: By default, subagents can spawn subagents of their own, up to three layers below the main conversation.
flagged.ourState: DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH is 1 in the spawner and DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG.depth is 1 in the host manifest, deliberately kept in lockstep. A depth-2 spawn is refused with `Subagent depth limit exceeded (1)`. No CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH (or NESSY_ equivalent) reader exists — the only repo occurrences of that identifier are in audit prose under docs/. This was correct when the page documented a default of 1 (v2.1.217–218); v2.1.219 raised it to 3 and made it configurable.
flagged.evidence: packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:110 (`export const DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1`) and :518-519 (refusal); packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:107 (`depth: 1`); absence via `grep -ra "SPAWN_DEPTH" --include="*.ts" .` → docs/ prose only

flagged.claim: An Agent tool call that omits run_in_background runs as a background subagent, regardless of nesting depth.
flagged.quote: An Agent tool call that omits the [`run_in_background`](/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript) input launches a background subagent, and Claude sets `run_in_background: false` when it needs the result before continuing.
flagged.ourState: The spawner's background default is `args.background ?? (depth === 1)` — top-level spawns default to background, nested spawns default to foreground. A nested Agent call that omits the input therefore blocks where Claude would detach it.

flagged.claim: AgentDefinition.effort accepts an integer as well as a named level.
flagged.quote: | `effort`           | `'low' \| 'medium' \| 'high' \| 'xhigh' \| 'max' \| number` | No       | Reasoning effort level for this agent                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
flagged.ourState: AgentDefinition.effort is typed `ThinkingLevel` and parsed by normalizeThinkingLevel, which returns undefined for anything outside the string set off|low|medium|high|xhigh|max. A numeric effort is silently dropped (the field is spread only when defined), not rejected and not honored.

flagged.claim: DirectoryAdded is a hook event, fired when /add-dir or the register_repo_root control request adds a directory.
flagged.quote: | "DirectoryAdded"
flagged.ourState: DirectoryAdded appears nowhere in the repo (`grep -ra "DirectoryAdded" . --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" --include="*.json" --include="*.md"` → 0 hits). It is absent from CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT_MAP and from DEFERRED_EXTERNAL_HOOK_EVENT_REASONS, so a Claude plugin declaring a DirectoryAdded hook is imported with a generic `plugin.format.unknown_hook_event` warning instead of a routed deferral. The map's own doc-comment still says '28 of the 30 documented Claude hook events'; the page now lists 31.

flagged.claim: The result message carries terminal_reason naming why the loop ended, across a 19-value vocabulary.
flagged.quote: * `terminal_reason`: why the loop ended. One of `"completed"`, `"max_turns"`, `"tool_deferred"`, `"aborted_streaming"`, `"aborted_tools"`, `"hook_stopped"`, `"stop_hook_prevented"`, `"background_requested"`, `"blocking_limit"`, `"rapid_refill_breaker"`, `"prompt_too_long"`, `"image_error"`, `"model_error"`, `"api_error"`, `"malformed_tool_use_exhausted"`, `"budget_exhausted"`, `"structured_output_retry_exhausted"`, `"tool_deferred_unavailable"`, or `"turn_setup_failed"`.
flagged.ourState: The Claude result adapter never reads msg.terminal_reason. It derives the reason from stop_reason==='refusal', then from subtype via a 4-entry table, with everything unrecognized collapsing to 'provider_error'. A run ending subtype:'error_during_execution' with terminal_reason:'prompt_too_long' (or hook_stopped, stop_hook_prevented, aborted_tools, blocking_limit, rapid_refill_breaker, image_error, model_error) is reported to the user as an undifferentiated provider error even though the SDK put the specific cause on the same message. The installed SDK 0.3.183 does declare the field (`terminal_reason?: TerminalReason`, 12 values).
flagged.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:581-585 and the 4-entry table at :50-57; field confirmed present in node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts

flagged.claim: system-subtype messages informational and local_command_output carry hook feedback, status lines and local slash-command output for display.
flagged.quote: Generic text banner emitted by the loop. Carries non-error status lines, hook feedback such as a `UserPromptSubmit` hook's block reason, and command output. Render `content` as plaintext at the given `level`.
flagged.ourState: adaptSystem is an if/else chain over init, compact_boundary, status and task_notification, with no trailing branch: every other system subtype is dropped without a debug line. Neither 'informational' nor 'local_command_output' appears anywhere in the repo (0 hits each). Both are declared by the installed SDK 0.3.183. A UserPromptSubmit automation that blocks under the Claude backend therefore produces a silent turn — the block reason the SDK emitted is discarded.
flagged.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:622-656; absence via `grep -ra "'informational'|'local_command_output'" packages apps` → 0 hits; both types declared in node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts

flagged.claim: A PreToolUse hook may return permissionDecision 'defer', and the run then ends carrying deferred_tool_use so the host can resume the pending call.
flagged.quote: When a `PreToolUse` hook returns `permissionDecision: "defer"`, the result has `stop_reason: "tool_deferred"` and `deferred_tool_use` carries the pending tool's `id`, `name`, and `input`.
flagged.ourState: Implemented on the Pi backend only (pi-agent.ts:3868 handles decision==='defer' and emits deferredToolUse). On the CLAUDE backend the PreToolUse translation switch handles allow/modify/block/ask and never emits permissionDecision:'defer', and the result adapter never reads msg.deferred_tool_use — `grep -ran "deferred_tool_use|deferredToolUse" packages apps` returns no hit under agent/backend/claude/ or claude-agent.ts. The SDK 0.3.183 supports both halves (`HookPermissionDecision = 'allow' | 'deny' | 'ask' | 'defer'`, `deferred_tool_use?: SDKDeferredToolUse`).
flagged.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1428-1434 (allow/modify/block/ask only); packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:581-619 (no deferred_tool_use read); Pi counterpart at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:3866-3893

flagged.claim: An approval that may outlive the process should return the defer hook decision so the run can end and resume later from the persisted session.
flagged.quote: If a user might take longer to respond than your process can reasonably stay running, return the [`defer` hook decision](/docs/en/hooks#defer-a-tool-call-for-later), which lets the process exit and resume later from the persisted session.
flagged.ourState: The defer round trip exists on the Pi backend only. Under the Claude backend the PreToolUse translation emits allow/modify/block/ask and never permissionDecision:'defer', so an approval that outlives the host process has no documented exit — the tool call stays blocked until the query is cancelled.

flagged.claim: A subagent may nest up to three layers below the main conversation by default (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` default 3, raised from 1 in v2.1.219).
flagged.quote: By default, a subagent can spawn subagents of its own, up to three layers below the main conversation.
flagged.ourState: `DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1` in the spawner and `depth: 1` in `DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG`, kept in lockstep on purpose. Depth 1 is exactly Claude's "nesting off" value. The repo's own note (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md`, R30 row: "default 1 — already matched by P9's depth-1 fix, so this one is closed") is now stale against the page.
flagged.evidence: packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:110 and packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:107; refusal path at spawner.ts:518-519 (`Subagent depth limit exceeded (1)`)

flagged.claim: A session-wide cap of 200 spawned subagents exists, raisable via `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION`, and the Agent tool fails with `Subagent spawn limit reached` when it is hit.
flagged.quote: By default, Claude can spawn at most 200 subagents per session.
flagged.ourState: No per-session subagent counter or cap exists anywhere. `orchestrator.maxAgents` (default 1000) is scoped to ONE workflow run only — `packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:49` calls it "maximum `agent()` calls per workflow run" and it is wired solely into the workflow tool (`packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1497` `getMaxAgents`). A session can spawn subagents without bound.
flagged.evidence: `grep -ran "MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION|Subagent spawn limit|sessionSpawn" packages apps/electron/src` → no output; packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1497

flagged.claim: 20 concurrently running subagents is the default ceiling, configurable via `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`, with the error `Concurrent subagent limit reached`.
flagged.quote: By default, when 20 subagents are running in a session, spawning another with the Agent tool fails with `Concurrent subagent limit reached`, and the error tells Claude not to retry.
flagged.ourState: One shared semaphore, `DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY = 16`, further narrowed at runtime to `min(concurrency, cpuCores - 2)`. It is also the workflow ceiling, where 16 IS the documented number (`workflows.md`: "Up to 16 concurrent agents"), so the two documented limits are collapsed into one and the subagent side sits 4 below spec. There is no `Concurrent subagent limit reached` error — over-limit spawns queue on the semaphore instead of failing.

flagged.claim: A subagent definition may carry a `hooks` frontmatter block whose hooks run only while that subagent is active, with frontmatter `Stop` converted to `SubagentStop` at runtime; the field is ignored for plugin subagents.
flagged.quote: Define hooks directly in the subagent's markdown file. These hooks only run while that specific subagent is active and are cleaned up when it finishes.
flagged.ourState: `hooks` is not in `UserAgentDefinition` (the frontmatter/JSON shape), not in `AgentDefinition`, and not in the runtime descriptor. A `hooks:` block in an imported Claude agent file is parsed as frontmatter and then silently dropped — no diagnostic, unlike the `TeammateIdle` deferral. `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop` from `settings.json` ARE supported (`packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-runtime.ts:171-172`); only the per-agent frontmatter channel is missing.

flagged.claim: A subagent `name` containing `:` is refused at load, because `:` is reserved for plugin-scoped identifiers.
flagged.quote: Names can't contain `:`, which is reserved for [plugin-scoped identifiers](/docs/en/plugins) such as `my-plugin:reviewer`.
flagged.ourState: `normalizeName` only trims and lowercases; no character validation. Our plugin capability keys DO contain colons (`qualifiedKey` joins with `::`, `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:263`) and become an agent's `name`/`aliases` (`runtime-agent-definitions.ts:153-154`). `resolveAgentDefinition` matches on exact `name` BEFORE searching `aliases`, so a workspace or project markdown agent file may declare a colon-bearing name equal to a plugin's capability key and be selected ahead of the alias lookup. Only the built-in and `fork` names are reserved.

flagged.claim: When `memory` is set, the subagent gets a real memory directory: prompt instructions to read/write it, up to the first 200 lines or 25KB of its `MEMORY.md` injected, and Read/Write/Edit force-enabled.
flagged.quote: The subagent's system prompt includes instructions for reading and writing to the memory directory.
flagged.ourState: `memory` is parsed, validated against `user|project|local`, and carried on the definition and the runtime descriptor — and consumed by nothing. No `agent-memory/<name>/` directory is created, no memory prompt block is composed for a child, and no tool is force-enabled. Our own code comment admits it: "Parsed, validated and carried; the per-agent memory DIRECTORY is not yet provisioned". A read-only agent definition with `memory: project` therefore cannot write the memory it is told it has.

flagged.claim: The output scan prepends a marker line when a subagent report imitates a harness tag OR mentions permission settings such as `bypassPermissions` / `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, leaving the text itself unchanged.
flagged.quote: **Marker line**: the scan prepends a line starting with `[harness: subagent output matched instruction-shaped pattern(s):` when the report imitates a tag like `<system-reminder>` or mentions permission settings such as `bypassPermissions` or `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.
flagged.ourState: `scanSubagentOutput` defangs `<untrusted|system-reminder|nessy_agent_environment` tags and line-leading `Human:`/`Assistant:` by inserting a zero-width space, and strips C0/C1 control characters. It never prepends a marker line, and it has no permission-setting pattern at all — a child report containing `bypassPermissions` or `--dangerously-skip-permissions` reaches the parent with nothing flagged. Two secondary differences on the same sentence pair: we insert U+200B where the page specifies a backslash (invisible vs visible), and we DO remove control characters where the page says "The scan never removes or rewords anything".

flagged.claim: A resumed session restores its permission mode, EXCEPT `plan` and `bypassPermissions`, which are never restored.
flagged.quote: Permission mode: the mode the session was in. `plan` and `bypassPermissions` are never restored; [bypassing permissions](/docs/en/permission-modes#skip-all-checks-with-bypasspermissions-mode) must be enabled again at launch, with one of its launch flags or `permissions.defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` in [settings](/docs/en/settings#permission-settings).
flagged.ourState: The persisted `permissionMode` is restored verbatim. `normalizePersistedSessionPermissionMode` runs only a provider-shape normalization (`normalizePiPermissionMode`) and has no exclusion list; `setPermissionMode(restoreModeKey, managed.permissionMode ?? 'default', { changedBy: 'restore' })` then installs it as-is. There is no bypass re-acceptance gate anywhere (`grep -rani "bypassAccepted|acceptedBypass|bypassDisclaimer"` → no hits), so a session last left in `bypassPermissions` comes back in `bypassPermissions` after an app restart, and a session left in `plan` comes back in `plan`.

flagged.claim: Auto memory loads the first 200 lines OR 25KB of MEMORY.md, whichever limit is reached first.
flagged.quote: The first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md, whichever comes first, load at the start of each session.
flagged.ourState: `readMemoryFile` caps at `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200` lines and nothing else — there is no byte cap anywhere (`grep -ran "25 \* 1024|25600|25000" packages/shared/src` finds only unrelated token budgets). A MEMORY.md of 200 long lines loads unbounded bytes into every session's system prompt. sub-agents.md repeats the same rule for per-agent memory ("the first 200 lines or 25KB of `MEMORY.md` in the memory directory, whichever comes first"), so the gap applies on both paths.

flagged.claim: `NO_PROXY` accepts a space-separated list as well as a comma-separated one.
flagged.quote: # Bypass proxy for specific requests - space-separated format
flagged.ourState: Both NO_PROXY parsers split on commas only. `parseNoProxyRules` calls `splitCommaSeparated` (`str.split(',')`), and the Pi interceptor does `NO_PROXY.split(',')`. `NO_PROXY="localhost 192.168.1.1 example.com .example.com"` therefore yields one rule whose host is the whole string, which matches no hostname — every request goes through the proxy with no error or warning, the opposite of what the operator configured.

flagged.claim: Subagents spawned by a workflow run in `acceptEdits` regardless of the session's permission mode; file edits are auto-approved and only the launch prompt follows the session mode.
flagged.quote: The subagents the workflow spawns always run in `acceptEdits` mode and inherit your [tool allowlist](/docs/en/settings#permission-settings), regardless of your session's mode.
flagged.ourState: No workflow-specific permission floor exists. Workflow `agent()` calls go through the same `spawnChildSession` as ordinary subagents, which forwards only `args.agentDef.permissionMode` and otherwise omits it so the host inherits the parent's mode. `grep -ran acceptEdits packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/workflow-tool.ts packages/shared/src/workflows/` returns nothing. A workflow launched from a `default`-mode session therefore prompts on every file edit its agents make — for a fan-out of dozens of agents, in a run the page describes as unattended.

flagged.claim: A saved workflow invoked without input sees `args` as `undefined`.
flagged.quote: If `args` is omitted, the global is `undefined` inside the script.
flagged.ourState: The runtime substitutes an empty object: `compiledScript(makeApi(input.args ?? {}))`. A script that branches on `args === undefined` (or on `!args`) to supply defaults never takes that branch, because `{}` is truthy and defined.

flagged.claim: A `.worktreeinclude` file at the project root, in .gitignore syntax, causes matching gitignored files to be copied into every worktree Claude creates with git.
flagged.quote: To copy them automatically when Claude creates a worktree, add a `.worktreeinclude` file to your project root.
flagged.ourState: The string `worktreeinclude` does not occur anywhere in our source (only in a planning spec, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md`, as an unbuilt item). `worktreeCreateCommands` emits only `worktree add`, optional `sparse-checkout set`, and `checkout`; `worktreeSymlinkPlan` handles only `symlinkDirectories`. No `.env`-style gitignored file is ever carried into a new worktree, so every subagent or session worktree starts without the local config the main checkout has.
flagged.evidence: packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.ts:74-96 and :112-124; `grep -rai worktreeinclude --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist .` → only the spec doc

flagged.claim: Under the default `"fresh"` base, Claude Code refreshes `origin/HEAD` before branching — fetching the default branch when the repo has not been fetched in 24 hours, capped at five seconds, falling back to the cached ref.
flagged.quote: For a `"fresh"` base, Claude Code keeps `origin/HEAD` current: when the repository hasn't been fetched in the last 24 hours, it fetches the default branch, capped at five seconds, and uses the locally cached ref if the fetch fails.
flagged.ourState: `worktreeBaseShaCandidates` for `baseRef: 'fresh'` emits exactly `git -C <root> rev-parse origin/HEAD` (allowFailure) then local `HEAD`. There is no fetch, no staleness check and no timeout anywhere on the worktree path (`grep -ran "'fetch'" packages/server-core/src` → no hit). A repository whose `origin/HEAD` was last updated weeks ago silently branches every "fresh" worktree off that stale commit — which is the pre-v2.1.208 behaviour the page calls out as changed.

flagged.claim: MEMORY.md is loaded truncated to whichever comes first of 200 lines or 25 KB.
flagged.quote: The first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation.
flagged.ourState: Only a 200-line constant exists (`MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200`); there is no byte cap anywhere in the repo. Worse, the LIVE path does not apply even the line cap: pinned memory layers are read through `materializer.readText`, which returns the whole file, and `composePinnedCapabilityContext` pushes that content verbatim. The 200-line `readMemoryFile` is only used by the legacy fallback composer and by the import-scan pass.

flagged.claim: `@path` imports are recognised anywhere in a CLAUDE.md line, not only when the line begins with `@`.
flagged.quote: To pull in a README, package.json, and a workflow guide, reference them with `@` syntax anywhere in your CLAUDE.md:
flagged.ourState: `parseMemoryImportPath` returns null unless the TRIMMED LINE ITSELF starts with `@`. Both of the page's own examples — `See @README for project overview and @package.json ...` and `- git workflow @docs/git-instructions.md` — are silently not imported. Only a whole-line `@path` (the shape our own CLAUDE.md uses) works.

flagged.claim: Import scanning must ignore `@…` occurrences inside fenced code blocks and code spans.
flagged.quote: Import parsing skips Markdown code spans and fenced code blocks.
flagged.ourState: No fence or code-span state is tracked. Both import walkers iterate raw lines and hand each to `parseMemoryImportPath`, so a line inside a ``` fence that begins with `@docs/x.md` is followed and inlined. (A backtick-wrapped `@README` at line start happens to be rejected, but only as a side effect of the leading-`@` gate.)

flagged.claim: Block-level HTML comments are removed from instruction files before their content reaches the model.
flagged.quote: Block-level HTML comments (`<!-- maintainer notes -->`) in CLAUDE.md files are stripped before the content is injected into Claude's context.
flagged.ourState: No HTML-comment stripping exists. The only `<!-- -->` handling in the repo is `stripAutoMemoryMarkers`, which removes exactly the `<!-- nessy:auto:YYYY-MM-DD -->` marker and nothing else; instruction bodies are pushed into the pinned block verbatim.

flagged.claim: A memory file that already has YAML frontmatter gets a `modified` ISO-8601 timestamp written on every agent write.
flagged.quote: When Claude writes a memory file that begins with YAML frontmatter, Claude Code records the write time in a `modified` frontmatter field as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
flagged.ourState: The `remember` handler appends a bullet plus a date marker and never parses or rewrites frontmatter; the string `modified` appears nowhere in the memory subsystem.

flagged.claim: A write that pushes MEMORY.md past its read limit still succeeds but returns an error instructing the model to rewrite the index.
flagged.quote: If the file is over a limit, the write still succeeds, but Claude Code returns an [error telling Claude to rewrite the index](/docs/en/errors#memory-index-is-over-its-read-limit), because everything past the limit is dropped on the next load.
flagged.ourState: `handleRemember` writes and returns `successResponse('Saved memory to …')` unconditionally; there is no post-write size measurement and no near-limit reminder.

flagged.claim: Auto memory enters context truncated to 200 lines or 25 KB, whichever comes first.
flagged.quote: The first 200 lines or 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded into the conversation context.
flagged.ourState: No byte cap exists, and the live capability path applies no cap at all: the MEMORY.md pinned layer is read in full via `materializer.readText` and pushed verbatim into the pinned block. Same defect as recorded on memory.md; listed here because this page restates it as a context-budget guarantee.

flagged.claim: Opus 5 is the model the `opus` alias and the `default` setting resolve to on the Anthropic API, so `claude-opus-5` must exist as a known model id.
flagged.quote: * **Max, Team Premium, Enterprise pay-as-you-go, and Anthropic API**: defaults to Opus 5
flagged.ourState: `claude-opus-5` occurs zero times in `packages`, `apps` and `scripts` (checked with `grep -ran`, NUL-safe). `MODEL_REGISTRY` tops out at `claude-opus-4-8` / `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-fable-5`; `DEFAULT_MODEL` resolves to the Opus short-name entry, i.e. Opus 4.8. The Bedrock/native alias map also has no `*.anthropic.claude-opus-5` row, and `claude-opus-4-6` is remapped forward to `claude-opus-4-8`.

flagged.claim: `fallbackModel` is an ordered array of up to three models tried in turn.
flagged.quote: To persist a chain across sessions, set `fallbackModel` in [settings](/docs/en/settings) as an array:
flagged.ourState: The stored-config schema types `fallbackModel` as a bare string (`z.string()`, default `''`, trimmed on load), and `PiAgent.getFallbackModel()` normalizes that single value. A settings file written from Claude's page (an array) fails validation rather than configuring a chain; there is no de-duplication, no three-entry cap and no `"default"` expansion.

flagged.claim: Default effort is `high` on every effort-capable model (except Opus 4.7, which defaults to `xhigh`).
flagged.quote: The default effort is `high` on every model that supports effort, except Opus 4.7, which defaults to `xhigh`.
flagged.ourState: One global constant, `DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL = 'medium'`, applies to every model, and there is no per-model default nor the documented cross-session hold on a model's first run. (Already carried in the deviation register at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:100`, but it is a changed default and is reported here as such.)

flagged.claim: Managed policy reaches devices through four sources in priority order (server-managed, plist/registry, file-based, HKCU registry), and the first non-empty one wins.
flagged.quote: Claude Code checks the four sources below in priority order and applies the first one that returns a non-empty configuration.
flagged.ourState: Only two sources exist: the server-delivered payload and the on-disk policy file. There is no macOS plist reader and no Windows registry reader (`grep -a` for `HKLM`, `SOFTWARE\\Policies`, `com.anthropic.claudecode` and plist reading finds nothing in our source; the only hits are vendored bundles under apps/electron/resources). The composition module states the two-source assumption as fact, and the winner label type has only `delivered | file | none`, so /status-style channel reporting can never say `(plist)`/`(HKLM)`/`(HKCU)`.
flagged.evidence: packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:4 ("We have exactly two, and they are the two the documentation names"), :130 (ManagedPolicyWinnerV1); packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:48

flagged.claim: A configured policyHelper executable preempts every other managed source and becomes the only managed configuration for the run.
flagged.quote: A configured [`policyHelper`](/docs/en/settings#compute-managed-settings-with-a-policy-helper) preempts all four sources: its output becomes the only managed configuration for the run.
flagged.ourState: `policyHelper` appears only inside a doc comment describing Claude's precedence chain; it is not a key in MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS and nothing executes a policy helper.

flagged.claim: strictPluginOnlyCustomization is a managed key that forces skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers to come only from plugins or managed settings.
flagged.quote: Block skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources, so they can only come from plugins or managed settings
flagged.ourState: Absent from the managed policy schema. We ship the neighbouring locks (`allowManagedHooksOnly`, `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`, `allowedMcpServers`/`deniedMcpServers`) but nothing blocks user/project-sourced skills and agents wholesale. `grep -a` over all of packages/ and apps/ hits only two vendored bundles under apps/electron/resources.

flagged.claim: minimumVersion is a managed version floor that stops auto-update from installing below an org-wide minimum, and is weaker than requiredMinimumVersion.
flagged.quote: Prevent auto-update from installing below an org-wide minimum
flagged.ourState: We implement `requiredMinimumVersion`/`requiredMaximumVersion` (refuse to start outside the range) but not `minimumVersion`. Our own gate comment names the difference and stops there, so a managed fleet with an auto-update feed has no floor on what the updater may install.

flagged.claim: processWrapper is a managed key that prefixes background agent processes with a required corporate launcher.
flagged.quote: Prefix the [background-agent supervisor](/docs/en/agent-view#how-background-sessions-are-hosted), its workers, and the [other covered background processes](/docs/en/corporate-launcher#what-the-launcher-covers) with a required corporate launcher instead of turning agent view off
flagged.ourState: No `processWrapper` key and no launcher-prefix path anywhere in source (0 hits repo-wide with `grep -a`, docs included except one spec mention). We spawn the Pi agent subprocess, the session MCP server and the headless server directly, so a corporate-launcher mandate cannot be enforced.

flagged.claim: fallbackModel is one of exactly two managed keys whose value replaces lower layers instead of merging.
flagged.quote: For [two exceptions](/docs/en/settings#settings-precedence), `fallbackModel` and `availableModels`, the managed value replaces lower layers rather than merging.
flagged.ourState: `availableModels` is a managed key; `fallbackModel` is not. Our `fallbackModel` lives only in user-editable workspace defaults and drives Pi's retry-on-error model choice, so an admin cannot pin the fallback.

flagged.claim: prefersReducedMotion is a setting that reduces or disables spinners, shimmer and other animation across the interface.
flagged.quote: The `prefersReducedMotion` [setting](/docs/en/settings#available-settings) reduces or disables spinners, shimmer, and other animations without changing the rest of the interface.
flagged.ourState: No such setting, and no global honouring of the OS signal either: the only `prefers-reduced-motion` media query in the whole source tree covers one markdown extension's task-item animation. The renderer's spinners, shimmer and transitions elsewhere are unconditional.

flagged.claim: The theme setting includes colorblind-friendly dark-daltonized and light-daltonized themes.
