flagged.ourState: Exactly one leading command is matched; everything after it, including a second `/skill-b`, becomes literal argument text. `customSlashCommandInputSubmission` returns a single `{message, customSlashCommandId}` and `resolveCustomSlashCommand` resolves one id, so `/skill-a /skill-b do XYZ` loads only `skill-a` and hands it the string "/skill-b do XYZ".

flagged.claim: A launcher path configured through an env var or a top-level settings key must wrap every process the product starts from its own binary; project/local settings must be ignored for it, and the env var must win when both are set.
flagged.quote: `CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER` starts every process Claude Code launches from its own binary through your launcher: the background service, every session it hosts in [agent view](/docs/en/agent-view), and Claude Code's relaunches after an update.
flagged.ourState: No launcher indirection exists. `grep -a` for `CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER`, `processWrapper`, or any NESSY_-prefixed equivalent across all `*.ts`/`*.tsx` in packages+apps returns zero source hits (only `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:725`). Subprocesses are spawned directly: `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/plugin-runtime-dependencies.ts:238` spawns stdio MCP servers with `spawn(invocation.command, invocation.args, invocation.options)`. `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` (34 keys) carries no launcher key.

flagged.claim: A second, distinct wrapper wraps the shell commands the agent runs on the user's behalf — Bash tool calls, hooks, and the commands that start stdio MCP servers — passing each as a single shell-quoted string in $1.
flagged.quote: [`CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX`](/docs/en/env-vars) wraps the shell commands Claude runs on your behalf, such as Bash tool calls, hooks, and the commands that start stdio MCP servers, and passes each one as a single shell-quoted string in `$1` for the wrapper to re-evaluate.
flagged.ourState: No shell-prefix mechanism. `grep -a` for `SHELL_PREFIX`/`shellPrefix` across packages+apps returns zero hits. Shell commands run unwrapped at `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:16320` (`const child = spawn(command, {`).

flagged.claim: `/context` reports context-window occupancy broken down into seven named categories, with the source each subagent loaded from.
flagged.quote: The `/context` command shows everything occupying the context window for the current session, broken down by category: system prompt, system tools, MCP tools, custom subagents with the source each loaded from, memory files, skills, and conversation messages.
flagged.ourState: No category dimension exists anywhere. `grep -a` for `contextBreakdown`/`contextCategories`/`categoryBreakdown` across all `*.ts`/`*.tsx` in the repo returns zero hits (including tests). `ContextUsageSnapshot` carries only totals — `inputTokens`, `contextWindow`, `percent`, auto-compact thresholds — and no `/context`-equivalent surface exists. Tracked open as parity row R11.

flagged.claim: A `--debug <category>` flag turns on live per-subsystem evaluation logging, naming `hooks` and `mcp` as categories.
flagged.quote: Start a session with `claude --debug hooks` and trigger the tool call.
flagged.ourState: The CLI has no `--debug` flag at all, categorised or otherwise. `apps/cli/src/index.ts` `printHelp()` lists Connection flags (`--url`, `--token`, `--workspace`, `--timeout`, `--tls-ca`, `--json`, `--safe-mode`) and LLM flags; `grep -a "'--debug'"` in `apps/cli/src/index.ts` returns nothing. We ship the hook/automation subsystem the flag exists to debug.

flagged.claim: The handler accepts exactly one path (`open`), and a deep link can only choose a directory and pre-fill the prompt box — nothing is sent or executed until the user presses Enter.
flagged.quote: A deep link never executes anything on its own. The link only chooses a directory and fills the prompt box.
flagged.ourState: `nessy://action/new-session?input=…&send=true` sends the prompt straight to the model with no user confirmation — `const shouldSend = parsed.params.send === 'true'` then `window.electronAPI.sendMessage(session.id, parsed.params.input!, …)`. The scheme is registered OS-wide via `app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient(DEEPLINK_SCHEME)` (`apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:197`), and the same handler also routes `delete-session/{id}`, `flag-session/{id}`, `rename-session` and `oauth` (`apps/electron/src/main/deep-link.ts:22-24`), so a link on any web page reaches them. There is no external-origin gate and no `Prompt from an external link` warning line.

flagged.claim: Registration of the URL-scheme handler can be prevented entirely by a settings key, and enforced fleet-wide from managed settings.
flagged.quote: To prevent registration entirely, set [`disableDeepLinkRegistration`](/docs/en/settings) to `"disable"` in `settings.json`.
flagged.ourState: Registration is unconditional at app start with no setting consulted. `grep -a` for `disableDeepLinkRegistration` across the repo returns zero hits, and `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` carries no equivalent. Given the auto-send finding above, this is the missing off-switch for it.

flagged.claim: Preview servers are configured from `.claude/launch.json` at the session folder root, with a fixed field set (`name`, `runtimeExecutable`, `runtimeArgs`, `port` defaulting to 3000, `cwd`, `env`, `autoPort`, `program`, `args`, `url`), a top-level `autoVerify` flag that is on by default, `autoPort` tri-state port-conflict handling, a `PORT` env var handed to the server, and a rule that a localhost `url` must be origin-only with a matching port.
flagged.quote: Claude automatically detects your dev server setup and stores the configuration in `.claude/launch.json` at the root of the folder you selected when starting the session.
flagged.ourState: No reader, no writer, no equivalent. `grep -rna -a "launch\.json\|autoVerify\|autoPort" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' packages apps` returns 0 lines; `runtimeExecutable` appears only in this repo's own `.claude/launch.json`, which is consumed by the Claude Code harness, not by our product. Our Browser pane ships a single `browser_tool` whose `navigate` subcommand takes a bare URL and starts nothing — there is no dev-server start/stop, no auto-verify-after-edit, and no port-conflict policy.

flagged.claim: Two managed settings keys govern the Browser pane: `browserExternalPageTools` set to `"disabled"` removes Claude's tools on external pages, and `disableBrowserExternalNavigation` set to the JSON boolean `true` blocks external navigation entirely while leaving localhost previews working.
flagged.quote: | `disableBrowserExternalNavigation`         | set to `true` to turn off external browsing in the [Browser pane](#browse-external-sites) entirely. Neither users nor Claude can navigate to external sites, and localhost dev server previews are unaffected. The value must be the JSON boolean `true`; the string `"true"` is ignored.
flagged.ourState: Neither key is read. `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` lists 34 keys and contains neither; `grep -a` for both names across all `*.ts` in the repo hits only the docs spec file. We ship the surface they govern: `browser_tool navigate` accepts any URL with no allowlist, no domain check and no managed off-switch — `grep -a "domain\|allowlist"` over `browser-tool-runtime.ts` and `browser-tools.ts` returns nothing.

flagged.claim: `managedMcpServers` pushes MCP server configurations to all users, each entry naming a transport of `"http"`, `"sse"` or `"stdio"` plus an optional per-server `toolPolicy` map, and is the documented delivery path for third-party deployments that receive no admin-console settings.
flagged.quote: | `managedMcpServers`                        | push MCP server configurations to all users in a third-party deployment. Each entry specifies a transport of `"http"`, `"sse"`, or `"stdio"`, connection details, and optionally a `toolPolicy` map that restricts which tools in that server users can invoke.
flagged.ourState: Our managed policy can only restrict — `allowedMcpServers` / `deniedMcpServers` (`managed-policy.ts:129-130`) — never push a server definition, and carries no per-server tool restriction. `grep -a managedMcpServers` across the repo hits only the docs spec. Our fork is precisely the third-party deployment shape the key exists for.

flagged.claim: Gitignored files are copied into a new worktree by declaring them in a `.worktreeinclude` file at the project root.
flagged.quote: To include gitignored files like `.env` in new worktrees, create a [`.worktreeinclude` file](/docs/en/worktrees#copy-gitignored-files-into-worktrees) in your project root.
flagged.ourState: We ship per-session worktree isolation (`WorktreeLeaseService`, namespace resolved by `resolveWorktreeNamespace`) but no include mechanism: `grep -a worktreeinclude` across the whole repo hits only `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md`. A session's worktree therefore never receives `.env` or any other gitignored file. (Our worktree root is a deliberate documented divergence — `<parent>/.nessy-worktrees/<slug>/` rather than `.claude/worktrees/` — and is not reported here.)

flagged.claim: Cross-session messaging is gated on whether a human is watching: an unattended run can neither send nor receive one.
flagged.quote: Claude can't send cross-session messages from a session nobody is watching, such as a scheduled-task run, and can't deliver messages into one.
flagged.ourState: `handleSendAgentMessage` validates only that the target id is non-empty and is not the caller's own session; there is no attended/unattended check on either the sender or the recipient. `grep -a "unattended\|isWatched\|attended"` over `packages/session-tools-core/src` returns nothing. Our `SchedulerTick` automations create exactly the unwatched sessions the rule exists for, and they carry the tool. The sender-envelope and 20-session-default halves of the same section do match (`tool-defs.ts:839`, `send-agent-message.ts:35-41`).

flagged.claim: On app start or wake, each task is checked for runs missed in the last seven days, and exactly one catch-up run fires for the most recently missed time.
flagged.quote: If it did, Desktop starts exactly one catch-up run for the most recently missed time and discards anything older.
flagged.ourState: No catch-up of any kind. `SchedulerService.start()` aligns to the next minute boundary and then fires `setInterval(… , 60_000)`; a tick that did not happen because the app was closed is simply never emitted, and `grep -ai "catch-up\|catchup\|missedRun\|lastRun"` over `packages/shared/src/automations` and `packages/shared/src/scheduler` returns zero non-test hits. A daily 9am task on a machine that was off at 9am never runs that day.

flagged.claim: A per-task toggle gives each scheduled run its own isolated Git worktree, rather than running against the working directory's current state including uncommitted changes.
flagged.quote: Enable the worktree toggle when creating the task to give each run its own isolated Git worktree, the same way [parallel sessions](/docs/en/desktop#work-in-parallel-with-sessions) work.
flagged.ourState: The automation schema carries `permissionMode` but no isolation field: `grep -a "permissionMode\|worktree\|isolat"` over `packages/shared/src/automations/schemas.ts` matches `permissionMode` only. `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove` exist as observable hook events (`automations/types.ts:74-75`) but nothing lets a scheduled automation request a worktree, so every scheduled run mutates the live checkout, uncommitted changes included.

flagged.claim: Environment variables can be set from a settings file under an `env` key at user, project, local and managed scope; values there are re-applied to a running session when the file changes and override the inherited shell value.
flagged.quote: Add variables under the `env` key in a `settings.json` file, creating the file if it doesn't exist.
flagged.ourState: An `env` block exists only on the MANAGED policy tier (`readonly env?: Readonly<Record<string,string>>`, applied by `applyManagedEnv`). There is no user-scope settings `env` block: the only other `env` record in the config schema is the per-MCP-stdio-server `env`. At project scope `env` is a deliberately FORBIDDEN section (project-config.ts:138), which is a recorded security decision — the user-scope gap is not.

flagged.claim: The subagent nesting-depth default is 3 as of v2.1.219 — a subagent can spawn its own subagents by default, and 1 is the value that turns nesting off.
flagged.quote: Number of [subagent layers](/docs/en/sub-agents#let-subagents-spawn-their-own-subagents) allowed below the main conversation {/* min-version: 2.1.219 */}(default: 3).
flagged.ourState: Default depth is 1 in both places that carry it, i.e. Claude's "nesting off" value is our default, so a subagent cannot spawn a subagent unless the host explicitly raises `orchestrator.depth`. There is also no `NESSY_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` env override. The repo's own parity note (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:559) records this row as CLOSED against the old default of 1.

flagged.claim: Subagent output over the cap is truncated, but the full output is written to disk and the truncated response carries the path; the cap is tunable via TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH (default 32000, maximum 160000).
flagged.quote: When truncated, the full output is saved to disk and the path is included in the truncated response
flagged.ourState: Truncation is a hard byte cut at 32 KiB with the overflow discarded — the trailing marker is a bare `[Output truncated to 32KB for the parent context.]` with no file path — and there is no env override (no `NESSY_TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH`; 0 hits for TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH repo-wide).

flagged.claim: A write that leaves the auto-memory index MEMORY.md over 200 lines or 25KB returns an error to the model naming the overflow, because everything past the limit is silently dropped on every subsequent load.
flagged.quote: Claude wrote to the [auto memory](/docs/en/memory#auto-memory) index `MEMORY.md` and left it over one of its read limits: 200 lines or 25KB.
flagged.ourState: We have the read limit (`MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200`) and we DO silently truncate at load (`readFileSync(...).split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)`), but the write path (`appendMemory`) performs no post-write size check and returns no error or reminder — exactly the pre-v2.1.210 behaviour the page describes as the defect. There is also no 25KB byte limit and no frontmatter/HTML-comment exclusion.

flagged.claim: When every entry in a subagent's `tools` frontmatter list fails to match a usable tool, the spawn is refused with a diagnostic grouping the entries by cause, rather than launching a toolless subagent.
flagged.quote: Every entry in the subagent's [`tools` list](/docs/en/sub-agents#supported-frontmatter-fields) failed to match a usable tool, so Claude Code refused to launch the subagent: with no tools, it couldn't act.
flagged.ourState: `allowedTools()` filters the declared list against `disallowedTools` only and hands the result straight to the child restrictions. Unrecognised names, names not available to subagents, and names matching nothing in the session are all passed through unvalidated, and an empty result is not detected — the child launches with no usable tools and no error.

flagged.claim: A `pkill` whose pattern matches the agent's own process is refused before it runs; the pattern is probed with `pgrep` and the refusal is returned in the Bash tool result.
flagged.quote: Claude Code tests the pattern with `pgrep` before running `pkill` and refuses when its own process ID is in the result.
flagged.ourState: `pkill` is only classified as a dangerous command that requires a permission decision — there is no self-PID probe. `pgrep` appears nowhere in the tool/permission path (only in build scripts and a shellguard corpus fixture), so in a mode that does not prompt, a matching pattern can terminate the agent process mid-turn.
flagged.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/core/pre-tool-use.ts:1751; packages/shared/src/agent/core/permission-manager.ts:46; grep -ra --include="*.ts" -ln "pgrep" . → no hit under packages/*/src runtime paths

flagged.claim: Fast mode applies to Opus 5 and Opus 4.8; Opus 4.7 is no longer served at fast speed and the API rejects fast-mode requests for it.
flagged.quote: Fast mode is supported on Opus 5 and Opus 4.8. It is not available on Sonnet, Haiku, or other models.
flagged.ourState: `shouldEnableFastMode` matches the single literal `claude-opus-4-7` and nothing else, so it targets only the removed model and never fires for Opus 4.8 (which IS in our catalogue, models-pi.ts:92) or Opus 5. When FEATURE_FLAGS.fastMode is turned on, every request it modifies sets `body.speed='fast'` plus the `fast-mode-2026-02-01` beta header on a model the API now rejects, while the two supported models get no speedup at all.

flagged.claim: When a skill of the same name exists at more than one level, the USER-scope definition wins over the project-scope one (managed > user > project).
flagged.quote: **Skills and subagents** override by name: when the same name exists at multiple levels, one definition wins based on priority (managed > user > project for skills; managed > CLI flag > project > user > plugin for subagents).
flagged.ourState: Skill collisions are resolved by `scopeSpecificity`, which ranks project(3) > workspace(2) > global(1) > builtin(0) for every non-MCP capability kind including skills — the inverse of the documented skill order for the user-vs-project pair. A repo checking in `.nessy-agent/skills/deploy` silently shadows the user's own `deploy` skill; on Claude it would not. The surrounding comment cites mcp.md for the MCP arm only, so the skill arm appears unexamined.

flagged.claim: A settings key `skillOverrides` hides or narrows a skill you did not write, without editing the skill file.
flagged.quote: For a skill you didn't write, set [`skillOverrides`](/docs/en/skills#override-skill-visibility-from-settings) in settings to do the same without editing its file.
flagged.ourState: No reader anywhere in the source tree — the identifier appears only in two planning documents under docs/superpowers/. `disable-model-invocation` frontmatter IS supported (packages/shared/src/capabilities/types.ts), so the file-authored half of the mechanism exists and only the settings-side override is missing.

flagged.claim: The MEMORY.md index load is capped by BOTH a line count and a byte size; we cap only lines, so a 200-line file with long lines loads unbounded into every session's context.
flagged.quote: The first 200 lines or 25 KB of the `MEMORY.md` index loads at the start of every session.
flagged.ourState: `readMemoryFile` slices to `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200` lines and applies no byte limit; no 25 KB (or any) size constant exists in the memory subsystem.
flagged.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:8 (`MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200`), :29-32 (`readMemoryFile` — `split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)`, no byte check); `grep -ran "25_000\|25600\|25 \* 1024" packages/shared/src/agent/memory` returns nothing

flagged.claim: Trusting your home directory must be session-scoped and re-prompt on every launch; in our fork a home-directory grant persists to disk like any other project.
flagged.quote: Acceptance is saved per project directory, except your home directory, where trust is held for the current session only and the prompt reappears on each launch.
flagged.ourState: `ProjectTrustStore.record`/`resolve` persist any grant whose identity `persistence` is `'stable'`; `persistence` is decided purely by whether the platform can stat the root, with no home-directory carve-out anywhere in `projects/` or `capabilities/`.

flagged.claim: `/goal` is a user-facing command with set / no-arg status / clear semantics and five clear aliases; we expose the goal only as a model-invocable session tool, so a user cannot set, inspect or clear a goal.
flagged.quote: `stop`, `off`, `reset`, `none`, and `cancel` are accepted as aliases for `clear`.

flagged.claim: A `yes` from the evaluator must clear the goal; ours records an advisory `complete_suggested` and leaves the goal active until the model separately calls `Goal complete` with evidence, so a satisfied condition can keep spending turns.
flagged.quote: **Yes**: Claude Code clears the goal and records an achieved entry in the transcript.
flagged.ourState: `evaluateAtSettlement` commits `lastEvaluation` with verdict `complete_suggested` and keeps `status: 'active'`; only an explicit `{ action: 'complete', evidence }` command reaches `terminalGoal`. The evaluator prompt itself states "Advisory goal check only."

flagged.claim: A SIGTERM'd non-interactive run must exit 143; ours exits 130 for both SIGINT and SIGTERM, so a supervisor cannot tell an operator interrupt from a shutdown signal.
flagged.quote: If you stop a `claude -p` run with SIGTERM, for example from `kill`, a process supervisor, or an SDK host closing the session, Claude Code aborts the in-progress turn, terminates the process tree of any running Bash command, runs [`SessionEnd` hooks](/docs/en/hooks#sessionend), and exits with code 143.

flagged.claim: No `--bare` flag exists, and the page states bare mode is slated to become the default for `-p`; `--safe-mode` is a different documented flag with different semantics (it does not skip OAuth/keychain reads and does not restrict the tool set).

flagged.claim: A `PreCompact` hook can stop a compaction, either by exiting 2 or by returning a top-level `decision: "block"`.
flagged.quote: PreCompact hooks can block compaction by exiting with code 2 or returning {"{"}"decision":"block"{"}"}
flagged.ourState: PreCompact cannot block anything, and the two halves of our own contract disagree. `hook-decision-contract.ts` lists PreCompact in `TOP_LEVEL_BLOCK_EVENTS`, so its parsed output is allowed to carry `block`/`deny` + `reason` — but the frozen event table declares it `kind: 'observational'`, and its single emission site awaits `options.emit('PreCompact', …)` whose signature returns `Promise<void> | void`, so any decision the parser produced is discarded before compaction proceeds. A hook author writing the documented blocker sees it accepted and parsed, and the context is compacted anyway.
flagged.evidence: packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:83 (`kind: 'observational'`) vs packages/shared/src/automations/hook-decision-contract.ts:49 (PreCompact in TOP_LEVEL_BLOCK_EVENTS); emission at packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:151 with the void-returning `emit` declared at :28

flagged.claim: Hooks receive the session's active effort level, both as an `effort.level` field in the hook JSON input and as a `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` environment variable; Bash tool commands can read the same variable.
flagged.quote: Hooks now receive the active effort level via the `effort.level` JSON input field and the `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` environment variable, and Bash tool commands can read $CLAUDE_EFFORT
flagged.ourState: `SdkAutomationInput` — the exact object serialised to hook stdin by `hookCommandStdinPayload` — has no `effort` member of any spelling, and the hook env builder emits only NESSY_EVENT/NESSY_EVENT_DATA/NESSY_SESSION_ID/NESSY_SESSION_NAME/NESSY_WORKSPACE_ID plus payload fields. `CLAUDE_EFFORT`/`NESSY_EFFORT` exist ONLY as skill-body substitution placeholders (runtime-skill-content.ts:136), never as a real env var, so neither a hook nor a Bash command can read one.

flagged.claim: Bash, hook, MCP and LSP subprocesses no longer inherit OTEL_* environment variables from the host process.
flagged.quote: Subprocesses such as Bash, hooks, MCP, and LSP no longer inherit OTEL_* environment variables, so OTEL-instrumented apps run via the Bash tool no longer pick up the CLI's own OTLP endpoint
flagged.ourState: Every subprocess inherits the host env wholesale. MCP stdio filters only a fixed 12-entry credential blocklist that contains no OTEL_ key; the Pi subprocess (which hosts the Bash tool) spawns with `...process.env`; the hook runner env is built from the full `process.env`. `grep -ran -a "OTEL_" packages apps` finds no scrubbing site at all — only settings/telemetry readers.

flagged.claim: The Agent tool's `subagent_type` resolves case-insensitively AND separator-insensitively, so "Code Reviewer" reaches the agent named code-reviewer.
flagged.quote: Agent tool subagent_type now matches case- and separator-insensitively, so "Code Reviewer" resolves to code-reviewer
flagged.ourState: `resolveAgentDefinition` normalises with `normalizeName` = `name.trim().toLowerCase()` only. No separator folding: spaces and underscores are not collapsed to hyphens, so "Code Reviewer" normalises to "code reviewer", misses both the name match and the author-declared alias list, and throws `Unknown agent "Code Reviewer"`. This is the same class as the Task→Agent rename that broke every turn.

flagged.claim: MCP stdio servers receive CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR in their spawn environment, the same as hooks, and configs may reference ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} inside commands.
flagged.quote: MCP stdio servers now receive CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR in their environment, matching hooks, and plugin configs can reference ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} in commands
flagged.ourState: Only half. Plugin-supplied MCP servers get the project dir via `claudeCompatPluginEnv` (`NESSY_PROJECT_DIR` + `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`). Native and project `.mcp.json` stdio servers take the non-plugin branch, whose env is `{...processEnv, ...getProxyEnvVars(), ...config.env}` — no project-dir variable is injected, so `${NESSY_PROJECT_DIR}`/`${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` in a project `.mcp.json` command expands from `process.env` and resolves to nothing.

flagged.claim: Fast mode's default model moved to Opus 4.8; Opus 4.7 and 4.6 keep the old price and Opus 4.6 fast mode is deprecated.
flagged.quote: Fast mode now defaults to Opus 4.8 at $10/$50 per MTok: 2x the standard rate for about 2.5x the speed. Opus 4.7 and 4.6 stay at $30/$150. Opus 4.6 fast mode is deprecated.
flagged.ourState: `shouldEnableFastMode` returns true for exactly one literal — `model === 'claude-opus-4-7'`. A session on `claude-opus-4-8` (which IS in our model table and IS the current default upstream) never gets the fast-mode beta header, so the fast toggle is silently inert on the model fast mode now defaults to. Stale pin, not a policy decision — the comment still reads "Only activates for Opus 4.7".

flagged.claim: A SessionStart hook can return `reloadSkills: true` to make skills it installed available in the same session, and `/reload-skills` re-scans skill directories without a restart.
flagged.quote: New /reload-skills command re-scans skill directories without restarting, and SessionStart hooks can return reloadSkills: true to make skills they install available in the same session
flagged.ourState: `reloadSkills` has zero occurrences in any .ts/.tsx in the repo (grep -ran -a, node_modules excluded) — the only hit anywhere is a docs file listing it as an open R9 item. The hook output parser reads `additionalContext`, `updatedInput`, `updatedToolOutput`, `worktreePath`, `retry`, elicitation `action`/`content` and the universal five, and ignores anything else, so a SessionStart hook that installs a skill cannot surface it this session.

flagged.claim: A `MessageDisplay` hook event fires per assistant message and lets a hook transform or hide the displayed text.
flagged.quote: New MessageDisplay hook event lets hooks transform or hide assistant message text as it is displayed
flagged.ourState: Not emitted. `PluginHookEventName` carries 28 of the documented events plus two of our own and deliberately excludes `MessageDisplay`; a plugin declaring it imports as a recorded deferral (`plugin.deferred.event_message_display_unsupported`) rather than registering a hook that can never fire. Reason on record: no per-message display interception channel exists.

flagged.claim: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES values are attached as labels on emitted metric datapoints.
flagged.quote: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES values are now attached as labels on metric datapoints, so you can slice usage metrics by custom dimensions like team or repo
flagged.ourState: We ship OTLP usage metrics, but `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` is read nowhere in the repo (grep -ran -a across packages/ and apps/ → 0 hits). The metrics module reads only the exporter selectors, endpoints, headers, timeout, protocol and export interval, so no custom resource dimension reaches a datapoint.

flagged.claim: `fallbackModel` holds an ordered list of up to three models, each tried in turn when the primary is overloaded or unavailable.
flagged.quote: fallbackModel configures up to three fallback models tried in order when the primary is overloaded or unavailable, and --fallback-model now applies to interactive sessions too
flagged.ourState: `fallbackModel` is a single string in both the schema (`z.string()`) and the default (`''`), and the runtime does exactly one hop: `getRetryFallbackModel` returns that one id, `setModel`s to it, and retries once with `fallbackModelRetry: true` — a second failure has nowhere to go. There is no `fallbackModels` array anywhere in the repo.

flagged.claim: A `sandbox.allowAppleEvents` opt-in setting lets sandboxed commands send Apple Events on macOS.
flagged.quote: New sandbox.allowAppleEvents opt-in setting lets sandboxed commands send Apple Events on macOS
flagged.ourState: No occurrence of `allowAppleEvents` (or `AppleEvent` at all) anywhere in the repo. `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS` is a closed seven-entry list — excludedCommands, deniedReadRoots, deniedWriteRoots, additionalWritableRoots, allowUnsandboxedCommands, network, filesystem — and unknown keys are rejected/stripped, so an admin or user who writes the documented key gets a validation drop rather than the opt-in. We do ship the macOS sandbox this governs.

flagged.claim: Output from a `!`-prefixed command now gets a model response by default; `respondToBashCommands: false` in settings.json restores the old context-only behavior.
flagged.quote: To keep the earlier behavior, where the output is added to context without a response, set respondToBashCommands to false in settings.json.
flagged.ourState: We ship `!` shell mode in the composer, and it is stuck on the pre-change behavior: `runShellCommand` spawns the command, records the result and returns — it never queues a turn — and `respondToBashCommands` has zero occurrences in the repo, so there is neither the new default nor the escape hatch.

flagged.claim: A `sandbox.credentials` setting blocks sandboxed commands from reading credential files and secret environment variables, with `files` and `envVars` sub-keys.
flagged.quote: New sandbox.credentials setting blocks sandboxed commands from reading credential files and secret environment variables
flagged.ourState: `credentials` is not a member of `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS`, so the key is stripped as unknown. The name appears in this repo only as a shape ANALOGY in two comments ("an individual invalid entry in `files` or `envVars` is stripped… a wholly invalid `credentials` value is dropped") borrowed to describe tolerant parsing of `sandbox.network` and of the permission DSL — the setting itself has no reader and no enforcement.

flagged.claim: A response stream that emits no events for 5 minutes must be aborted and retried; the watchdog is on by default for every provider and is disabled by an env var.
flagged.quote: The streaming idle watchdog is now on by default for all providers: it aborts and retries when a response stream produces no events for 5 minutes (CLAUDE\_ENABLE\_STREAM\_WATCHDOG=0 to disable)
flagged.ourState: No streaming idle watchdog exists on any provider path. There is no abort-and-retry on stream silence and no on/off knob for one. The only 'watchdog' in the agent layer is the stdio-death watchdog for the Pi subprocess (pi-agent.ts:6053), which fires on process death, not on a silent stream; the compact RPC has an unrelated 300s timeout.
flagged.evidence: grep -ra -F over packages/ apps/ (node_modules excluded) for STREAM_WATCHDOG / streamWatchdog / idleWatchdog returns 0 hits; nearest neighbour is packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6053

flagged.claim: A transient server rate-limit error that is not the account usage limit must be retried automatically with backoff rather than ending the turn.
flagged.quote: Transient server rate-limit errors unrelated to your usage limit are now retried automatically with backoff for subscribers instead of failing the turn
flagged.ourState: Both backends classify a rate limit and surface it to the user instead of retrying. claude-agent.ts carries the explicit comment 'Rate limit errors - don't retry immediately, surface to user' and then yields typed_error + complete; pi-agent.ts returns a `rate_limited` diagnostic with a manual 'Retry' action and retryDelayMs 5000. No backoff loop, and no distinction between a transient server 429 and the account usage limit. (Backoff retry does exist elsewhere — MCP connect, webhooks, session mirror — so the absence is specific to the model turn.)

flagged.claim: `/doctor` is a fix-capable setup checkup (installation health, unused skills/MCP/plugins against context cost, CLAUDE.md dedup and trim, slow hooks) that proposes changes and asks for confirmation, and it answers to `/checkup` as well.
flagged.quote: /doctor now diagnoses issues and can fix them, instead of printing a read-only report. It checks installation health, finds unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost, deduplicates local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones, proposes trimming CLAUDE.md content Claude could derive from the codebase, and flags slow hooks. It reports findings first and asks for confirmation before changing anything. /checkup is its alias.
flagged.ourState: `doctor` is a CLI subcommand only (`nessy-general-agent doctor`), explicitly read-only — it renders a settings/managed-policy/agent-definition report and an exit code, with no fix flow and no confirmation step. There is no `checkup` alias (the word appears only in prose), no in-session `/doctor` slash command in the composer's command set, and none of the unused-extension, CLAUDE.md-dedup/trim or slow-hook checks. The narrowed scope is a recorded decision in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-doctor-surface.md (status: closed), which predates this tier change.
flagged.evidence: apps/cli/src/doctor.ts:2 ('the read-only configuration checkup'), apps/cli/src/index.ts:2149, packages/shared/src/config/config-doctor.ts:21-32; grep -ra -F checkup finds no command registration

flagged.claim: Auto mode must block writes that tamper with session transcript files.
flagged.quote: Auto mode now blocks tampering with session transcript files, and asks before running rm -rf on a variable it can't resolve from context
flagged.ourState: No rule anywhere names session transcript files as a protected target. Transcripts live at <configDir>/sessions/<ws>/<id>/session.jsonl, and the sandbox deny list deliberately excludes that directory because it doubles as the supervised process's scratch/TMPDIR root — so a Bash write there is unguarded. The file-tool protected-path floor does fire on the `.nessy-agent` segment, but in auto mode its outcome is 'routed to the classifier', and the guardian prompt carries no transcript-tampering instruction.
flagged.evidence: packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation/self-config-deny.ts:31-34 ('The whole config dir. SESSIONS_DIR … is <configDir>/sessions' — listed under 'NOT here, deliberately'); packages/shared/src/prompts/guardian.ts (no transcript rule; lines 128-130 mention the transcript only as untrusted evidence)

flagged.claim: An `rm -rf` whose target is a variable the model cannot resolve from context must prompt.
flagged.quote: Auto mode now blocks tampering with session transcript files, and asks before running rm -rf on a variable it can't resolve from context
flagged.ourState: The removal circuit breaker deliberately does the opposite: an unresolvable removal target does not fire. The module states 'rm -rf "$(cat targets.txt)" has an unresolvable target and does not fire', and its 'Known limits' section confirms `${HOME:?}`, `$(echo ~)` and `rm -rf *` are not detected — every limit 'fail[s] toward NOT prompting'. The guardian prompt's rm -rf guidance (lines 150, 177) is about inspecting a specific local path, not about an unresolved variable.

flagged.claim: Subagent spawns are capped per session at a default of 200, tunable by env var.
flagged.quote: Session-wide caps stop runaway loops: WebSearch calls and subagent spawns each default to 200, tunable with CLAUDE\_CODE\_MAX\_WEB\_SEARCHES\_PER\_SESSION and CLAUDE\_CODE\_MAX\_SUBAGENTS\_PER\_SESSION
flagged.ourState: The spawner enforces only a DEPTH limit (DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1, error 'Subagent depth limit exceeded'). There is no per-session spawn COUNT budget and no concurrency limit — a depth-1 loop can spawn unboundedly. Neither MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION nor MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS has a reader.
flagged.evidence: packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:110 and :518-519; grep -ra -F for MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION / MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS over packages/ apps/ → 0 source hits

flagged.claim: WebSearch calls are capped per session at a default of 200, tunable by env var.
flagged.quote: Session-wide caps stop runaway loops: WebSearch calls and subagent spawns each default to 200, tunable with CLAUDE\_CODE\_MAX\_WEB\_SEARCHES\_PER\_SESSION and CLAUDE\_CODE\_MAX\_SUBAGENTS\_PER\_SESSION
flagged.ourState: We do ship a `web_search` tool (DDG-backed with a fallback provider), and it has no per-session call budget of any kind. The cap and its env var have no reader.
flagged.evidence: packages/pi-agent-server/src/tools/search/create-search-tool.ts:61; grep -ra -F MAX_WEB_SEARCHES over packages/ apps/ → 0 hits

flagged.claim: Administrators disable auto mode with a `disableAutoMode` setting.
flagged.quote: Auto mode no longer needs the CLAUDE\_CODE\_ENABLE\_AUTO\_MODE opt-in on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry; administrators can turn it off with disableAutoMode
flagged.ourState: The managed-policy reader has no `disableAutoMode` key. Auto mode can only be removed by omitting it from `cyclablePermissionModes` or by the disabled-permission-mode list — there is no key of that name an administrator can set. The five `disableAutoMode` hits in the repo are all inside vendored/built bundles (pi-agent-server/dist, electron resources), not our source.
flagged.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:405-420 (policy interface) and :662 (disabledPermissionModeList); grep -ra -F -l disableAutoMode lists only dist/resource bundles

flagged.claim: A `processWrapper` setting / `CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER` env var forces every process the binary spawns (background service, agent-view sessions) through a required wrapper executable.
flagged.quote: New corporate launcher support: CLAUDE\_CODE\_PROCESS\_WRAPPER or the processWrapper setting runs the processes Claude Code starts from its own binary, such as the background service and agent view sessions, through a required wrapper executable
flagged.ourState: No reader for either name. Our own process spawns — the Pi subprocess supervisor, the session MCP server, background agent sessions — launch their executables directly with no wrapper indirection and no setting to require one. This is the exact surface a corporate deployment (which is what this fork is) would need.
flagged.evidence: grep -ra -F for PROCESS_WRAPPER / processWrapper over packages/ apps/ (node_modules excluded) → 0 hits; spawn sites in packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts take the binary path unwrapped

flagged.claim: Screen-reader mode is reachable three ways: a CLI flag, a `CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER` env var, and an `axScreenReader` setting.
flagged.quote: Turn it on per session with a flag, per shell with the CLAUDE\_AX\_SCREEN\_READER environment variable, or everywhere with the axScreenReader setting.
flagged.ourState: None of the three exists. Our CLI does render in-place spinner frames on a TTY (the exact 'spinners and in-place redraws' the mode is meant to replace) and exposes only `--no-spinner`/`--disable-spinner`, which suppresses the animation but does not switch to labelled linear output. No `axScreenReader` settings key, no env var, no flag.
flagged.evidence: apps/cli/src/index.ts:266-275 (spinner) and :116-118 (--no-spinner); grep -ra -F for axScreenReader / AX_SCREEN_READER → 0 hits

flagged.claim: A flag and env var include subagent text and thinking blocks in stream-json output.
flagged.quote: `--forward-subagent-text` and CLAUDE\_CODE\_FORWARD\_SUBAGENT\_TEXT include subagent text and thinking blocks in stream-json output
flagged.ourState: We ship stream-json output (`--output-format stream-json` in the CLI) but no way to include subagent text or thinking blocks in it. Neither the flag nor the env var has a reader.
flagged.evidence: apps/cli/src/index.ts (streamJson output format); grep -ra -F for forward-subagent-text / FORWARD_SUBAGENT_TEXT over packages/ apps/ → 0 hits

flagged.claim: `claude auto-mode reset` restores the default auto-mode configuration, with `--yes` to skip confirmation.
flagged.quote: New claude auto-mode reset restores the default auto-mode configuration, and `--yes` skips the confirmation prompt
flagged.ourState: No `auto-mode` CLI subcommand and no reset path for auto-mode configuration. The CLI's subcommand set does not include it.
flagged.evidence: grep -ra -F 'auto-mode reset' over packages/ apps/ → 0 hits; apps/cli/src/index.ts command dispatch has no auto-mode branch

flagged.claim: `fallbackModel` holds an ordered list of up to three models tried in sequence.
flagged.quote: **`--safe-mode`** starts Claude Code with all customizations disabled for troubleshooting; and **`fallbackModel`** configures up to three fallback models tried in order.
flagged.ourState: `fallbackModel` is a single string in both the schema and the defaults, documented as 'Pi model ID to retry once after model/network drain errors. Empty disables fallback.' — one model, one retry, no ordered list. The Zod schema is `fallbackModel: z.string()` and the normalizer coerces anything non-string to ''.

flagged.claim: A configured MCP server can be authenticated and de-authenticated from the shell, outside the interactive menu.
flagged.quote: **`claude mcp login`**: authenticate a configured MCP server from your shell instead of the interactive `/mcp` menu, and clear its stored credentials later with `claude mcp logout`.
flagged.ourState: The CLI has no `mcp` subcommand at all, so neither `login` nor `logout` exists. MCP OAuth is reachable only through the app's interactive surfaces; there is no shell path to authenticate a server or to clear its stored credentials.
flagged.evidence: apps/cli/src/index.ts command dispatch (doctor / plugin validate|list|details / run / help / version — no mcp branch); grep -ra -F 'mcp login' over packages/ apps/ → 0 hits

flagged.claim: Plugins load for the current session from a local `.zip` archive via `--plugin-dir` and from a remote archive via `--plugin-url`.
flagged.quote: **Plugins load from `.zip` archives and URLs**: `--plugin-dir` now accepts `.zip` files, and `--plugin-url` fetches a plugin archive for the current session.
flagged.ourState: Neither flag has a reader in our source. Plugin installation goes through the marketplace/install service (which does handle .zip and .mcpb archives internally), but there is no session-scoped side-load of a plugin from a local archive path or a URL. The only `plugin-dir` hits in the tree are inside vendored bundles and the Codex binaries.
flagged.evidence: grep -ra -F -l 'plugin-dir' over packages/ apps/ → only dist/vendor bundles; grep -ra -F 'plugin-url'/'pluginUrl' → 0 hits; apps/cli/src/index.ts exposes only `plugin validate|list|details`
